import sys
import threading

# special case python < 3.8
if sys.version_info.major == 3 and sys.version_info.minor < 8:
    import mock
else:
    from unittest import mock

import pytest

from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber import client
from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber import scheduler
from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber._protocol import leaser
from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber._protocol import streaming_pull_manager
from google.pubsub_v1 import types as gapic_types


def _make_manager():
    client_ = mock.create_autospec(client.Client, instance=True)
    scheduler_ = mock.create_autospec(scheduler.Scheduler, instance=True)
    manager = streaming_pull_manager.StreamingPullManager(
        client_,
        "subscription-name",
        scheduler=scheduler_,
        await_callbacks_on_shutdown=True,
    )

    leaser_ = mock.create_autospec(leaser.Leaser, instance=True)
    leaser_.message_count = 0
    leaser_.bytes = 0

    manager._leaser = leaser_
    manager._dispatcher = mock.Mock()
    manager._consumer = mock.Mock()
    manager._consumer.is_active = True
    manager._consumer.is_paused = False
    manager._heartbeater = mock.Mock()
    manager._callback = mock.Mock()

    # Keep the test focused on response leasing/scheduling rather than RPCs used
    # to update lease deadlines.
    manager._obtain_ack_deadline = mock.Mock(return_value=10)
    manager._send_lease_modacks = mock.Mock(return_value=set())

    return manager, scheduler_, leaser_


def _make_response(with_message=True):
    received_messages = []
    if with_message:
        received_messages.append(
            gapic_types.ReceivedMessage(
                ack_id="ack-id",
                message=gapic_types.PubsubMessage(
                    data=b"test message", message_id="message-id"
                ),
            )
        )

    return gapic_types.StreamingPullResponse(
        received_messages=received_messages,
        subscription_properties=gapic_types.StreamingPullResponse.SubscriptionProperties(
            exactly_once_delivery_enabled=False
        ),
    )


def _mark_shutting_down(manager, cleared):
    """Represent the manager state visible while/after close() shuts it down."""
    manager._closed = True
    manager._consumer.is_active = False

    if cleared in ("scheduler", "both"):
        manager._scheduler = None
    if cleared in ("leaser", "both"):
        manager._leaser = None


def _assert_no_response_side_effects(manager, scheduler_, leaser_):
    leaser_.add.assert_not_called()
    leaser_.start_lease_expiry_timer.assert_not_called()
    scheduler_.queue.put.assert_not_called()
    scheduler_.schedule.assert_not_called()
    manager._callback.assert_not_called()
    if manager._consumer is not None:
        manager._consumer.pause.assert_not_called()
    assert manager._messages_on_hold.size == 0


def test_on_response_still_leases_and_schedules_messages_during_normal_operation():
    """The shutdown guard must not disable ordinary response processing."""
    manager, scheduler_, leaser_ = _make_manager()

    manager._on_response(_make_response())

    leaser_.add.assert_called_once()
    lease_requests = list(leaser_.add.call_args[0][0])
    assert [request.ack_id for request in lease_requests] == ["ack-id"]
    leaser_.start_lease_expiry_timer.assert_called_once_with(["ack-id"])

    scheduler_.schedule.assert_called_once()
    scheduled_callback = scheduler_.schedule.call_args[0][0]
    scheduled_args = scheduler_.schedule.call_args[0][1:]
    scheduled_kwargs = scheduler_.schedule.call_args[1]

    # The response must result in real callback work, not merely a no-op that
    # happens to avoid the shutdown assertion.
    scheduled_callback(*scheduled_args, **scheduled_kwargs)
    manager._callback.assert_called_once()
    delivered_message = manager._callback.call_args[0][0]
    assert delivered_message.ack_id == "ack-id"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("cleared", ["scheduler", "leaser", "both"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_message", [False, True])
def test_on_response_is_a_noop_once_shutdown_has_cleared_helpers(
    cleared, with_message
):
    """Late responses must not assert or use helpers cleared by shutdown."""
    manager, scheduler_, leaser_ = _make_manager()
    _mark_shutting_down(manager, cleared)

    # In particular, this must not raise AssertionError or AttributeError.
    manager._on_response(_make_response(with_message=with_message))

    _assert_no_response_side_effects(manager, scheduler_, leaser_)


def test_response_arriving_after_close_is_ignored():
    """Exercise the actual close() shutdown followed by a late RPC response."""
    manager, scheduler_, leaser_ = _make_manager()

    manager.close()
    shutdown_thread = manager._regular_shutdown_thread
    if shutdown_thread is not None:
        shutdown_thread.join(timeout=5)
        assert not shutdown_thread.is_alive(), "manager shutdown did not finish"

    assert manager._closed
    assert manager._scheduler is None
    assert manager._leaser is None

    # This is the response that previously reached
    # ``assert self._scheduler is not None`` after future.cancel() closed the
    # manager.
    manager._on_response(_make_response())

    _assert_no_response_side_effects(manager, scheduler_, leaser_)


def test_in_flight_response_observes_shutdown_before_leasing_or_scheduling():
    """Deterministically race an in-flight response with shutdown.

    The response is held just before its pause/resume critical section. Shutdown
    then clears the helpers, reproducing the window in which the old assertions
    failed. A check performed only before this critical section is insufficient.
    """
    manager, scheduler_, leaser_ = _make_manager()

    raw_lock = threading.Lock()
    response_at_critical_section = threading.Event()

    class SignallingLock:
        def __enter__(self):
            response_at_critical_section.set()
            raw_lock.acquire()

        def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_value, traceback):
            raw_lock.release()

    manager._pause_resume_lock = SignallingLock()
    raw_lock.acquire()

    errors = []

    def process_response():
        try:
            manager._on_response(_make_response())
        except BaseException as exc:  # Capture AssertionError from the worker.
            errors.append(exc)

    response_thread = threading.Thread(target=process_response)
    response_thread.start()

    try:
        reached_critical_section = response_at_critical_section.wait(timeout=5)
        if reached_critical_section:
            _mark_shutting_down(manager, "both")
    finally:
        raw_lock.release()

    response_thread.join(timeout=5)

    assert reached_critical_section, "response did not reach the test barrier"
    assert not response_thread.is_alive(), "response processing deadlocked"
    assert not errors, f"late response raised an exception: {errors!r}"
    _assert_no_response_side_effects(manager, scheduler_, leaser_)

import pytest

from xsdata.codegen.mappers import DefinitionsMapper
from xsdata.codegen.models import Class
from xsdata.formats.dataclass.models.generics import AnyElement
from xsdata.models.enums import Tag
from xsdata.models.wsdl import (
    BindingMessage,
    BindingOperation,
    Definitions,
    Message,
    Part,
    PortTypeMessage,
    PortTypeOperation,
)
from xsdata.utils.namespaces import build_qname


def _get_body(envelope: Class) -> Class:
    return next(inner for inner in envelope.inner if inner.name == "Body")


def _get_fault_attr(body: Class):
    attrs = [attr for attr in body.attrs if attr.name == "Fault"]
    assert len(attrs) == 1
    return attrs[0]


def _assert_fault_is_optional(body: Class):
    fault_attr = _get_fault_attr(body)

    # A successful SOAP response has no Fault element. In particular, the
    # generated field must receive a default even when kw_only is enabled.
    assert fault_attr.is_optional
    assert fault_attr.restrictions.min_occurs == 0


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "declare_fault", [False, True], ids=["no-declared-fault", "declared-fault"]
)
def test_envelope_fault_is_optional(declare_fault):
    """The Body fault is optional with and without operation fault messages."""
    target = Class(
        qname=build_qname("urn:test", "Operation_output"),
        tag=Tag.BINDING_MESSAGE,
        location="test.wsdl",
    )
    body = DefinitionsMapper.build_inner_class(target, "Body")

    # Making the fault optional must not make the actual response payload
    # optional as a side effect.
    payload = DefinitionsMapper.build_attr(
        "result", build_qname("urn:test", "Result")
    )
    body.attrs.append(payload)

    definitions = Definitions(target_namespace="urn:test")
    operation = PortTypeOperation()

    if declare_fault:
        detail_part = Part(name="detail", element="tns:FaultDetail")
        detail_part.ns_map["tns"] = "urn:test"
        definitions.messages.append(
            Message(name="FaultMessage", parts=[detail_part])
        )
        operation.faults.append(PortTypeMessage(message="tns:FaultMessage"))

    DefinitionsMapper.build_envelope_fault(definitions, operation, target)

    _assert_fault_is_optional(body)
    assert not payload.is_optional
    assert payload.restrictions.min_occurs is None


def test_only_output_envelope_receives_an_optional_fault():
    """Exercise fault creation through binding-operation message mapping."""
    definitions = Definitions(
        target_namespace="urn:test",
        messages=[Message(name="Request"), Message(name="Response")],
    )
    port_operation = PortTypeOperation(
        input=PortTypeMessage(message="tns:Request"),
        output=PortTypeMessage(message="tns:Response"),
    )
    binding_operation = BindingOperation(
        name="Operation",
        input=BindingMessage(
            location="test.wsdl",
            extended=[AnyElement(qname="Body")],
        ),
        output=BindingMessage(
            location="test.wsdl",
            extended=[AnyElement(qname="Body")],
        ),
    )

    envelopes = list(
        DefinitionsMapper.map_binding_operation_messages(
            definitions,
            binding_operation,
            port_operation,
            "Service_Operation",
            "document",
            "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/",
        )
    )

    assert len(envelopes) == 2
    input_body = _get_body(envelopes[0])
    output_body = _get_body(envelopes[1])

    assert not any(attr.name == "Fault" for attr in input_body.attrs)
    _assert_fault_is_optional(output_body)

    statement = parse_one(sql, read=dialect)
    statement.assert_is(exp.Alter)

    drop = statement.find(exp.Drop)
    assert drop is not None, "ALTER TABLE should contain a structured Drop action"

    return statement, drop


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql, expected_sql, exists",
    [
        (
            "ALTER TABLE ride DROP COLUMN activity_id",
            "ALTER TABLE ride DROP COLUMN activity_id",
            False,
        ),
        (
            # MySQL permits omitting the COLUMN keyword.
            "ALTER TABLE ride DROP activity_id",
            "ALTER TABLE ride DROP COLUMN activity_id",
            False,
        ),
        (
            "ALTER TABLE ride DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS activity_id",
            "ALTER TABLE ride DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS activity_id",
            True,
        ),
        (
            "ALTER TABLE `ride` DROP COLUMN `activity_id`",
            "ALTER TABLE `ride` DROP COLUMN `activity_id`",
            False,
        ),
    ],
    ids=["explicit-column", "implicit-column", "if-exists", "quoted-identifiers"],
)
def test_drop_column_name_is_not_a_table(sql, expected_sql, exists):
    statement, drop = _parse_alter_drop(sql, "mysql")

    assert [table.name for table in statement.find_all(exp.Table)] == ["ride"]
    assert drop.args["kind"] == "COLUMN"
    assert drop.this.name == "activity_id"
    assert not isinstance(drop.this, exp.Table)
    assert bool(drop.args.get("exists")) is exists
    assert statement.sql(dialect="mysql") == expected_sql


def test_drop_column_preserves_qualified_table_name():
    statement, drop = _parse_alter_drop(
        "ALTER TABLE analytics.ride DROP COLUMN activity_id", "mysql"
    )

    tables = list(statement.find_all(exp.Table))
    assert len(tables) == 1
    assert tables[0].name == "ride"
    assert tables[0].db == "analytics"
    assert drop.this.name == "activity_id"
    assert statement.sql(dialect="mysql") == (
        "ALTER TABLE analytics.ride DROP COLUMN activity_id"
    )


def test_multiple_drop_column_actions_do_not_introduce_phantom_tables():
    sql = "ALTER TABLE ride DROP COLUMN activity_id, DROP COLUMN legacy_id"
    statement = parse_one(sql, read="mysql")
    statement.assert_is(exp.Alter)

    assert [table.name for table in statement.find_all(exp.Table)] == ["ride"]

    drops = list(statement.find_all(exp.Drop))
    assert len(drops) == 2
    assert [drop.args["kind"] for drop in drops] == ["COLUMN", "COLUMN"]
    assert [drop.this.name for drop in drops] == ["activity_id", "legacy_id"]
    assert statement.sql(dialect="mysql") == sql


def test_drop_constraint_name_is_not_a_table():
    sql = "ALTER TABLE customers DROP CONSTRAINT fk_order"
    statement, drop = _parse_alter_drop(sql, "mysql")

    assert [table.name for table in statement.find_all(exp.Table)] == ["customers"]
    assert drop.args["kind"] == "CONSTRAINT"
    assert drop.this.name == "fk_order"
    assert not isinstance(drop.this, exp.Table)
    assert statement.sql(dialect="mysql") == sql


def test_drop_column_preserves_if_exists_and_cascade():
    # CASCADE is part of PostgreSQL's DROP COLUMN syntax. Fixing the column
    # identifier must not leave CASCADE unconsumed and degrade the statement
    # to an unparsed Command.
    sql = "ALTER TABLE ride DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS activity_id CASCADE"
    statement, drop = _parse_alter_drop(sql, "postgres")

    assert [table.name for table in statement.find_all(exp.Table)] == ["ride"]
    assert drop.args["kind"] == "COLUMN"
    assert drop.this.name == "activity_id"
    assert drop.args.get("exists") is True
    assert drop.args.get("cascade") is True
    assert statement.sql(dialect="postgres") == sql


def test_alter_table_drop_index_is_not_reclassified_as_drop_column():
    # _parse_drop_column also sits on the parsing path for other ALTER TABLE
    # DROP actions; fixing column identifiers must not change their meaning or
    # make an otherwise supported statement fall back to Command.
    sql = "ALTER TABLE ride DROP INDEX idx_activity"
    statement, drop = _parse_alter_drop(sql, "mysql")

    assert drop.args["kind"] == "INDEX"
    assert drop.this.name == "idx_activity"
    assert statement.sql(dialect="mysql") == sql

from jwst.stpipe.core import JwstPipeline, JwstStep

class _Pipeline(JwstPipeline):
    def process(self, data):

    yield model

    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(crds_client, "get_svn_version", lambda: "test-svn-version")


def assert_version_follows_crds_context(records):
    """The final CRDS report must be followed by the actual jwst version."""
    messages = [record.getMessage() for record in records]

    assert len(messages) >= 2
    assert messages[-2] == f"Results used CRDS context: {CRDS_CONTEXT}"

    version_record = records[-1]
    version_message = messages[-1]
    assert version_record.levelno == logging.INFO
    assert "jwst" in version_message.lower()
    assert "version" in version_message.lower()
    assert __version__ in version_message

    """A top-level step using reference files reports its software version."""
    step = _Step()

    with capture_log() as records:
        step.finalize_result(image_model, [("flat", "flat.fits")])

    assert_version_follows_crds_context(records)


def test_pipeline_reports_version_after_crds_context_without_references(image_model):

        pipeline.finalize_result(image_model, [])

    assert_version_follows_crds_context(records)

    )

import dns.exception
import dns.message
import dns.name
import dns.rdataclass
import dns.rdatatype
import dns.rrset
import dns.xfr
import dns.zone
import pytest


_BASE_ZONE = """
@ 3600 IN SOA ns.example. hostmaster.example. 1 3600 1800 604800 3600
@ 3600 IN NS ns.example.
www 3600 IN A 192.0.2.1
stale 3600 IN A 192.0.2.99
"""

_SOA_1 = (
    "example.",
    3600,
    "IN",
    "SOA",
    "ns.example. hostmaster.example. 1 3600 1800 604800 3600",
)
_SOA_2 = (
    "example.",
    3600,
    "IN",
    "SOA",
    "ns.example. hostmaster.example. 2 3600 1800 604800 3600",
)
_WWW_OLD = ("www.example.", 3600, "IN", "A", "192.0.2.1")
_WWW_NEW = ("www.example.", 3600, "IN", "A", "192.0.2.2")
_MAIL = ("mail.example.", 3600, "IN", "A", "192.0.2.25")


def _make_zone():
    return dns.zone.from_text(_BASE_ZONE, origin="example.")


def _wire_response(query, zone, records):
    """Build and parse a response as the inbound XFR query code does."""
    response = dns.message.make_response(query)
    for record in records:
        response.answer.append(dns.rrset.from_text(*record))
    return dns.message.from_wire(
        response.to_wire(),
        xfr=True,
        origin=zone.from_wire_origin(),
        one_rr_per_rrset=True,
    )


def _assert_fallback_zone_contents(zone):
    soa = zone.get_rdataset(dns.name.empty, dns.rdatatype.SOA)
    assert soa is not None
    assert soa[0].serial == 2

    www = zone.get_rdataset(
        dns.name.from_text("www.example."), dns.rdatatype.A
    )
    assert www is not None
    assert [rdata.address for rdata in www] == ["192.0.2.2"]

    mail = zone.get_rdataset(
        dns.name.from_text("mail.example."), dns.rdatatype.A
    )
    assert mail is not None
    assert [rdata.address for rdata in mail] == ["192.0.2.25"]

    # An AXFR-style answer replaces the zone rather than incrementally
    # updating it, so data omitted from the answer must not survive.
    assert (
        zone.get_rdataset(
            dns.name.from_text("stale.example."), dns.rdatatype.A
        )
        is None
    )


def test_ixfr_query_contains_serial_after_wire_roundtrip():
    zone = _make_zone()
    query, serial = dns.xfr.make_query(zone, serial=1)

    assert serial == 1
    assert query.question[0].rdtype == dns.rdatatype.IXFR
    assert dns.xfr.extract_serial_from_query(query) == 1

    parsed = dns.message.from_wire(query.to_wire())
    authority_soa = parsed.find_rrset(
        parsed.authority,
        dns.name.from_text("example."),
        dns.rdataclass.IN,
        dns.rdatatype.SOA,
    )
    assert authority_soa[0].serial == 1


def test_multimessage_ixfr_with_question_on_each_message():
    zone = _make_zone()
    query, serial = dns.xfr.make_query(zone, serial=1)
    inbound = dns.xfr.Inbound(zone, dns.rdatatype.IXFR, serial)

    first = _wire_response(query, zone, [_SOA_2, _SOA_1, _WWW_OLD])
    second = _wire_response(query, zone, [_SOA_2, _WWW_NEW, _SOA_2])

    with inbound:
        assert inbound.process_message(first) is False
        assert inbound.process_message(second) is True

    soa = zone.get_rdataset(dns.name.empty, dns.rdatatype.SOA)
    assert soa is not None
    assert soa[0].serial == 2
    www = zone.get_rdataset(
        dns.name.from_text("www.example."), dns.rdatatype.A
    )
    assert www is not None
    assert [rdata.address for rdata in www] == ["192.0.2.2"]


def test_single_message_axfr_style_answer_to_ixfr():
    zone = _make_zone()
    query, serial = dns.xfr.make_query(zone, serial=1)
    inbound = dns.xfr.Inbound(zone, dns.rdatatype.IXFR, serial)
    response = _wire_response(query, zone, [_SOA_2, _WWW_NEW, _MAIL, _SOA_2])

    with inbound:
        assert inbound.process_message(response) is True

    _assert_fallback_zone_contents(zone)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "answer_chunks",
    [
        # Fallback occurs in the first message.  The next message still has
        # the original IXFR question, as required for an IXFR response.
        ((_SOA_2, _WWW_NEW), (_MAIL, _SOA_2)),
        # Fallback occurs after one or more continuation messages.
        ((_SOA_2,), (_WWW_NEW,), (_MAIL, _SOA_2)),
        # The final message can consist solely of the terminating SOA.
        ((_SOA_2, _WWW_NEW, _MAIL), (_SOA_2,)),
    ],
    ids=[
        "fallback-in-first-message",
        "fallback-in-later-message",
        "final-soa-in-separate-message",
    ],
)
def test_multimessage_axfr_style_answer_to_ixfr_keeps_ixfr_question(
    answer_chunks,
):
    """AXFR fallback must not change the type expected in the question.

    RFC 1995 permits a server to answer an IXFR request with an AXFR-style
    answer.  The question section still describes the original IXFR request,
    including on later TCP messages; it does not change into an AXFR question.
    """
    zone = _make_zone()
    query, serial = dns.xfr.make_query(zone, serial=1)
    inbound = dns.xfr.Inbound(zone, dns.rdatatype.IXFR, serial)

    with inbound:
        for index, records in enumerate(answer_chunks):
            message = _wire_response(query, zone, records)
            assert message.question[0].rdtype == dns.rdatatype.IXFR
            is_last = index == len(answer_chunks) - 1
            assert inbound.process_message(message) is is_last

    _assert_fallback_zone_contents(zone)


def test_invalid_initial_question_type_is_still_rejected():
    zone = _make_zone()
    query, serial = dns.xfr.make_query(zone, serial=1)
    inbound = dns.xfr.Inbound(zone, dns.rdatatype.IXFR, serial)
    response = _wire_response(query, zone, [_SOA_2])
    response.question[0].rdtype = dns.rdatatype.AXFR

    with inbound:
        with pytest.raises(dns.exception.FormError, match="wrong question rdatatype"):
            inbound.process_message(response)

import pytest

from yarl import URL


class _CustomPort:
    pass


class _IntPortSubclass(int):
    pass


@pytest.mark.parametrize("encoded", [False, True])
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("port", "type_name"),
    [
        pytest.param(8080.0, "float", id="float"),
        pytest.param("8080", "str", id="string"),
        pytest.param("", "str", id="empty-string"),
        pytest.param(True, "bool", id="true"),
        pytest.param(False, "bool", id="false"),
        pytest.param([8080], "list", id="list"),
        pytest.param({"port": 8080}, "dict", id="dict"),
        pytest.param(_CustomPort(), "_CustomPort", id="custom-class"),
    ],
)
def test_build_invalid_port_error_identifies_actual_type(
    port, type_name, encoded
):
    with pytest.raises(TypeError) as exc_info:
        URL.build(
            scheme="http",
            host="example.com",
            port=port,
            encoded=encoded,
        )

    message = str(exc_info.value)
    # Accept both the concise form requested in the issue and Python's
    # fully qualified type representation.
    assert message in {
        f"The port is required to be int, got {type_name}.",
        f"The port is required to be int, got {type(port)}.",
    }
    assert type_name in message


def test_build_invalid_port_type_is_checked_before_missing_host():
    with pytest.raises(TypeError) as exc_info:
        URL.build(port=8080.0)

    message = str(exc_info.value)
    assert message.startswith("The port is required to be int, got ")
    assert "float" in message


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("port", "expected"),
    [
        pytest.param(None, "http://example.com", id="none"),
        pytest.param(0, "http://example.com:0", id="zero"),
        pytest.param(80, "http://example.com", id="default-port"),
        pytest.param(8080, "http://example.com:8080", id="non-default-port"),
        pytest.param(65535, "http://example.com:65535", id="maximum-port"),
    ],
)
def test_build_still_accepts_valid_integer_ports_and_none(port, expected):
    url = URL.build(scheme="http", host="example.com", port=port)

    assert str(url) == expected


def test_build_accepts_integer_subclasses():
    url = URL.build(
        scheme="http",
        host="example.com",
        port=_IntPortSubclass(8080),
    )

    assert str(url) == "http://example.com:8080"
    assert url.explicit_port == 8080

"""Tests for ``raise_when_missing`` on the public client ``get()`` methods.

The schema and filters methods are mocked so these tests exercise client behavior
without requiring a running Infrahub server or making network requests.
"""

from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock

import pytest

from infrahub_sdk import Config, InfrahubClient, InfrahubClientSync
from infrahub_sdk.exceptions import NodeNotFoundError
from infrahub_sdk.schema import NodeSchema

KIND = "BuiltinLocation"
BRANCH = "branch01"


@pytest.fixture
def location_schema() -> NodeSchema:
    return NodeSchema(
        name="Location",
        namespace="Builtin",
        default_filter="name__value",
        human_friendly_id=["name__value"],
        attributes=[{"name": "name", "kind": "String", "unique": True}],
    )


@pytest.fixture
def async_client() -> InfrahubClient:
    return InfrahubClient(config=Config(address="http://mock"))


@pytest.fixture
def sync_client() -> InfrahubClientSync:
    return InfrahubClientSync(config=Config(address="http://mock"))


def mock_async_lookup(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    client: InfrahubClient,
    schema: NodeSchema,
    results: list[object],
) -> AsyncMock:
    monkeypatch.setattr(client.schema, "get", AsyncMock(return_value=schema))
    filters = AsyncMock(return_value=results)
    monkeypatch.setattr(client, "filters", filters)
    return filters


def mock_sync_lookup(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    client: InfrahubClientSync,
    schema: NodeSchema,
    results: list[object],
) -> MagicMock:
    monkeypatch.setattr(client.schema, "get", MagicMock(return_value=schema))
    filters = MagicMock(return_value=results)
    monkeypatch.setattr(client, "filters", filters)
    return filters


def expected_filters_call(filters: dict[str, object]) -> dict[str, object]:
    return {
        "kind": KIND,
        "at": None,
        "branch": BRANCH,
        "populate_store": False,
        "include": None,
        "exclude": None,
        "fragment": False,
        "prefetch_relationships": False,
        **filters,
    }


LOOKUPS = [
    ({"id": "missing"}, {"name__value": "missing"}),
    ({"hfid": ["missing"]}, {"hfid": ["missing"]}),
    ({"name__value": "missing"}, {"name__value": "missing"}),
]


@pytest.mark.asyncio
class TestAsyncGetRaiseWhenMissing:
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("options", [{}, {"raise_when_missing": True}])
    async def test_missing_node_raises_by_default_and_when_explicitly_requested(
        self,
        monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
        async_client: InfrahubClient,
        location_schema: NodeSchema,
        options: dict[str, bool],
    ):
        filters = mock_async_lookup(monkeypatch, async_client, location_schema, [])

        with pytest.raises(NodeNotFoundError):
            await async_client.get(kind=KIND, branch=BRANCH, id="missing", **options)

        filters.assert_awaited_once()

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(("lookup", "expected_filters"), LOOKUPS)
    async def test_missing_node_returns_none_when_raise_is_disabled(
        self,
        monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
        async_client: InfrahubClient,
        location_schema: NodeSchema,
        lookup: dict[str, object],
        expected_filters: dict[str, object],
    ):
        filters = mock_async_lookup(monkeypatch, async_client, location_schema, [])

        result = await async_client.get(
            kind=KIND,
            branch=BRANCH,
            raise_when_missing=False,
            **lookup,
        )

        assert result is None
        # In particular, raise_when_missing must be consumed by get(), not sent
        # to Infrahub as a node filter.
        filters.assert_awaited_once_with(**expected_filters_call(expected_filters))

    async def test_existing_node_is_returned_when_raise_is_disabled(
        self,
        monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
        async_client: InfrahubClient,
        location_schema: NodeSchema,
    ):
        node = object()
        mock_async_lookup(monkeypatch, async_client, location_schema, [node])

        result = await async_client.get(
            kind=KIND,
            branch=BRANCH,
            id="present",
            raise_when_missing=False,
        )

        assert result is node

    async def test_multiple_results_still_raise_when_raise_is_disabled(
        self,
        monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
        async_client: InfrahubClient,
        location_schema: NodeSchema,
    ):
        mock_async_lookup(monkeypatch, async_client, location_schema, [object(), object()])

        with pytest.raises(IndexError, match="More than 1 node returned"):
            await async_client.get(
                kind=KIND,
                branch=BRANCH,
                name__value="duplicate",
                raise_when_missing=False,
            )

    async def test_missing_filters_still_raise_validation_error(
        self,
        monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
        async_client: InfrahubClient,
        location_schema: NodeSchema,
    ):
        filters = mock_async_lookup(monkeypatch, async_client, location_schema, [])

        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="At least one filter must be provided"):
            await async_client.get(kind=KIND, branch=BRANCH, raise_when_missing=False)

        filters.assert_not_awaited()

    async def test_query_errors_are_not_converted_to_none(
        self,
        monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
        async_client: InfrahubClient,
        location_schema: NodeSchema,
    ):
        filters = mock_async_lookup(monkeypatch, async_client, location_schema, [])
        error = RuntimeError("query failed")
        filters.side_effect = error

        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError) as exc_info:
            await async_client.get(
                kind=KIND,
                branch=BRANCH,
                id="missing",
                raise_when_missing=False,
            )

        assert exc_info.value is error

import numpy as np
import pytest
from astropy import units as u
from astropy.modeling import fitting, models

from specutils import Spectrum1D
from specutils.fitting import fit_lines


LINE_CENTER = 6563 * u.AA


class _RecordingFitter:
    """Fitter that exposes the samples actually passed by ``fit_lines``."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.dispersion = None
        self.flux = None

    def __call__(self, model, x, y, weights=None, **kwargs):
        self.dispersion = x
        self.flux = y
        return model


def _make_spectrum():
    # The step deliberately does not land exactly on either window boundary.
    wavelength = np.arange(6500.0, 6620.0, 0.11) * u.AA
    x = wavelength.to_value(u.AA)

    target_line = 2000 * np.exp(-0.5 * ((x - 6563.0) / 2.0) ** 2)
    # A strong feature outside the requested window makes fitting the whole
    # spectrum observably different from fitting only the target line.
    contaminating_line = 5000 * np.exp(-0.5 * ((x - 6590.0) / 3.0) ** 2)
    flux = 25 + target_line + contaminating_line

    return Spectrum1D(spectral_axis=wavelength, flux=flux * u.Jy)


def _make_model(compound):
    model = models.Gaussian1D(
        amplitude=2000,
        mean=LINE_CENTER,
        stddev=3 * u.AA,
    )
    if compound:
        model = model + models.Const1D(0)
    return model


def _quantity_values(value, unit):
    """Handle both unit-aware and internally unit-stripped fitter inputs."""
    if hasattr(value, "unit"):
        return value.to_value(unit)
    return np.asarray(value)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "compound", [False, True], ids=["gaussian", "gaussian-plus-constant"]
)
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "window", [10 * u.AA, 1 * u.nm], ids=["angstrom", "equivalent-unit"]
)
def test_scalar_quantity_window_selects_only_centered_samples(compound, window):
    """The fitter must receive only samples inside the centered window."""
    spectrum = _make_spectrum()
    fitter = _RecordingFitter()

    fit_lines(spectrum, _make_model(compound), fitter=fitter, window=window)

    dispersion = spectrum.spectral_axis.to_value(u.AA)
    half_width = window.to_value(u.AA)
    center = LINE_CENTER.to_value(u.AA)
    selected = (dispersion >= center - half_width) & (
        dispersion < center + half_width
    )

    expected_dispersion = dispersion[selected]
    expected_flux = spectrum.flux.to_value(u.Jy)[selected]
    assert 0 < expected_dispersion.size < dispersion.size

    np.testing.assert_array_equal(
        _quantity_values(fitter.dispersion, u.AA), expected_dispersion
    )
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(
        _quantity_values(fitter.flux, u.Jy), expected_flux
    )

    "compound", [False, True], ids=["gaussian", "gaussian-plus-constant"]
)
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "window", [10 * u.AA, 1 * u.nm], ids=["angstrom", "equivalent-unit"]
)
def test_scalar_quantity_window_matches_explicit_centered_bounds(compound, window):
    """A scalar Quantity window must be applied around the initial line center."""
    spectrum = _make_spectrum()

    automatic = fit_lines(
        spectrum,
        _make_model(compound),
        fitter=fitting.LevMarLSQFitter(calc_uncertainties=False),
        window=window,
    )
    explicit = fit_lines(
        spectrum,
        _make_model(compound),
        fitter=fitting.LevMarLSQFitter(calc_uncertainties=False),
        window=(LINE_CENTER - window, LINE_CENTER + window),
    )

    parameter_names = (
        ("amplitude_0", "mean_0", "stddev_0", "amplitude_1")
        if compound
        else ("amplitude", "mean", "stddev")
    )

    # Both calls should fit exactly the same samples from the same initial
    # conditions, so all fitted parameters should agree numerically.
    for name in parameter_names:
        automatic_value = getattr(automatic, name).value
        explicit_value = getattr(explicit, name).value
        np.testing.assert_allclose(
            automatic_value,
            explicit_value,
            rtol=1e-6,
            atol=1e-8,
            err_msg=f"Scalar and explicit windows produced different {name} values",
        )

    mean_name = "mean_0" if compound else "mean"
    assert getattr(automatic, mean_name).value == pytest.approx(6563.0, abs=0.05)

    """An applied window containing no pixels must not silently fit everything."""
    spectrum = _make_spectrum()

    # LINE_CENTER lies between spectral pixels, so this narrow positive window
    # contains no samples.
    with pytest.raises(Exception, match="Spectrum flux is empty or None"):
        fit_lines(
            spectrum,
            _make_model(compound=True),
            fitter=fitting.LevMarLSQFitter(calc_uncertainties=False),
            window=1e-6 * u.AA,
        )

"""Regression tests for optional SOAP Body fault elements."""

from xsdata.codegen.mappers import DefinitionsMapper
from xsdata.formats.dataclass.models.generics import AnyElement
from xsdata.models.wsdl import (
    BindingMessage,
    BindingOperation,
    Definitions,
    Message,
    Part,
    PortTypeMessage,
    PortTypeOperation,
)
from xsdata.utils.testing import ClassFactory


SOAP_ENVELOPE_NS = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"


def get_body(envelope):
    return next(inner for inner in envelope.inner if inner.name == "Body")


def get_fault_attr(body):
    return next(attr for attr in body.attrs if attr.name == "Fault")


def test_output_envelope_fault_is_optional_without_declared_faults():
    """A successful output message must not require a SOAP Fault element."""
    definitions = Definitions(target_namespace="urn:calculator")
    definitions.messages.extend(
        [
            Message(name="AddRequest"),
            Message(name="AddResponse"),
        ]
    )

    binding_operation = BindingOperation(name="Add")
    binding_operation.input = BindingMessage(
        location="calculator.wsdl",
        extended=[AnyElement(qname="Body")],
    )
    binding_operation.output = BindingMessage(
        location="calculator.wsdl",
        extended=[AnyElement(qname="Body")],
    )

    port_operation = PortTypeOperation()
    port_operation.input = PortTypeMessage(
        message="tns:AddRequest", location="calculator.wsdl"
    )
    port_operation.output = PortTypeMessage(
        message="tns:AddResponse", location="calculator.wsdl"
    )

    envelopes = list(
        DefinitionsMapper.map_binding_operation_messages(
            definitions,
            binding_operation,
            port_operation,
            "CalculatorSoap_Add",
            "document",
            SOAP_ENVELOPE_NS,
        )
    )

    assert len(envelopes) == 2
    input_body = get_body(envelopes[0])
    output_body = get_body(envelopes[1])

    # Faults belong to output envelopes only.
    assert not any(attr.name == "Fault" for attr in input_body.attrs)

    fault_attr = get_fault_attr(output_body)
    assert fault_attr.restrictions.min_occurs == 0
    assert fault_attr.is_optional


def test_output_envelope_fault_is_optional_with_fault_detail_messages():
    """Declared fault details must not make the Body fault itself mandatory."""
    fault_part = Part(element="tns:FaultDetail")
    fault_part.ns_map["tns"] = "urn:calculator"

    definitions = Definitions(target_namespace="urn:calculator")
    definitions.messages.append(
        Message(name="AddFaultMessage", parts=[fault_part])
    )

    port_operation = PortTypeOperation()
    port_operation.faults.append(
        PortTypeMessage(message="tns:AddFaultMessage")
    )

    envelope = ClassFactory.create()
    body = ClassFactory.create(qname="Body")
    envelope.inner.append(body)

    # Making Fault optional must not change the occurrence constraints of the
    # actual response payload stored alongside it in the Body.
    payload_attr = DefinitionsMapper.build_attr(
        "add_response", "{urn:calculator}AddResponse"
    )
    body.attrs.append(payload_attr)

    DefinitionsMapper.build_envelope_fault(
        definitions, port_operation, envelope
    )

    fault_attr = get_fault_attr(body)
    assert fault_attr.restrictions.min_occurs == 0
    assert fault_attr.is_optional

    assert payload_attr.restrictions.min_occurs is None
    assert not payload_attr.is_optional

    # Exercise the declared-fault path far enough to ensure its detail class is
    # still generated; optionality must not come at the expense of fault data.
    fault_class = next(
        inner for inner in body.inner if inner.name == "Fault"
    )
    detail_class = next(
        inner for inner in fault_class.inner if inner.name == "detail"
    )
    assert [attr.name for attr in detail_class.attrs] == ["FaultDetail"]

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def test_duckdb_struct_pack_unpack_columns_issue_example():
    sql = r"""SELECT id, struct_pack(*COLUMNS('m\d')) AS measurements
FROM many_measurements"""

    tree = parse_one(sql, read="duckdb")

    # The complete projection, including its alias, must be preserved.
    projection = tree.expressions[1]
    assert isinstance(projection, exp.Alias)
    assert projection.alias == "measurements"

    struct_pack = tree.find(exp.Struct)
    assert struct_pack is not None
    assert len(struct_pack.expressions) == 1

    unpacked = struct_pack.expressions[0]
    assert isinstance(unpacked, exp.Unpack)

    columns = unpacked.this
    assert isinstance(columns, exp.Anonymous)
    assert columns.name.upper() == "COLUMNS"
    assert columns.expressions[0].this == r"m\d"

    # Generation must retain the unpacking operator and produce parseable SQL.
    generated = tree.sql("duckdb")
    assert r"*COLUMNS('m\d')" in generated
    assert parse_one(generated, read="duckdb") == tree


def test_duckdb_unpack_columns_in_generic_function_arguments():
    tree = parse_one(
        r"SELECT pack(*COLUMNS('m\d'), 5) FROM measurements",
        read="duckdb",
    )

    function = tree.find(exp.Anonymous)
    assert function is not None
    assert function.name.lower() == "pack"
    assert len(function.expressions) == 2
    assert isinstance(function.expressions[0], exp.Unpack)
    assert isinstance(function.expressions[0].this, exp.Anonymous)
    assert function.expressions[1] == exp.Literal.number(5)

    assert tree.sql("duckdb") == (
        r"SELECT PACK(*COLUMNS('m\d'), 5) FROM measurements"
    )


def test_duckdb_multiple_unpacked_arguments():
    tree = parse_one(
        "SELECT struct_pack(*COLUMNS('a.*'), *COLUMNS('b.*')) FROM measurements",
        read="duckdb",
    )

    struct_pack = tree.find(exp.Struct)
    assert struct_pack is not None
    assert len(struct_pack.expressions) == 2
    assert all(isinstance(arg, exp.Unpack) for arg in struct_pack.expressions)

    patterns = [arg.this.expressions[0].this for arg in struct_pack.expressions]
    assert patterns == ["a.*", "b.*"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql", ["SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tbl", "SELECT struct_pack(*) FROM tbl"]
)
def test_duckdb_ordinary_function_star_is_unchanged(sql):
    tree = parse_one(sql, read="duckdb")

    function = tree.find(exp.Count) or tree.find(exp.Struct)
    assert function is not None

    if isinstance(function, exp.Count):
        star = function.this
    else:
        assert len(function.expressions) == 1
        star = function.expressions[0]

    assert isinstance(star, exp.Star)
    assert not isinstance(star, exp.Unpack)


def test_duckdb_multiplication_in_function_argument_is_not_unpacking():
    tree = parse_one("SELECT pack(a * b) FROM tbl", read="duckdb")

    assert tree.find(exp.Mul) is not None
    assert tree.find(exp.Unpack) is None
    assert tree.sql("duckdb") == "SELECT PACK(a * b) FROM tbl"

import threading
from unittest import mock

import pytest

from google.api_core import bidi
from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber import client
from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber import scheduler
from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber._protocol import streaming_pull_manager
from google.pubsub_v1 import types as gapic_types


def _make_manager():
    client_ = mock.create_autospec(client.Client, instance=True)
    scheduler_ = mock.create_autospec(scheduler.Scheduler, instance=True)
    manager = streaming_pull_manager.StreamingPullManager(
        client_,
        "projects/project/subscriptions/subscription",
        scheduler=scheduler_,
        await_callbacks_on_shutdown=True,
    )

    manager._rpc = mock.create_autospec(bidi.ResumableBidiRpc, instance=True)
    manager._consumer = mock.create_autospec(
        bidi.BackgroundConsumer, instance=True
    )
    manager._consumer.is_active = True
    manager._consumer.is_paused = False
    manager._dispatcher = mock.Mock()
    manager._leaser = mock.Mock()
    manager._leaser.message_count = 0
    manager._leaser.bytes = 0
    manager._heartbeater = mock.Mock()
    manager._callback = mock.Mock()

    # Model the leaser's accounting so that adding a message does not leave the
    # load calculation based on stale mock attributes.
    def add_to_lease(items):
        manager._leaser.message_count += len(items)
        manager._leaser.bytes += len(items) * 10

    manager._leaser.add.side_effect = add_to_lease

    # Keep the test focused on response processing rather than lease-histogram
    # calculations or exactly-once modack handling. The real
    # _maybe_release_messages() must run because it releases newly received
    # messages from the on-hold queue and schedules their callbacks.
    manager._exactly_once_delivery_enabled = mock.Mock(return_value=False)
    manager._obtain_ack_deadline = mock.Mock(return_value=10)
    manager._send_lease_modacks = mock.Mock(return_value=set())

    return manager, scheduler_, manager._leaser


def _response():
    return gapic_types.StreamingPullResponse(
        received_messages=[
            gapic_types.ReceivedMessage(
                ack_id="test-ack-id",
                message=gapic_types.PubsubMessage(
                    data=b"test message",
                    message_id="1",
                ),
            )
        ],
        subscription_properties=(
            gapic_types.StreamingPullResponse.SubscriptionProperties(
                exactly_once_delivery_enabled=False
            )
        ),
    )


def test_on_response_processes_messages_while_manager_is_running():
    manager, scheduler_, leaser_ = _make_manager()

    manager._on_response(_response())

    # A guard against responses arriving during shutdown must not disable
    # normal delivery and lease management.
    assert scheduler_.schedule.call_count == 1
    assert leaser_.add.call_count == 1
    assert manager._messages_on_hold.size == 0


@pytest.mark.parametrize("missing_helper", ["scheduler", "leaser", "both"])
def test_on_response_ignores_response_after_shutdown_state(missing_helper):
    manager, scheduler_, leaser_ = _make_manager()

    # Shutdown clears these helpers while the background consumer may still
    # have a response callback in flight.
    if missing_helper in ("scheduler", "both"):
        manager._scheduler = None
    if missing_helper in ("leaser", "both"):
        manager._leaser = None

    # In particular, this must not raise AssertionError from _on_response.
    manager._on_response(_response())

    scheduler_.schedule.assert_not_called()
    leaser_.add.assert_not_called()
    assert manager._messages_on_hold.size == 0


def test_close_while_on_response_is_in_flight_does_not_assert_or_dispatch():
    manager, scheduler_, leaser_ = _make_manager()
    response_started = threading.Event()
    finish_response = threading.Event()
    response_errors = []

    def pause_response_processing(*args, **kwargs):
        # Hold _on_response before it dispatches the message, allowing close()
        # to complete and clear the manager's helpers.
        response_started.set()
        assert finish_response.wait(timeout=5)
        return 10

    manager._obtain_ack_deadline = mock.Mock(
        side_effect=pause_response_processing
    )

    def process_response():
        try:
            manager._on_response(_response())
        except BaseException as exc:  # surface background-thread failures
            response_errors.append(exc)

    response_thread = threading.Thread(target=process_response)
    response_thread.start()

    assert response_started.wait(timeout=5)
    try:
        manager.close()
        shutdown_thread = manager._regular_shutdown_thread
        if shutdown_thread is not None:
            shutdown_thread.join(timeout=5)
    finally:
        finish_response.set()

    response_thread.join(timeout=5)

    assert not response_thread.is_alive()
    if shutdown_thread is not None:
        assert not shutdown_thread.is_alive()
    assert response_errors == []
    scheduler_.schedule.assert_not_called()
    leaser_.add.assert_not_called()
    assert manager._messages_on_hold.size == 0

from streamlink import Streamlink
from streamlink.plugin.api import useragents
from streamlink.plugins.kick import Kick, KickAdapter

VOD_HLS_URL = "https://kick.com/hls/vod/master.m3u8"
CLIP_HLS_URL = "https://kick.com/hls/clip/master.m3u8"

#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=1280000,RESOLUTION=1280x720
https://kick.com/hls/media.m3u8
"""


@pytest.fixture
def session():
    return Streamlink()


def test_kick_session_headers_and_adapter(session):
    """Kick requests need the Chrome user agent and custom TLS adapter."""
    session.http.headers["User-Agent"] = "custom-user-agent"

    Kick(session, "https://kick.com/zmok")

    assert session.http.headers["User-Agent"] == useragents.CHROME
    assert session.http.headers["Sec-Fetch-User"] == "?1"
    assert isinstance(
        session.http.get_adapter("https://kick.com/api/v2/channels/zmok/livestream"),
        KickAdapter,
    )


def test_kick_does_not_clobber_unrelated_session_headers(session):
    """The 403 workaround must not discard user-defined HTTP configuration."""
    custom_headers = {
        "Accept": "application/custom",
        "Accept-Language": "en-GB",
        "Accept-Encoding": "identity",
        "Sec-Fetch-Dest": "empty",
        "Sec-Fetch-Mode": "cors",
        "Sec-Fetch-Site": "same-origin",
        "Cache-Control": "max-age=60",
        "X-Streamlink-Test": "custom-value",
    }
    session.http.headers.update(custom_headers)

    Kick(session, "https://kick.com/zmok")

    for name, value in custom_headers.items():
        assert session.http.headers[name] == value

            VOD_HLS_URL,

        ),
        pytest.param(
            "https://kick.com/CLIP_CHANNEL?clip=CLIP_ID",
            "https://kick.com/api/v2/clips/CLIP_ID",
            CLIP_HLS_URL,
            {
                "clip": {
                    "clip_url": CLIP_HLS_URL,
                    "category": {"name": "Clip category"},
                    "title": "Clip title",
                },
            },
            "CLIP_ID",
            "CLIP_CHANNEL",
            "Clip title",
            "Clip category",
            id="clip",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_kick_api_requests_avoid_403_and_return_streams(
    session,
    requests_mock,
    url,
    api_url,
    hls_url,
    payload,
    expected_id,
    expected_author,
    expected_title,
    expected_category,
):
    """Live, VOD and clip requests must all use the Cloudflare-compatible headers."""
    requests_mock.get(
        "https://kick.com/",
        headers={"Set-Cookie": "XSRF-TOKEN=TEST_TOKEN; Path=/; Secure"},
        text="",
    )

    def api_response(request, context):
        # Reproduce the reported server behavior: requests without the required
        # browser user agent are rejected before the API returns its JSON data.
        if request.headers.get("User-Agent") != useragents.CHROME:
            context.status_code = 403
            context.headers["Content-Type"] = "text/html"
            return "Forbidden"

        context.headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
        return json.dumps(payload)

    requests_mock.get(api_url, text=api_response)
    requests_mock.get(hls_url, text=VARIANT_PLAYLIST)

    plugin = Kick(session, url)
    streams = plugin.streams()

    assert streams
    assert all(isinstance(stream, HLSStream) for stream in streams.values())
    assert plugin.id == expected_id
    assert plugin.author == expected_author
    assert plugin.title == expected_title
    if expected_category is not None:
        assert plugin.category == expected_category

    history = requests_mock.request_history
    api_requests = [request for request in history if request.url == api_url]
    assert len(api_requests) == 1

    # The token request, API request and playlist request all need the same
    # session-level workaround, rather than only the API request being fixed.
    assert history[0].url == "https://kick.com/"
    for request in history:
        assert request.headers["User-Agent"] == useragents.CHROME
        assert request.headers["Sec-Fetch-User"] == "?1"

    api_request = api_requests[0]
    assert api_request.headers["Accept"] == "application/json"
    assert api_request.headers["Referer"] == url
    assert api_request.headers["Authorization"] == "Bearer TEST_TOKEN"

import pytest

from infrahub_sdk import Config, InfrahubClient, InfrahubClientSync
from infrahub_sdk.exceptions import NodeNotFoundError
from infrahub_sdk.schema import NodeSchema


KIND = "BuiltinLocation"


def _location_schema() -> NodeSchema:
    return NodeSchema(
        name="Location",
        namespace="Builtin",
        default_filter="name__value",
        attributes=[
            {"name": "name", "kind": "String", "unique": True},
            {"name": "description", "kind": "String", "optional": True},
        ],
    )


def _async_client(results: list[object]) -> InfrahubClient:
    client = InfrahubClient(config=Config(address="http://mock"))
    client.schema.get = AsyncMock(return_value=_location_schema())
    client.filters = AsyncMock(return_value=results)
    return client


def _sync_client(results: list[object]) -> InfrahubClientSync:
    client = InfrahubClientSync(config=Config(address="http://mock"))
    client.schema.get = MagicMock(return_value=_location_schema())
    client.filters = MagicMock(return_value=results)
    return client

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


def _drop_actions(statement):
    return [
        action
        for action in statement.args.get("actions", [])
        if isinstance(action, exp.Drop)
    ]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("sql", "dialect", "if_exists"),
    [
        ("ALTER TABLE ride DROP COLUMN activity_id", "mysql", False),
        ("ALTER TABLE ride DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS activity_id", "mysql", True),
        ("ALTER TABLE `ride` DROP COLUMN `activity_id`", "mysql", False),
        ("ALTER TABLE ride DROP COLUMN activity_id CASCADE", "postgres", False),
    ],
)
def test_alter_table_drop_column_is_not_a_table(sql, dialect, if_exists):
    statement = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read=dialect)

    assert isinstance(statement, exp.Alter)
    assert [table.name for table in statement.find_all(exp.Table)] == ["ride"]

    drops = _drop_actions(statement)
    assert len(drops) == 1

    drop = drops[0]
    assert drop.args.get("kind") == "COLUMN"
    assert bool(drop.args.get("exists")) is if_exists
    assert isinstance(drop.this, exp.Column)
    assert drop.this.name == "activity_id"

    # Fixing the AST must not discard valid DROP COLUMN options.
    assert statement.sql(dialect=dialect) == sql


def test_alter_table_with_multiple_drop_columns_has_only_the_altered_table():

    statement = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="mysql")

    assert [table.name for table in statement.find_all(exp.Table)] == ["ride"]

    drops = _drop_actions(statement)
    assert len(drops) == 2

    assert all(isinstance(drop.this, exp.Column) for drop in drops)
    assert [drop.this.name for drop in drops] == ["activity_id", "legacy_id"]
    assert statement.sql(dialect="mysql") == sql

import threading
from unittest import mock

import pytest

from google.api_core import bidi
from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber import client
from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber import message
from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber import scheduler
from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber._protocol import dispatcher
from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber._protocol import heartbeater
from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber._protocol import leaser
from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber._protocol import streaming_pull_manager
from google.pubsub_v1 import types as gapic_types


def _make_manager():
    client_ = mock.create_autospec(client.Client, instance=True)
    scheduler_ = mock.create_autospec(scheduler.Scheduler, instance=True)
    scheduler_.queue = mock.sentinel.request_queue

    manager = streaming_pull_manager.StreamingPullManager(
        client_, "subscription-name", scheduler=scheduler_
    )
    manager._callback = mock.sentinel.callback
    manager._dispatcher = mock.create_autospec(dispatcher.Dispatcher, instance=True)
    manager._leaser = mock.create_autospec(leaser.Leaser, instance=True)
    manager._leaser.message_count = 0
    manager._leaser.bytes = 0
    manager._consumer = mock.create_autospec(bidi.BackgroundConsumer, instance=True)
    manager._consumer.is_active = True
    manager._consumer.is_paused = False
    manager._heartbeater = mock.create_autospec(
        heartbeater.Heartbeater, instance=True
    )
    manager._rpc = mock.create_autospec(bidi.ResumableBidiRpc, instance=True)

    # Lease modacks happen before the response-processing critical section. Keep
    # these tests focused on what happens when shutdown clears the helpers.
    manager._send_lease_modacks = mock.Mock(return_value=set())
    return manager, scheduler_, manager._leaser


def _response():
    return gapic_types.StreamingPullResponse(
        received_messages=[
            gapic_types.ReceivedMessage(
                ack_id="ack-1",
                message=gapic_types.PubsubMessage(
                    data=b"payload", message_id="message-1"
                ),
            )
        ],
        subscription_properties=gapic_types.StreamingPullResponse.SubscriptionProperties(
            exactly_once_delivery_enabled=False
        ),
    )


def _assert_response_was_ignored(manager, scheduler_, leaser_):
    assert manager._messages_on_hold.size == 0
    assert manager._on_hold_bytes == 0
    scheduler_.schedule.assert_not_called()
    leaser_.add.assert_not_called()
    leaser_.start_lease_expiry_timer.assert_not_called()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("cleared_helper", ["scheduler", "leaser", "both"])
def test_on_response_ignores_response_when_shutdown_has_cleared_helpers(
    cleared_helper,
):
    """A response arriving during shutdown must not hit assertions or use helpers."""
    manager, scheduler_, leaser_ = _make_manager()

    if cleared_helper in ("scheduler", "both"):
        manager._scheduler = None
    if cleared_helper in ("leaser", "both"):
        manager._leaser = None

    manager._on_response(_response())

    _assert_response_was_ignored(manager, scheduler_, leaser_)


def test_on_response_after_close_returns_without_processing_messages():
    """Exercise the actual close() shutdown path from the issue report."""
    manager, scheduler_, leaser_ = _make_manager()

    manager.close()
    shutdown_thread = manager._regular_shutdown_thread
    assert shutdown_thread is not None
    shutdown_thread.join(timeout=5)
    assert not shutdown_thread.is_alive()
    assert manager._scheduler is None
    assert manager._leaser is None

    # This represents a response already in flight when future.cancel() caused
    # the manager to close. It should be discarded rather than raising.
    manager._on_response(_response())

    _assert_response_was_ignored(manager, scheduler_, leaser_)


def test_on_response_close_race_before_response_critical_section():
    """Deterministically interleave shutdown and an in-flight response."""
    manager, scheduler_, leaser_ = _make_manager()
    modacks_started = threading.Event()
    finish_modacks = threading.Event()
    errors = []

    def blocked_modacks(*args, **kwargs):
        modacks_started.set()
        if not finish_modacks.wait(timeout=5):
            raise TimeoutError("test did not release _on_response")
        return set()

    manager._send_lease_modacks.side_effect = blocked_modacks

    def process_response():
        try:
            manager._on_response(_response())
        except BaseException as exc:
            errors.append(exc)

    response_thread = threading.Thread(target=process_response)
    response_thread.start()

    if not modacks_started.wait(timeout=5):
        finish_modacks.set()
        response_thread.join(timeout=5)
        pytest.fail("_on_response did not reach the synchronization point")

    # _on_response is now in flight, but has not entered its response-processing
    # critical section. This is the state produced when close() wins the race.
    with manager._pause_resume_lock:
        manager._scheduler = None
        manager._leaser = None

    finish_modacks.set()
    response_thread.join(timeout=5)

    assert not response_thread.is_alive()
    assert errors == []
    _assert_response_was_ignored(manager, scheduler_, leaser_)


def test_on_response_still_processes_messages_while_running():
    """The shutdown guard must not suppress normal message delivery."""
    manager, scheduler_, leaser_ = _make_manager()

    def fake_add(items):
        leaser_.message_count += len(items)
        leaser_.bytes += len(items) * 10

    leaser_.add.side_effect = fake_add

    manager._on_response(_response())

    scheduler_.schedule.assert_called_once()
    callback, scheduled_message = scheduler_.schedule.call_args[0]
    assert callback is manager._callback
    assert isinstance(scheduled_message, message.Message)
    assert scheduled_message.ack_id == "ack-1"
    assert scheduled_message.data == b"payload"

    # With load below the flow-control limit, the message is released from the
    # internal hold queue and its lease-expiry timer is started.
    assert manager._messages_on_hold.size == 0
    assert manager._on_hold_bytes == 0
    leaser_.start_lease_expiry_timer.assert_called_once_with(["ack-1"])

from __future__ import annotations

import _asyncio as c_asyncio
import asyncio
import math
from contextlib import contextmanager, suppress
from unittest.mock import patch

import pytest

from anyio._backends import _asyncio as asyncio_backend
from anyio.lowlevel import checkpoint_if_cancelled, get_async_backend


async def _make_c_task() -> c_asyncio.Task:
    """Create a real C-accelerated task, independently of the loop task factory."""
    task = c_asyncio.Task(asyncio.sleep(60), loop=asyncio.get_running_loop())
    assert type(task) is c_asyncio.Task
    assert not isinstance(task, asyncio.tasks._PyTask)
    return task


async def _dispose_task(task: c_asyncio.Task) -> None:
    task.cancel()
    with suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
        await task


@contextmanager
def _return_c_task_with_split_task_classes(task: c_asyncio.Task):
    """
    Reproduce a loop returning a C task while asyncio.Task names the Python task.

    Normally asyncio.Task is an alias for _asyncio.Task. The regression concerns
    the runtime case where that identity check does not hold; a typing cast cannot
    change the result of isinstance().
    """
    with patch.object(asyncio_backend, "current_task", return_value=task):
        with patch.object(asyncio_backend.asyncio, "Task", asyncio.tasks._PyTask):
            yield


def test_checkpoint_if_cancelled_accepts_c_task_without_task_state() -> None:
    async def scenario() -> None:
        task = await _make_c_task()
        try:
            with _return_c_task_with_split_task_classes(task):
                # An unknown task has no AnyIO cancel scope, so this is a no-op.
                await checkpoint_if_cancelled()
        finally:
            await _dispose_task(task)

    asyncio.run(scenario())


def test_current_effective_deadline_accepts_c_task_without_task_state() -> None:
    async def scenario() -> None:
        task = await _make_c_task()
        try:
            with _return_c_task_with_split_task_classes(task):
                assert get_async_backend().current_effective_deadline() == math.inf
        finally:
            await _dispose_task(task)

    asyncio.run(scenario())


def test_checkpoint_if_cancelled_uses_state_registered_for_c_task() -> None:
    async def scenario() -> None:
        task = await _make_c_task()
        scope = asyncio_backend.CancelScope()
        scope.cancel()
        asyncio_backend._task_states[task] = asyncio_backend.TaskState(None, scope)
        try:
            with _return_c_task_with_split_task_classes(task):
                # The C task must not merely be tolerated: its registered cancel
                # scope still has to participate in cancellation checkpoints.
                with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
                    await checkpoint_if_cancelled()
        finally:
            del asyncio_backend._task_states[task]
            await _dispose_task(task)

    asyncio.run(scenario())


def test_current_effective_deadline_uses_state_registered_for_c_task() -> None:
    async def scenario() -> None:
        task = await _make_c_task()
        deadline = asyncio.get_running_loop().time() + 60
        try:
            # An active scope has a timeout handle, which makes its deadline
            # visible through current_effective_deadline().
            with asyncio_backend.CancelScope(deadline=deadline) as scope:
                asyncio_backend._task_states[task] = asyncio_backend.TaskState(
                    None, scope
                )
                try:
                    with _return_c_task_with_split_task_classes(task):
                        assert (
                            get_async_backend().current_effective_deadline()
                            == pytest.approx(deadline)
                        )
                finally:
                    del asyncio_backend._task_states[task]
        finally:
            await _dispose_task(task)

    asyncio.run(scenario())


def test_no_current_task_remains_supported() -> None:
    async def scenario() -> None:
        with patch.object(asyncio_backend, "current_task", return_value=None):
            await checkpoint_if_cancelled()
            assert get_async_backend().current_effective_deadline() == math.inf

    asyncio.run(scenario())

import pytest

import dns.exception
import dns.message
import dns.rdatatype
import dns.versioned
import dns.xfr
import dns.zone


# An IXFR response can use AXFR-style answer contents when the server cannot
# provide incremental differences.  The response question still describes the
# original IXFR request, including in subsequent messages of a TCP transfer.
IXFR_AXFR_FIRST = """id 1
opcode QUERY
rcode NOERROR
flags AA
;QUESTION
example. IN IXFR
;ANSWER
@ 3600 IN SOA foo bar 2 2 3 4 5
@ 3600 IN NS ns1
"""

IXFR_AXFR_SOA_ONLY = """id 1
opcode QUERY
rcode NOERROR
flags AA
;QUESTION
example. IN IXFR
;ANSWER
@ 3600 IN SOA foo bar 2 2 3 4 5
"""

IXFR_AXFR_NS_ONLY = """id 1
opcode QUERY
rcode NOERROR
flags AA
;QUESTION
example. IN IXFR
;ANSWER
@ 3600 IN NS ns1
"""

IXFR_AXFR_LAST = """id 1
opcode QUERY
rcode NOERROR
flags AA
;QUESTION
example. IN IXFR
;ANSWER
@ 3600 IN NS ns2
ns1 3600 IN A 10.0.0.1
ns2 3600 IN A 10.0.0.2
@ 3600 IN SOA foo bar 2 2 3 4 5
"""

EXPECTED = """@ 3600 IN SOA foo bar 2 2 3 4 5
@ 3600 IN NS ns1
@ 3600 IN NS ns2
ns1 3600 IN A 10.0.0.1
ns2 3600 IN A 10.0.0.2
"""


def _message(text, zone):
    return dns.message.from_text(
        text, origin=zone.origin, one_rr_per_rrset=True
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "parts",
    [
        [IXFR_AXFR_FIRST, IXFR_AXFR_LAST],
        [IXFR_AXFR_SOA_ONLY, IXFR_AXFR_NS_ONLY, IXFR_AXFR_LAST],
    ],
    ids=["fallback-in-first-message", "fallback-in-later-message"],
)
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "zone_factory",
    [dns.zone.Zone, dns.versioned.Zone],
    ids=["zone", "versioned"],
)
def test_multipart_ixfr_axfr_fallback_keeps_ixfr_question_valid(
    zone_factory, parts
):
    """Switching answer processing to AXFR must not change the query type."""
    zone = zone_factory("example.")
    messages = [_message(part, zone) for part in parts]

    with dns.xfr.Inbound(zone, dns.rdatatype.IXFR, serial=1) as xfr:
        for message in messages[:-1]:
            assert not xfr.process_message(message)
        assert xfr.process_message(messages[-1])

    expected = dns.zone.from_text(EXPECTED, "example.")
    assert zone == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("question", "error"),
    [
        ("example. IN AXFR", "wrong question rdatatype"),
        ("other.example. IN IXFR", "wrong question name"),
    ],
    ids=["wrong-type", "wrong-name"],
)
def test_multipart_ixfr_axfr_fallback_still_validates_question(
    question, error
):
    """Fallback must not disable validation against the original IXFR query."""
    zone = dns.zone.Zone("example.")

    with dns.xfr.Inbound(zone, dns.rdatatype.IXFR, serial=1) as xfr:
        assert not xfr.process_message(_message(IXFR_AXFR_FIRST, zone))
        bad_last = IXFR_AXFR_LAST.replace("example. IN IXFR", question)
        with pytest.raises(dns.exception.FormError, match=error):
            xfr.process_message(_message(bad_last, zone))


def test_multipart_ixfr_axfr_fallback_allows_omitted_later_question():
    """A later response message may omit its question section entirely."""
    zone = dns.zone.Zone("example.")
    last_without_question = IXFR_AXFR_LAST.replace(
        ";QUESTION\nexample. IN IXFR\n", ""
    )

    with dns.xfr.Inbound(zone, dns.rdatatype.IXFR, serial=1) as xfr:
        assert not xfr.process_message(_message(IXFR_AXFR_FIRST, zone))
        assert xfr.process_message(_message(last_without_question, zone))

    expected = dns.zone.from_text(EXPECTED, "example.")
    assert zone == expected

"""Tests for reporting the JWST software version at the end of processing."""

import logging

import pytest
from stpipe import crds_client
from stdatamodels.jwst import datamodels

import jwst
from jwst.stpipe import Pipeline, Step
from jwst.stpipe.tests.util import capture_log


CRDS_CONTEXT = "jwst_1234.pmap"
CORE_LOGGER = "jwst.stpipe.core"


class ReferenceUsingStep(Step):
    """Minimal step that exercises finalization with a reference file."""

    reference_file_types = ["flat"]

    def process(self, model):
        self.get_reference_file(model, "flat")
        return model


class PassthroughPipeline(Pipeline):
    """Pipeline whose result needs no reference files."""

    step_defs = {}

    def process(self, model):
        return model


class PipelineWithReferenceStep(Pipeline):
    """Pipeline used to check that nested steps do not duplicate the report."""

    step_defs = {"reference_step": ReferenceUsingStep}

    def process(self, model):
        return self.reference_step(model)


@pytest.fixture
def offline_crds(monkeypatch):
    """Provide deterministic CRDS results without files or network access."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        crds_client,
        "get_reference_file",
        lambda *args, **kwargs: "flat.fits",
    )
    # Step.get_reference_file normally verifies that the returned path can be
    # opened.  Reference-file I/O is irrelevant to these logging tests.
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        crds_client,
        "check_reference_open",
        lambda reference_name, *args, **kwargs: reference_name,
    )
    # Pipelines prefetch all reference types used by their substeps before
    # process() runs.  Disable that separate lookup; the step still retrieves
    # a reference explicitly, so finalization sees a nonempty reference list.
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        crds_client,
        "get_multiple_reference_paths",
        lambda *args, **kwargs: {},
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(crds_client, "get_svn_version", lambda: "1.2.3")
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        crds_client,
        "get_context_used",
        lambda *args, **kwargs: CRDS_CONTEXT,
    )


def assert_version_reported_after_crds(records):
    """Check placement, content, and level of the final core log messages."""
    core_records = [
        record for record in records if record.name == CORE_LOGGER
    ]
    messages = [record.getMessage() for record in core_records]
    crds_message = f"Results used CRDS context: {CRDS_CONTEXT}"

    version_indices = [
        index
        for index, message in enumerate(messages)
        if jwst.__version__ in message and "version" in message.lower()
    ]

    # There should be one report, at the end of finalization, rather than
    # reports from every nested step scattered throughout the log.
    assert len(version_indices) == 1
    version_index = version_indices[0]
    assert version_index == len(messages) - 1
    assert version_index > 0

    # Preserve the existing CRDS report and put the version immediately next
    # to it, as requested, rather than moving version reporting to startup.
    assert messages[version_index - 1] == crds_message
    assert messages.count(crds_message) == 1
    assert core_records[version_index].levelno == logging.INFO


def test_pipeline_reports_version_after_crds_context(offline_crds):
    with capture_log() as records:
        with datamodels.ImageModel((2, 2)) as model:
            result = PassthroughPipeline().run(model)
            assert isinstance(result, datamodels.ImageModel)

    assert_version_reported_after_crds(records)


def test_standalone_step_reports_version_after_crds_context(offline_crds):
    with capture_log() as records:
        with datamodels.ImageModel((2, 2)) as model:
            result = ReferenceUsingStep().run(model)

            # Confirm that the test actually exercised the reference-file
            # branch which produces the existing end-of-run CRDS report.
            assert result.meta.ref_file.crds.context_used == CRDS_CONTEXT

    assert_version_reported_after_crds(records)


def test_nested_step_does_not_duplicate_version_report(offline_crds):
    with capture_log() as records:
        with datamodels.ImageModel((2, 2)) as model:
            result = PipelineWithReferenceStep().run(model)
            assert isinstance(result, datamodels.ImageModel)

    assert_version_reported_after_crds(records)

            username="admin",
            password="infrahub",
            sync_requester=test_client.sync_request,
        )
        return InfrahubClientSync(config=config)

    async def test_get_missing_node_returns_none_when_raise_is_disabled(
        self, client: InfrahubClientSync, init_db_base
    ):
        node = client.get(
            kind="BuiltinLocation",
            name__value="sync-location-that-does-not-exist",
            raise_when_missing=False,
        )

        assert node is None

    async def test_get_missing_node_still_raises_by_default_and_when_enabled(
        self, client: InfrahubClientSync, init_db_base
    ):
        with pytest.raises(NodeNotFoundError):
            client.get(kind="BuiltinLocation", id="sync-default-missing-location")

        with pytest.raises(NodeNotFoundError):
            client.get(
                kind="BuiltinLocation",
                id="sync-explicit-raise-missing-location",
                raise_when_missing=True,
            )

    async def test_get_existing_node_is_unaffected_when_raise_is_disabled(
        self, client: InfrahubClientSync, init_db_base
    ):
        created = client.create(
            kind="BuiltinLocation",
            name="sync-existing-raise-when-missing",
            description="existing node",
            type="site",
        )
        created.save()

        node = client.get(kind="BuiltinLocation", id=created.id, raise_when_missing=False)

        assert isinstance(node, InfrahubNodeSync)
        assert node.id == created.id
        assert node.name.value == "sync-existing-raise-when-missing"

    async def test_raise_disabled_does_not_bypass_filter_validation(
        self, client: InfrahubClientSync, init_db_base
    ):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="At least one filter must be provided"):
            client.get(kind="BuiltinLocation", raise_when_missing=False)

    async def test_raise_disabled_does_not_hide_multiple_results(
        self, client: InfrahubClientSync, init_db_base
    ):
        description = "sync-duplicate-raise-when-missing"
        for name in ("sync-duplicate-location-1", "sync-duplicate-location-2"):
            node = client.create(
                kind="BuiltinLocation",
                name=name,
                description=description,
                type="site",
            )
            node.save()

        with pytest.raises(IndexError, match="More than 1 node returned"):
            client.get(
                kind="BuiltinLocation",
                description__value=description,
                raise_when_missing=False,
            )

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest
import tomlkit

from pdm.models.requirements import parse_requirement


def _read_pyproject(project):
    return tomlkit.parse(project.root.joinpath("pyproject.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def _configure_dependency_tables(project, legacy_groups, dependency_groups=None):
    """Set up the dependency tables without going through the code under test."""
    tool = project.pyproject._data.setdefault("tool", {})
    pdm_settings = tool.setdefault("pdm", {})
    pdm_settings["dev-dependencies"] = legacy_groups
    if dependency_groups is not None:
        project.pyproject._data["dependency-groups"] = dependency_groups
    project.pyproject.write()


def _add_dev_requirement_to_pyproject(project, group, requirement="ruff"):
    """Perform the pyproject-editing part of ``pdm add -d`` without resolving.

    Resolution and installation are irrelevant to this regression and would require
    package indexes or builds of the legacy editable requirements.
    """
    dependencies, setter = project.use_pyproject_dependencies(group, dev=True)
    setter([*dependencies, requirement])
    project.pyproject.write()


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "expected_group",
    [
        pytest.param("dev", id="default-dev-group"),
        pytest.param("lint", id="explicit-dev-group"),
    ],
)
def test_add_dev_dependency_uses_requested_group_with_legacy_dev_dependencies(
    project, expected_group
):
    """A legacy group name must not replace the group requested by ``pdm add``."""
    legacy_groups = {
        "workspaces": [
            "-e ./packages/pkg-app",
            "-e ./packages/pkg-core",
        ]
    }
    _configure_dependency_tables(project, legacy_groups)

    _add_dev_requirement_to_pyproject(project, expected_group)

    document = _read_pyproject(project)
    groups = document["dependency-groups"]

    assert set(groups) == {expected_group}
    added = list(groups[expected_group])
    assert len(added) == 1
    assert parse_requirement(str(added[0])).name == "ruff"

    # The legacy editable-only group must neither be modified nor migrated.
    assert document["tool"]["pdm"]["dev-dependencies"].unwrap() == legacy_groups


def test_add_to_existing_group_does_not_duplicate_legacy_editable_group(project):
    """Merging legacy groups for lookup must not mutate dependency-groups.

    A mixed legacy group must not be partially copied with only its non-editable
    requirements either: the group containing editables stays exclusively in
    tool.pdm.dev-dependencies.
    """
    legacy_groups = {
        "workspaces": [
            "-e ./packages/pkg-app",
            "packaging>=24",
        ]
    }
    _configure_dependency_tables(
        project,
        legacy_groups,
        dependency_groups={
            "lint": ["black>=24"],
            "test": ["pytest>=8"],
        },
    )

    _add_dev_requirement_to_pyproject(project, "lint")

    document = _read_pyproject(project)
    groups = document["dependency-groups"]

    # Only the requested existing group changes; no legacy group is duplicated.
    assert set(groups) == {"lint", "test"}
    lint = [str(item) for item in groups["lint"]]
    assert len(lint) == 2
    assert "black>=24" in lint
    assert sum(parse_requirement(item).name == "ruff" for item in lint) == 1
    assert list(groups["test"]) == ["pytest>=8"]

    assert document["tool"]["pdm"]["dev-dependencies"].unwrap() == legacy_groups
