import re

import pytest

from streamlink.exceptions import PluginError
from streamlink.plugin.api import useragents
from streamlink.plugins.kick import Kick
from streamlink.session import Streamlink
from streamlink.stream.hls import HLSStream


LIVE_URL = "https://kick.com/zmok"
LIVE_API_URL = "https://kick.com/api/v2/channels/zmok/livestream"
VOD_ID = "4acba712-a1cd-45b0-8ce0-4b534d4c271f"
VOD_URL = f"https://kick.com/kukudota2/videos/{VOD_ID}"
VOD_API_URL = f"https://kick.com/api/v1/video/{VOD_ID}"
KICK_HOME_URL = "https://kick.com/"

MASTER_PLAYLIST = """#EXTM3U
#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:PROGRAM-ID=1,BANDWIDTH=1280000,RESOLUTION=1280x720
https://media.example.com/720p.m3u8
"""


@pytest.fixture
def session():
    return Streamlink()


def assert_browser_api_request(request, referer):
    match = re.search(r"Chrome/(?P<full>(?P<main>\d+)\S+)", useragents.CHROME)
    assert match is not None

    expected_headers = {
        "Accept": "application/json",
        "Accept-Language": "en-US",
        "Referer": referer,
        "User-Agent": useragents.CHROME,
        "sec-ch-ua": f'"Not:A-Brand";v="24", "Chromium";v="{match["main"]}"',
        "sec-ch-ua-arch": '"x86"',
        "sec-ch-ua-bitness": '"64"',
        "sec-ch-ua-full-version": f'"{match["full"]}"',
        "sec-ch-ua-full-version-list": (
            f'"Not:A-Brand";v="24.0.0.0", "Chromium";v="{match["full"]}"'
        ),
        "sec-ch-ua-mobile": "?0",
        "sec-ch-ua-model": '""',
        "sec-ch-ua-platform": '"Windows"',
        "sec-ch-ua-platform-version": '"6.14.0"',
        "sec-fetch-dest": "empty",
        "sec-fetch-mode": "cors",
        "sec-fetch-site": "same-origin",
        "sec-fetch-user": "?1",
    }
    for name, value in expected_headers.items():
        assert request.headers.get(name) == value

    # API access must not depend on the old, unreliable XSRF bearer token.
    assert "Authorization" not in request.headers


def test_live_stream_uses_browser_headers_without_token_request(session, requests_mock):
    playback_url = "https://media.example.com/live/master.m3u8"
    home = requests_mock.get(KICK_HOME_URL, json={})
    api = requests_mock.get(
        LIVE_API_URL,
        json={
            "data": {
                "playback_url": playback_url,
                "id": 12345,
                "category": {"name": "Just Chatting"},
                "session_title": "Live title",
            },
        },
    )
    requests_mock.get(playback_url, text=MASTER_PLAYLIST)

    plugin = Kick(session, LIVE_URL)
    streams = plugin.streams()

    assert streams
    assert all(isinstance(stream, HLSStream) for stream in streams.values())
    assert plugin.id == 12345
    assert plugin.author == "zmok"
    assert plugin.category == "Just Chatting"
    assert plugin.title == "Live title"

    assert home.call_count == 0
    assert api.call_count == 1
    assert_browser_api_request(api.request_history[0], LIVE_URL)


def test_vod_stream_uses_browser_headers_without_token_request(session, requests_mock):
    playback_url = "https://media.example.com/vod/master.m3u8"
    home = requests_mock.get(KICK_HOME_URL, json={})
    api = requests_mock.get(
        VOD_API_URL,
        json={
            "source": playback_url,
            "livestream": {
                "session_title": "VOD title",
                "channel": {
                    "user": {
                        "username": "kukudota2",
                    },
                },
            },
        },
    )
    requests_mock.get(playback_url, text=MASTER_PLAYLIST)

    plugin = Kick(session, VOD_URL)
    streams = plugin.streams()

    assert streams
    assert all(isinstance(stream, HLSStream) for stream in streams.values())
    assert plugin.id == VOD_ID
    assert plugin.author == "kukudota2"
    assert plugin.title == "VOD title"

    assert home.call_count == 0
    assert api.call_count == 1
    assert_browser_api_request(api.request_history[0], VOD_URL)


def test_clip_stream_still_uses_the_same_api_request_handling(session, requests_mock):
    url = "https://kick.com/CLIP_CHANNEL/clips/CLIP_ID?foo=bar"
    api_url = "https://kick.com/api/v2/clips/CLIP_ID"
    playback_url = "https://media.example.com/clips/clip.m3u8"
    home = requests_mock.get(KICK_HOME_URL, json={})
    api = requests_mock.get(
        api_url,
        json={
            "clip": {
                "clip_url": playback_url,
                "category": {"name": "Clip category"},
                "title": "Clip title",
            },
        },
    )

    plugin = Kick(session, url)
    streams = plugin.streams()

    assert "clip" in streams
    assert isinstance(streams["clip"], HLSStream)
    assert plugin.id == "CLIP_ID"
    assert plugin.author == "CLIP_CHANNEL"
    assert plugin.category == "Clip category"
    assert plugin.title == "Clip title"

    assert home.call_count == 0
    assert api.call_count == 1
    assert_browser_api_request(api.request_history[0], url)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("url", "api_url"),
    [
        (LIVE_URL, LIVE_API_URL),
        (VOD_URL, VOD_API_URL),
    ],
)
def test_403_is_reported_as_a_plugin_error(session, requests_mock, url, api_url):
    home = requests_mock.get(KICK_HOME_URL, json={})
    api = requests_mock.get(api_url, status_code=403, text="Forbidden")

    plugin = Kick(session, url)
    with pytest.raises(PluginError, match="403"):
        plugin.streams()

    assert home.call_count == 0
    assert api.call_count == 1


def test_offline_livestream_returns_no_streams(session, requests_mock):
    home = requests_mock.get(KICK_HOME_URL, json={})
    api = requests_mock.get(LIVE_API_URL, status_code=404, json={"data": None})

    plugin = Kick(session, LIVE_URL)

    assert plugin.streams() == {}
    assert home.call_count == 0
    assert api.call_count == 1


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("url", "api_url"),
    [
        (LIVE_URL, LIVE_API_URL),
        (VOD_URL, VOD_API_URL),
    ],
)
def test_api_error_messages_are_not_silently_treated_as_no_streams(
    session,
    requests_mock,
    url,
    api_url,
):
    message = "Content is unavailable"
    home = requests_mock.get(KICK_HOME_URL, json={})
    api = requests_mock.get(api_url, status_code=404, json={"message": message})

    plugin = Kick(session, url)
    with pytest.raises(PluginError, match=message):
        plugin.streams()

    assert home.call_count == 0
    assert api.call_count == 1


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("url", "channel", "clip"),
    [
        (
            "https://kick.com/CLIP_CHANNEL?clip=CLIP_ID&foo=bar",
            "CLIP_CHANNEL",
            "CLIP_ID",
        ),
        (
            "https://kick.com/CLIP_CHANNEL/clips/CLIP_ID?foo=bar",
            "CLIP_CHANNEL",
            "CLIP_ID",
        ),
        (
            "https://kick.com/CLIP_CHANNEL/clips/CLIP_ID?clip=OTHER_CLIP_ID&foo=bar",
            "CLIP_CHANNEL",
            "CLIP_ID",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_clip_url_variants(session, url, channel, clip):
    plugin = Kick(session, url)

    assert plugin.matches["clip"]
    assert plugin.match["channel"] == channel
    assert plugin.match["clip"] == clip

import importlib
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

import pytest

from django_cmd import main


def test_main_makes_current_directory_importable(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """A settings module in the invocation directory must be importable."""
    settings_module = "django_cmd_settings_only_in_cwd"
    (tmp_path / f"{settings_module}.py").write_text(
        'SECRET_KEY = "loaded-from-current-directory"\n',
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
    monkeypatch.setenv("DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE", settings_module)
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", ["django", "check"])
    # Prevent a correct implementation from permanently altering the test
    # runner's import path.
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "path", sys.path.copy())
    monkeypatch.delitem(sys.modules, settings_module, raising=False)

    delegated = {}

    def execute(argv):
        delegated["argv"] = argv
        delegated["settings"] = importlib.import_module(settings_module)

    monkeypatch.setattr("django_cmd.execute_from_command_line", execute)

    try:
        main()
    finally:
        sys.modules.pop(settings_module, None)

    assert delegated["argv"] == ["django", "check"]
    assert (
        delegated["settings"].SECRET_KEY == "loaded-from-current-directory"
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("config_filename", "config_contents", "use_environment"),
    [
        pytest.param(None, None, True, id="environment-settings"),
        pytest.param(
            "pyproject.toml",
            '[tool.django]\nsettings_module = "django_cmd_cwd_settings"\n',
            False,
            id="pyproject-settings",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            "setup.cfg",
            "[django]\nsettings_module = django_cmd_cwd_settings\n",
            False,
            id="setup-cfg-settings",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_django_command_loads_settings_from_current_directory(
    tmp_path, config_filename, config_contents, use_environment
):
    """The installed command must work without PYTHONPATH or --pythonpath."""
    settings_module = "django_cmd_cwd_settings"
    (tmp_path / f"{settings_module}.py").write_text(
        "\n".join(
            [
                'SECRET_KEY = "django-cmd-current-directory-test"',
                "INSTALLED_APPS = []",
                "DATABASES = {}",
                "",
            ]
        ),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    if config_filename is not None:
        (tmp_path / config_filename).write_text(
            config_contents, encoding="utf-8"
        )

    env = os.environ.copy()
    # A console script does not normally put its working directory on
    # sys.path. Remove ambient configuration that could hide that fact.
    env.pop("PYTHONPATH", None)
    env.pop("DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE", None)
    if use_environment:
        env["DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE"] = settings_module

    django_executable = shutil.which("django")
    assert django_executable is not None, "The django command should be installed"

    result = subprocess.run(
        [django_executable, "check"],
        cwd=tmp_path,
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=30,
    )

    assert result.returncode == 0, (
        "The django command should automatically make its current working "
        "directory importable, without requiring --pythonpath or an "
        "explicit PYTHONPATH.\n"
        f"stdout:\n{result.stdout}\n"
        f"stderr:\n{result.stderr}"
    )

import logging

import pytest
from stdatamodels.jwst.datamodels import ImageModel

from jwst import __version__
from jwst.stpipe import core
from jwst.stpipe.core import JwstPipeline, JwstStep


CRDS_CONTEXT = "jwst_1234.pmap"


def _mock_crds(monkeypatch):
    """Avoid CRDS access while testing the reporting done by finalize_result."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        core.crds_client, "get_context_used", lambda observatory: CRDS_CONTEXT
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(core.crds_client, "get_svn_version", lambda: "1.2.3")


@pytest.fixture
def core_log_messages():
    """Capture records directly from the stpipe logger, regardless of propagation."""
    messages = []

    class MessageHandler(logging.Handler):
        def emit(self, record):
            messages.append(record.getMessage())

    handler = MessageHandler()
    previous_level = core.log.level
    core.log.addHandler(handler)
    core.log.setLevel(logging.INFO)
    try:
        yield messages
    finally:
        core.log.removeHandler(handler)
        core.log.setLevel(previous_level)


def test_step_reports_jwst_version_after_crds_context(
    monkeypatch, core_log_messages
):
    _mock_crds(monkeypatch)
    step = JwstStep()
    result = ImageModel()

    step.finalize_result(result, [("flat", "flat.fits")])

    # Version reporting belongs at the end of the log, immediately after the
    # existing CRDS context report.
    assert core_log_messages[-2:] == [
        f"Results used CRDS context: {CRDS_CONTEXT}",
        f"Results used jwst version: {__version__}",
    ]


def test_pipeline_reports_jwst_version_after_crds_context(
    monkeypatch, core_log_messages
):
    _mock_crds(monkeypatch)
    pipeline = JwstPipeline()
    result = ImageModel()

    pipeline.finalize_result(result, [])

    assert core_log_messages[-2:] == [
        f"Results used CRDS context: {CRDS_CONTEXT}",
        f"Results used jwst version: {__version__}",
    ]


def test_nested_step_does_not_duplicate_version_report(
    monkeypatch, core_log_messages
):
    _mock_crds(monkeypatch)
    step = JwstStep()
    step.parent = JwstStep()
    result = ImageModel()

    step.finalize_result(result, [("flat", "flat.fits")])

    # As with the CRDS context report, only the top-level step should report
    # the software version; otherwise every substep would duplicate it.
    assert core_log_messages == []

import numpy as np
import pytest
from astropy import units as u
from astropy.modeling import models

from specutils.fitting import fit_lines
from specutils.spectra import Spectrum1D


class RecordingFitter:
    """Minimal fitter that records the data actually passed to the fit."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.x = None
        self.y = None

    def __call__(self, model, x, y, weights=None, **kwargs):
        self.x = x.copy()
        self.y = y.copy()
        return model


def _values(values):
    return values.value if isinstance(values, u.Quantity) else np.asarray(values)


def _issue_spectrum():
    # The step deliberately does not land on either window boundary. This makes
    # the scalar window's exclusive upper bound and the tuple window's inclusive
    # upper bound select exactly the same pixels.
    wavelength = (6500 + 0.3 * np.arange(334)) * u.AA
    x = wavelength.value

    # A strong, well-separated feature outside the desired window makes fitting
    # the whole spectrum observably different from fitting the requested window.
    flux = (
        100
        + 0.08 * (x - 6500)
        + 2000 * np.exp(-0.5 * ((x - 6563) / 3) ** 2)
        + 1400 * np.exp(-0.5 * ((x - 6520) / 4) ** 2)
    )
    flux += np.random.default_rng(12345).normal(0, 2, x.size)

    return Spectrum1D(flux=flux * u.adu, spectral_axis=wavelength)


def _issue_model():
    # This is the compound-model form used in the issue. The initial mean is
    # offset from the data peak so centering on the initial model mean, rather
    # than on the peak or fitted mean, is also checked.
    gaussian = models.Gaussian1D(
        amplitude=2000, mean=6560 * u.AA, stddev=3 * u.AA
    )
    return gaussian + models.Const1D(0)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("window", [10 * u.AA, 1 * u.nm])
def test_scalar_quantity_window_centers_on_compound_model_mean(window):
    spectrum = _issue_spectrum()
    fitter = RecordingFitter()

    fit_lines(spectrum, _issue_model(), fitter=fitter, window=window)

    x = spectrum.spectral_axis.value
    expected = (x >= 6550) & (x < 6570)
    assert 0 < expected.sum() < x.size

    np.testing.assert_array_equal(_values(fitter.x), x[expected])
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(
        _values(fitter.y), spectrum.flux.value[expected]
    )


def test_scalar_quantity_window_matches_manual_bounds_and_excludes_outlying_data():
    spectrum = _issue_spectrum()

    scalar_fit = fit_lines(
        spectrum, _issue_model(), window=10 * u.AA
    )
    manual_fit = fit_lines(
        spectrum,
        _issue_model(),
        window=(6550 * u.AA, 6570 * u.AA),
    )

    # Both forms must fit precisely the same data and therefore produce the
    # same parameters, including for the Gaussian + Const1D compound model.
    for parameter in ("amplitude", "mean", "stddev"):
        np.testing.assert_allclose(
            getattr(scalar_fit[0], parameter).value,
            getattr(manual_fit[0], parameter).value,
            rtol=1e-10,
            atol=1e-10,
        )
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        scalar_fit[1].amplitude.value,
        manual_fit[1].amplitude.value,
        rtol=1e-10,
        atol=1e-10,
    )

    # Check the scientific result as well as equality with the manual window:
    # the strong feature near 6520 AA must not pull the H-alpha fit away.
    assert abs(scalar_fit[0].mean.value - 6563) < 0.15
    assert abs(scalar_fit[0].amplitude.value - 2000) < 60

import pytest

import dns.exception
import dns.message
import dns.rdatatype
import dns.versioned
import dns.xfr
import dns.zone


FIRST_FALLBACK_MESSAGE = """id 1
opcode QUERY
rcode NOERROR
flags AA
;QUESTION
ee. IN IXFR
;ANSWER
@ 3600 IN SOA foo bar 4 2 3 4 5
@ 3600 IN NS ns1
"""

EXPECTED_ZONE = """@ 3600 IN SOA foo bar 4 2 3 4 5
@ 3600 IN NS ns1
@ 3600 IN NS ns2
ns1 3600 IN A 10.0.0.1
ns2 3600 IN A 10.0.0.2
"""


def _message(text, zone):
    return dns.message.from_text(
        text, origin=zone.origin, one_rr_per_rrset=True
    )


def _continuation_message(question="ee. IN IXFR"):
    question_section = f";QUESTION\n{question}\n" if question else ""
    return (
        """id 1
opcode QUERY
rcode NOERROR
flags AA
"""
        + question_section
        + """;ANSWER
@ 3600 IN NS ns2
ns1 3600 IN A 10.0.0.1
ns2 3600 IN A 10.0.0.2
@ 3600 IN SOA foo bar 4 2 3 4 5
"""
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("zone_factory", [dns.zone.Zone, dns.versioned.Zone])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("later_question", ["ee. IN IXFR", None])
def test_ixfr_axfr_fallback_spanning_messages(zone_factory, later_question):
    """An AXFR-style answer still has IXFR in any repeated question section."""
    zone = zone_factory("ee")

    with dns.xfr.Inbound(zone, dns.rdatatype.IXFR, serial=1) as xfr:
        # The NS after the initial SOA makes this an AXFR-style response,
        # but the transfer is not complete yet.
        assert not xfr.process_message(_message(FIRST_FALLBACK_MESSAGE, zone))

        # Servers may repeat the original IXFR question in subsequent
        # messages, or omit the question section entirely.
        message = _message(_continuation_message(later_question), zone)
        assert xfr.process_message(message)

    expected = dns.zone.from_text(EXPECTED_ZONE, "ee.")
    assert zone == expected


def test_ixfr_axfr_fallback_after_soa_only_first_message():
    """Packetization before the fallback must not affect question handling."""
    zone = dns.zone.Zone("ee")
    first = """id 1
opcode QUERY
rcode NOERROR
flags AA
;QUESTION
ee. IN IXFR
;ANSWER
@ 3600 IN SOA foo bar 4 2 3 4 5
"""
    second = """id 1
opcode QUERY
rcode NOERROR
flags AA
;QUESTION
ee. IN IXFR
;ANSWER
@ 3600 IN NS ns1
"""

    with dns.xfr.Inbound(zone, dns.rdatatype.IXFR, serial=1) as xfr:
        assert not xfr.process_message(_message(first, zone))
        assert not xfr.process_message(_message(second, zone))
        assert xfr.process_message(
            _message(_continuation_message("ee. IN IXFR"), zone)
        )

    expected = dns.zone.from_text(EXPECTED_ZONE, "ee.")
    assert zone == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "bad_question", ["ee. IN AXFR", "not-ee. IN IXFR"]
)
def test_ixfr_axfr_fallback_still_validates_later_questions(bad_question):
    """Fallback must not disable validation of subsequent question sections."""
    zone = dns.zone.Zone("ee")
    final_message = (
        """id 1
opcode QUERY
rcode NOERROR
flags AA
;QUESTION
"""
        + bad_question
        + """
;ANSWER
@ 3600 IN SOA foo bar 4 2 3 4 5
"""
    )

    with dns.xfr.Inbound(zone, dns.rdatatype.IXFR, serial=1) as xfr:
        assert not xfr.process_message(_message(FIRST_FALLBACK_MESSAGE, zone))
        with pytest.raises(dns.exception.FormError):
            xfr.process_message(_message(final_message, zone))

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


ISSUE_SQL = """
SELECT
    1730098800::DATETIME64 DATETIME,
    'test' interp
ORDER BY DATETIME
WITH FILL
FROM toDateTime64(1730098800, 3)
TO toDateTime64(1730185140, 3)
STEP toIntervalSecond(900)
INTERPOLATE (interp)
"""

ISSUE_SQL_WITH_INTERVALS = """
SELECT
    1730098800::DATETIME64 DATETIME,
    'test' interp
ORDER BY DATETIME
WITH FILL
FROM toDateTime64(1730098800, 3) - INTERVAL 7 HOUR
TO toDateTime64(1730185140, 3) - INTERVAL 7 HOUR
STEP toIntervalSecond(900)
INTERPOLATE (interp)
"""


def _with_fill_and_interpolations(statement):
    with_fill = statement.find(exp.WithFill)
    assert with_fill is not None
    return with_fill, with_fill.args.get("interpolate") or []


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [ISSUE_SQL, ISSUE_SQL_WITH_INTERVALS],
    ids=["issue-query", "issue-query-with-intervals"],
)
def test_clickhouse_with_fill_interpolate_bare_column(sql):
    """A bare INTERPOLATE column must not require an AS expression."""
    statement = parse_one(sql, read="clickhouse")

    assert isinstance(statement, exp.Select)
    with_fill, interpolations = _with_fill_and_interpolations(statement)

    assert len(interpolations) == 1
    assert interpolations[0].output_name == "interp"

    # Parsing INTERPOLATE must not discard the other WITH FILL clauses.
    assert with_fill.args.get("from") is not None
    assert with_fill.args.get("to") is not None
    assert with_fill.args.get("step") is not None

    # Round-tripping must preserve the bare item rather than inventing an
    # explicit self-alias that was not present in the input query.
    generated = statement.sql(dialect="clickhouse")
    assert generated.endswith("INTERPOLATE (interp)")

    reparsed = parse_one(generated, read="clickhouse")
    _, reparsed_interpolations = _with_fill_and_interpolations(reparsed)
    assert len(reparsed_interpolations) == 1
    assert reparsed_interpolations[0].output_name == "interp"


def test_clickhouse_interpolate_multiple_bare_columns_and_following_limit():
    sql = "SELECT a, b ORDER BY a WITH FILL INTERPOLATE (a, b) LIMIT 10"
    statement = parse_one(sql, read="clickhouse")

    _, interpolations = _with_fill_and_interpolations(statement)
    assert [item.output_name for item in interpolations] == ["a", "b"]
    assert statement.args.get("limit") is not None

    assert statement.sql(dialect="clickhouse") == sql


def test_clickhouse_interpolate_mixed_bare_and_aliased_columns():
    sql = (
        "SELECT a, b, c FROM test ORDER BY a WITH FILL "
        "INTERPOLATE (a AS a + 1, b, c AS 'default')"
    )
    statement = parse_one(sql, read="clickhouse")

    _, interpolations = _with_fill_and_interpolations(statement)
    assert len(interpolations) == 3
    assert [item.output_name for item in interpolations] == ["a", "b", "c"]

    assert isinstance(interpolations[0], exp.Alias)
    assert interpolations[0].alias == "a"
    assert interpolations[0].this.sql(dialect="clickhouse") == "a + 1"

    assert isinstance(interpolations[2], exp.Alias)
    assert interpolations[2].alias == "c"
    assert interpolations[2].this == exp.Literal.string("default")

    # Only the items that explicitly used AS should be generated as aliases.
    assert statement.sql(dialect="clickhouse") == sql


def test_clickhouse_interpolate_explicit_as_still_works():
    sql = (
        "SELECT n, inter FROM "
        "(SELECT number AS n, number AS inter FROM numbers(1)) "
        "ORDER BY n WITH FILL INTERPOLATE (inter AS inter + 1)"
    )
    statement = parse_one(sql, read="clickhouse")

    _, interpolations = _with_fill_and_interpolations(statement)
    assert len(interpolations) == 1

    interpolation = interpolations[0]
    assert isinstance(interpolation, exp.Alias)
    assert interpolation.alias == "inter"
    assert interpolation.this.sql(dialect="clickhouse") == "inter + 1"
    assert statement.sql(dialect="clickhouse") == sql


def test_clickhouse_interpolate_bare_quoted_identifier():
    sql = "SELECT `a b` ORDER BY `a b` WITH FILL INTERPOLATE (`a b`)"
    statement = parse_one(sql, read="clickhouse")

    _, interpolations = _with_fill_and_interpolations(statement)
    assert len(interpolations) == 1
    assert interpolations[0].output_name == "a b"

    # ClickHouse generation normalizes identifier quoting to double quotes,
    # but the INTERPOLATE item must remain bare.
    assert statement.sql(dialect="clickhouse") == (
        'SELECT "a b" ORDER BY "a b" WITH FILL INTERPOLATE ("a b")'
    )

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


ISSUE_SQL = """CREATE TABLE foo AS
WITH stream AS (
    SELECT * FROM bar
)
SELECT * FROM stream;"""


def _assert_has_no_stream_expression(expression):
    assert not list(expression.find_all(exp.Stream))


def test_create_table_as_with_cte_named_stream():
    expression = parse_one(ISSUE_SQL)

    assert isinstance(expression, exp.Create)
    query = expression.expression
    assert isinstance(query, exp.Select)

    with_ = query.args.get("with")
    assert isinstance(with_, exp.With)
    assert len(with_.expressions) == 1

    cte = with_.expressions[0]
    assert isinstance(cte, exp.CTE)
    assert cte.alias == "stream"
    assert isinstance(cte.this, exp.Select)

    from_table = query.args["from"].this
    assert isinstance(from_table, exp.Table)
    assert from_table.name == "stream"

    _assert_has_no_stream_expression(expression)
    assert expression.sql() == (
        "CREATE TABLE foo AS WITH stream AS (SELECT * FROM bar) "
        "SELECT * FROM stream"
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("sql", "aliases"),
    [
        (
            "WITH stream AS (SELECT * FROM bar) SELECT * FROM stream",
            ["stream"],
        ),
        (
            "WITH STREAM AS (SELECT * FROM bar) SELECT * FROM STREAM",
            ["STREAM"],
        ),
        (
            "WITH StReAm AS (SELECT * FROM bar) SELECT * FROM StReAm",
            ["StReAm"],
        ),
        (
            "WITH a AS (SELECT 1), stream AS (SELECT * FROM a) "
            "SELECT * FROM stream",
            ["a", "stream"],
        ),
        (
            "WITH stream AS (SELECT id FROM bar), "
            "b AS (SELECT * FROM stream) SELECT * FROM b",
            ["stream", "b"],
        ),
    ],
)
def test_cte_named_stream_variants(sql, aliases):
    expression = parse_one(sql)

    assert isinstance(expression, exp.Select)
    with_ = expression.args.get("with")
    assert isinstance(with_, exp.With)
    assert [cte.alias for cte in with_.expressions] == aliases
    _assert_has_no_stream_expression(expression)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [
        "SELECT * FROM stream",
        "SELECT * FROM STREAM",
        "SELECT * FROM schema.stream",
        "SELECT * FROM stream AS s",
        "SELECT stream FROM t",
        "SELECT * FROM a JOIN stream ON a.id = stream.id",
        "SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM stream) AS sub",
        "SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stream) AS cnt",
    ],
)
def test_stream_remains_an_identifier(sql):
    expression = parse_one(sql)

    assert expression.sql() == sql
    _assert_has_no_stream_expression(expression)


def test_quoted_cte_named_stream():
    sql = 'WITH "stream" AS (SELECT * FROM bar) SELECT * FROM "stream"'
    expression = parse_one(sql)

    with_ = expression.args["with"]
    assert with_.expressions[0].alias == "stream"
    assert expression.args["from"].this.name == "stream"
    assert expression.sql() == sql
    _assert_has_no_stream_expression(expression)


def test_stream_string_literal_is_unaffected():
    sql = "SELECT * FROM t WHERE col = 'stream'"
    expression = parse_one(sql)

    literal = expression.find(exp.Literal)
    assert literal is not None
    assert literal.this == "stream"
    assert literal.is_string
    assert expression.sql() == sql
    _assert_has_no_stream_expression(expression)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(

    [

        "SELECT STREAM(), col FROM t",
    ],
)
def test_stream_function_behavior_is_preserved(sql):
    expression = parse_one(sql)

    assert expression.sql() == sql
    _assert_has_no_stream_expression(expression)

import importlib
import os
import sys

import pytest

import django_cmd


def _is_cwd_entry(entry, cwd):
    """Return whether a sys.path entry resolves to the current directory."""
    if entry in ("", "."):
        return True
    return os.path.normcase(os.path.abspath(entry)) == os.path.normcase(
        os.fspath(cwd)
    )


def test_main_makes_settings_in_working_directory_importable(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Django must be able to import a local settings module from the cwd."""
    module_name = "ttg_generated_cwd_settings"
    (tmp_path / f"{module_name}.py").write_text(
        'MARKER = "loaded from the working directory"\n',
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
    monkeypatch.setenv("DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE", module_name)
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", ["django", "check"])

    # Simulate a console-script invocation: unlike `python ...`, neither the
    # script directory nor an empty/cwd entry necessarily puts the cwd on the
    # import path.
    path_without_cwd = [
        entry
        for entry in sys.path
        if entry not in ("", ".") and not _is_cwd_entry(entry, tmp_path)
    ]
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "path", path_without_cwd)

    sys.modules.pop(module_name, None)
    importlib.invalidate_caches()
    imported_modules = []
    command_lines = []

    def execute_from_command_line(argv):
        command_lines.append(argv)
        # Django imports the configured settings module while handling the
        # command, so the path must be fixed before this function is called.
        imported_modules.append(importlib.import_module(module_name))

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        django_cmd, "execute_from_command_line", execute_from_command_line
    )

    try:
        django_cmd.main()

        assert command_lines == [sys.argv]
        assert len(imported_modules) == 1
        assert imported_modules[0].MARKER == "loaded from the working directory"
        assert any(_is_cwd_entry(entry, tmp_path) for entry in sys.path)
    finally:
        sys.modules.pop(module_name, None)


def test_main_preserves_path_and_adds_cwd_only_once(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
    monkeypatch.setenv("DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE", "example.settings")
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", ["django", "check"])

    original_path = ["/existing/first", "/existing/second"]
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "path", original_path.copy())
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        django_cmd, "execute_from_command_line", lambda argv: None
    )

    django_cmd.main()
    adjusted_path = sys.path.copy()

    assert len(adjusted_path) == len(original_path) + 1
    assert all(entry in adjusted_path for entry in original_path)
    assert sum(_is_cwd_entry(entry, tmp_path) for entry in adjusted_path) == 1

    # Repeated invocation in the same process must not keep growing sys.path.
    django_cmd.main()
    assert sys.path == adjusted_path


@pytest.mark.parametrize("cwd_entry", ["", "."])
def test_main_leaves_an_existing_cwd_entry_unchanged(
    cwd_entry, monkeypatch
):
    monkeypatch.setenv("DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE", "example.settings")
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", ["django", "check"])

    original_path = [cwd_entry, "/existing/path"]
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "path", original_path.copy())
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        django_cmd, "execute_from_command_line", lambda argv: None
    )

    django_cmd.main()
    django_cmd.main()

    assert sys.path == original_path

import warnings

import h5py
import pytest
import scipp as sc
from scipp.testing import assert_identical

import scippnexus as snx


@pytest.fixture()
def nxroot():
    """Yield an NXroot containing a single NXentry named 'entry'."""
    with h5py.File('dummy.nxs', mode='w', driver='core', backing_store=False) as f:
        root = snx.Group(f, definitions=snx.base_definitions())
        root.create_class('entry', snx.NXentry)
        yield root


def _timestamps(values):
    return sc.epoch(unit='ns') + sc.array(
        dims=['time'], unit='s', values=values
    ).to(unit='ns', dtype='int64')


def _load_without_warnings(group, index=()):
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
        warnings.simplefilter('always')
        loaded = group[index]
    assert not caught, '\n'.join(str(warning.message) for warning in caught)
    return loaded


def test_nxlog_without_value_loads_time_as_data_array_without_warning(nxroot):
    time = _timestamps([4.4, 5.5, 6.6])
    log = nxroot['entry'].create_class('log', snx.NXlog)
    log['time'] = time - sc.epoch(unit='ns')

    loaded = _load_without_warnings(log)

    # With no value dataset, time takes the role of the signal. It must therefore
    # be returned as the data of the assembled log, not via the invalid-NXdata
    # fallback DataGroup.
    assert isinstance(loaded, sc.DataArray)
    assert_identical(loaded, sc.DataArray(time))


def test_nxlog_without_value_supports_positional_time_slicing(nxroot):
    time = _timestamps([4.4, 5.5, 6.6])
    log = nxroot['entry'].create_class('log', snx.NXlog)
    log['time'] = time - sc.epoch(unit='ns')

    loaded = _load_without_warnings(log, slice(1, 3))

    assert isinstance(loaded, sc.DataArray)
    assert_identical(loaded, sc.DataArray(time[1:3]))


def test_nxlog_with_value_still_uses_value_as_signal(nxroot):
    da = sc.DataArray(
        sc.array(dims=['time'], unit='K', values=[1.0, 2.0, 3.0]),
        coords={'time': _timestamps([4.4, 5.5, 6.6])},
    )
    log = nxroot['entry'].create_class('log', snx.NXlog)
    log['value'] = da.data
    log['time'] = da.coords['time'] - sc.epoch(unit='ns')

    loaded = _load_without_warnings(log)

    assert_identical(loaded, da)


def test_time_only_nxlog_does_not_drop_sublogs(nxroot):
    time = _timestamps([4.4, 5.5, 6.6])
    alarm = sc.DataArray(
        sc.array(dims=['time'], values=[0, 1], dtype='int64'),
        coords={'time': _timestamps([4.5, 6.5])},
    )
    log = nxroot['entry'].create_class('log', snx.NXlog)
    log['time'] = time - sc.epoch(unit='ns')
    log['alarm_severity'] = alarm.data
    log['alarm_time'] = alarm.coords['time'] - sc.epoch(unit='ns')

    loaded = _load_without_warnings(log)

    assert isinstance(loaded, sc.DataGroup)
    assert set(loaded) == {'value', 'alarm'}
    assert_identical(loaded['value'], sc.DataArray(time))
    assert_identical(loaded['alarm'], alarm)

import re

import pytest

from sqlglot import parse_one


ISSUE_SQL = r"""SELECT id, struct_pack(*COLUMNS('m\d')) AS measurements
FROM many_measurements"""
ISSUE_DUCKDB_SQL = (
    r"SELECT id, STRUCT_PACK(*COLUMNS('m\d')) AS measurements FROM many_measurements"
)


def _generate_duckdb(sql: str) -> str:
    return parse_one(sql, dialect="duckdb").sql(dialect="duckdb")


def _assert_stable_roundtrip(sql: str, expected: str) -> None:
    expression = parse_one(sql, dialect="duckdb")
    generated = expression.sql(dialect="duckdb")

    assert generated == expected
    assert _generate_duckdb(generated) == expected


def test_duckdb_unpack_issue_example():
    # The example must not only parse, but also remain valid DuckDB when generated.
    # Unpacking cannot be turned into an ordinary struct field such as
    # {'_0': *COLUMNS(...)}; STRUCT_PACK is what accepts the unpacked arguments.
    _assert_stable_roundtrip(ISSUE_SQL, ISSUE_DUCKDB_SQL)


def test_duckdb_unpack_multiple_column_groups():
    _assert_stable_roundtrip(
        r"SELECT STRUCT_PACK(*COLUMNS('m\d'), *COLUMNS('n\d')) AS measurements "
        "FROM many_measurements",
        r"SELECT STRUCT_PACK(*COLUMNS('m\d'), *COLUMNS('n\d')) AS measurements "
        "FROM many_measurements",
    )


def test_duckdb_unpack_mixed_with_named_struct_pack_arguments():
    generated = _generate_duckdb(
        r"SELECT STRUCT_PACK(a := 1, *COLUMNS('m\d'), b := 2) AS packed "
        "FROM many_measurements"
    )

    # All arguments must be retained as arguments of STRUCT_PACK. Accept either
    # identifier or string-literal rendering of the field names.
    assert generated.startswith("SELECT STRUCT_PACK(")
    assert generated.endswith(" AS packed FROM many_measurements")
    assert r"*COLUMNS('m\d')" in generated
    assert re.search(r"[\"']?a[\"']?\s*:=\s*1\b", generated)
    assert re.search(r"[\"']?b[\"']?\s*:=\s*2\b", generated)
    assert "_0" not in generated
    assert "_2" not in generated

    # Generated SQL must itself be parseable and stable.
    assert _generate_duckdb(generated) == generated


def test_duckdb_unpack_in_select_list():
    _assert_stable_roundtrip(
        r"SELECT *COLUMNS('m\d') FROM many_measurements",
        r"SELECT *COLUMNS('m\d') FROM many_measurements",
    )


def test_duckdb_unpack_is_case_insensitive_and_allows_whitespace():
    _assert_stable_roundtrip(
        r"SELECT struct_pack(* columns('m\d')) FROM many_measurements",
        r"SELECT STRUCT_PACK(*COLUMNS('m\d')) FROM many_measurements",
    )


def test_duckdb_regular_struct_pack_generation_is_unchanged():
    # STRUCT_PACK without unpacked arguments has existing canonical DuckDB output.
    assert (
        _generate_duckdb("SELECT STRUCT_PACK(a := 1, b := 2)")
        == "SELECT {'a': 1, 'b': 2}"
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [
        "SELECT * FROM t",
        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t",
        "SELECT a * b FROM t",
        "SELECT a * b, * FROM t",
    ],
)
def test_duckdb_existing_star_syntax_is_unchanged(sql):
    assert _generate_duckdb(sql) == sql

from dataclasses import dataclass, field, fields
from typing import Any

from xsdata.formats.dataclass.filters import Filters
from xsdata.models.config import GeneratorConfig
from xsdata.models.enums import DataType
from xsdata.utils.testing import AttrFactory, ClassFactory


def _build_generated_model(definitions):
    """Create a dataclass using field definitions emitted by xsdata."""
    source = ["@dataclass", "class GeneratedModel:"]
    for name, definition in definitions:
        source.append(f"    {name}: Any = {definition}")

    namespace = {
        "__name__": __name__,
        "Any": Any,
        "dataclass": dataclass,
        "field": field,
    }
    exec("\n".join(source), namespace)
    return namespace["GeneratedModel"]


def _model_with_ignored_fields():
    filters = Filters(GeneratorConfig())
    obj = ClassFactory.create(qname="a")
    definitions = []

    # Cover prohibited attributes both with and without a schema default. In
    # either case no runtime default is generated, so the instance attributes
    # remain unset.
    for name, default in (("first_ignored", "1"), ("second_ignored", None)):
        attr = AttrFactory.native(DataType.INT)
        attr.restrictions.max_occurs = 0
        attr.default = default
        definitions.append(
            (name, filters.field_definition(obj, attr, None))
        )

    visible = AttrFactory.native(DataType.STRING)
    visible.default = "visible"
    definitions.append(
        ("visible", filters.field_definition(obj, visible, None))
    )

    return _build_generated_model(definitions)


def test_generated_ignore_fields_do_not_break_repr():
    model = _model_with_ignored_fields()

    ignored_fields = fields(model)[:2]
    assert [item.name for item in ignored_fields] == [
        "first_ignored",
        "second_ignored",
    ]
    for item in ignored_fields:
        # Making repr safe must not turn an ignored field back into a binding
        # field or make it a constructor argument.
        assert item.init is False
        assert item.metadata["type"] == "Ignore"

    instance = model()
    representation = repr(instance)

    assert representation.startswith("GeneratedModel(")
    assert "visible='visible'" in representation
    # print() uses the same generated representation and must be safe too.
    assert "visible='visible'" in str(instance)


def test_generated_ignore_fields_do_not_break_container_repr():
    model = _model_with_ignored_fields()

    @dataclass
    class Container:
        item: Any

    representation = repr(Container(item=model()))

    assert "item=GeneratedModel(" in representation
    assert "visible='visible'" in representation


def test_initialized_init_false_fields_remain_in_repr():
    filters = Filters(GeneratorConfig())
    obj = ClassFactory.create(qname="a")

    # Fixed fields also use init=False, but unlike ignored fields they have a
    # default and are safe and useful to include in the representation.
    attr = AttrFactory.native(DataType.INT)
    attr.fixed = True
    attr.default = "1"
    definition = filters.field_definition(obj, attr, None)
    model = _build_generated_model([("value", definition)])

    assert fields(model)[0].init is False
    assert "value=1" in repr(model())

import re
from unittest.mock import Mock

import pytest

from streamlink.exceptions import PluginError
from streamlink.plugin.api import useragents
from streamlink.plugins.kick import Kick
from streamlink.session import Streamlink
from streamlink.stream.hls import HLSStream


LIVE_URL = "https://kick.com/zmok"
LIVE_API_URL = "https://kick.com/api/v2/channels/zmok/livestream"
VOD_ID = "4acba712-a1cd-45b0-8ce0-4b534d4c271f"
VOD_URL = f"https://kick.com/kukudota2/videos/{VOD_ID}"
VOD_API_URL = f"https://kick.com/api/v1/video/{VOD_ID}"


@pytest.fixture()
def kick_session():
    return Streamlink()


def _expected_api_headers():
    match = re.search(r"Chrome/(?P<full>(?P<main>\d+)\S+)", useragents.CHROME)
    assert match is not None

    return {
        "Accept": "application/json",
        "Accept-Language": "en-US",
        "User-Agent": useragents.CHROME,
        "sec-ch-ua": f'"Not:A-Brand";v="24", "Chromium";v="{match["main"]}"',
        "sec-ch-ua-arch": '"x86"',
        "sec-ch-ua-bitness": '"64"',
        "sec-ch-ua-full-version": f'"{match["full"]}"',
        "sec-ch-ua-full-version-list": (
            f'"Not:A-Brand";v="24.0.0.0", "Chromium";v="{match["full"]}"'
        ),
        "sec-ch-ua-mobile": "?0",
        "sec-ch-ua-model": '""',
        "sec-ch-ua-platform": '"Windows"',
        "sec-ch-ua-platform-version": '"6.14.0"',
        "sec-fetch-dest": "empty",
        "sec-fetch-mode": "cors",
        "sec-fetch-site": "same-origin",
        "sec-fetch-user": "?1",
    }


def _has_accepted_headers(request, referer):
    return (
        all(request.headers.get(name) == value for name, value in _expected_api_headers().items())
        and request.headers.get("Referer") == referer
        and request.headers.get("Authorization") is None
    )


def _mock_secured_api(requests_mock, api_url, referer, payload, status_code=200):
    """Simulate an API which rejects the old token-based/non-browser requests."""
    # The old implementation requests this page to obtain an XSRF token. A fixed
    # implementation must not need this preliminary request.
    requests_mock.get("https://kick.com/", text="")

    def respond(request, context):
        context.headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
        if not _has_accepted_headers(request, referer):
            context.status_code = 403
            return json.dumps({"error": "Request blocked by security policy."})

        context.status_code = status_code
        return json.dumps(payload)

    requests_mock.get(api_url, text=respond)


def _assert_single_browser_api_request(requests_mock, api_url, referer):
    history = requests_mock.request_history
    assert [request.url for request in history] == [api_url]

    request = history[0]
    for name, value in _expected_api_headers().items():
        assert request.headers.get(name) == value
    assert request.headers.get("Referer") == referer
    assert request.headers.get("Authorization") is None


def _mock_variant_playlist(monkeypatch, session, stream_name, hls_url):
    stream = HLSStream(session, hls_url)
    parser = Mock(return_value={stream_name: stream})
    monkeypatch.setattr("streamlink.plugins.kick.HLSStream.parse_variant_playlist", parser)
    return parser, stream

    kick_session,
    requests_mock,
    monkeypatch,
):
    hls_url = "https://example.com/live/playlist.m3u8"
    _mock_secured_api(
        requests_mock,
        LIVE_API_URL,
        LIVE_URL,
        {
            "data": {
                "playback_url": hls_url,
                "id": 123456,
                "category": {"name": "Just Chatting"},
                "session_title": "Live stream title",
            },
        },
    )
    parser, stream = _mock_variant_playlist(monkeypatch, kick_session, "live", hls_url)
    plugin = Kick(kick_session, LIVE_URL)

    streams = plugin.streams()

    assert streams["live"] is stream
    parser.assert_called_once_with(kick_session, hls_url)
    assert plugin.id == 123456
    assert plugin.author == "zmok"
    assert plugin.category == "Just Chatting"
    assert plugin.title == "Live stream title"
    _assert_single_browser_api_request(requests_mock, LIVE_API_URL, LIVE_URL)


def test_issue_vod_url_uses_browser_api_request_without_token(

    _mock_secured_api(

        VOD_API_URL,
        VOD_URL,
        {
            "source": hls_url,
            "livestream": {

                "channel": {"user": {"username": "kukudota2"}},
            },
        },
    )
    parser, stream = _mock_variant_playlist(monkeypatch, kick_session, "vod", hls_url)

    assert plugin.author == "kukudota2"
    assert plugin.title == "VOD title"
    _assert_single_browser_api_request(requests_mock, VOD_API_URL, VOD_URL)


def test_clip_api_uses_same_browser_request(kick_session, requests_mock):
    url = "https://kick.com/CLIP_CHANNEL?clip=CLIP_ID"

    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="clickhouse")

import pytest

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


def _assert_single_stream_cte(select: exp.Select, expected_name: str = "stream") -> None:
    """Check both the CTE definition and its reference in the outer query."""
    assert isinstance(select, exp.Select)

    with_clause = select.args.get("with")
    assert isinstance(with_clause, exp.With)
    assert len(with_clause.expressions) == 1

    cte = with_clause.expressions[0]
    assert isinstance(cte, exp.CTE)
    assert cte.alias_or_name.lower() == expected_name.lower()
    assert isinstance(cte.this, exp.Select)

    from_clause = select.args.get("from")
    assert isinstance(from_clause, exp.From)
    assert isinstance(from_clause.this, exp.Table)
    assert from_clause.this.name.lower() == expected_name.lower()

    # The CTE name must remain an identifier, not become a STREAM expression.
    assert select.find(exp.Stream) is None


def test_create_table_as_with_cte_named_stream() -> None:
    create = sqlglot.parse_one(
        """
        CREATE TABLE foo AS
        WITH stream AS (
            SELECT * FROM bar
        )
        SELECT * FROM stream;
        """
    )

    assert isinstance(create, exp.Create)
    assert create.kind == "TABLE"
    assert isinstance(create.this, exp.Table)
    assert create.this.name == "foo"
    _assert_single_stream_cte(create.expression)

    # The complete statement, including the CTE, must survive generation and
    # reparsing rather than merely avoiding the original exception.
    generated = create.sql()
    assert generated == (
        "CREATE TABLE foo AS WITH stream AS "
        "(SELECT * FROM bar) SELECT * FROM stream"
    )
    assert sqlglot.parse_one(generated).sql() == generated


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("cte_name", "column_list"),
    [
        ("stream", ""),
        ("STREAM", ""),
        ("Stream", "(id)"),
    ],
)
def test_plain_query_with_cte_named_stream(cte_name: str, column_list: str) -> None:
    select = sqlglot.parse_one(
        f"WITH {cte_name}{column_list} AS (SELECT 1 AS id) "
        f"SELECT id FROM {cte_name}"
    )

    _assert_single_stream_cte(select, cte_name)
    assert sqlglot.parse_one(select.sql()).sql() == select.sql()


def test_stream_cte_can_appear_between_other_ctes() -> None:
    select = sqlglot.parse_one(
        """
        WITH seed AS (SELECT 1 AS id),
             stream AS (SELECT id FROM seed),
             final_cte AS (SELECT id FROM stream)
        SELECT id FROM final_cte
        """
    )

    assert isinstance(select, exp.Select)
    with_clause = select.args.get("with")
    assert isinstance(with_clause, exp.With)
    assert [cte.alias_or_name for cte in with_clause.expressions] == [
        "seed",
        "stream",
        "final_cte",
    ]
    assert select.find(exp.Stream) is None
    assert sqlglot.parse_one(select.sql()).sql() == select.sql()


def test_stream_cte_inside_nested_query() -> None:
    outer = sqlglot.parse_one(
        """
        SELECT * FROM (
            WITH stream AS (SELECT 1 AS id)
            SELECT id FROM stream
        ) AS s
        """
    )

    with_clause = outer.find(exp.With)
    assert isinstance(with_clause, exp.With)
    _assert_single_stream_cte(with_clause.parent)
    assert outer.find(exp.Stream) is None
    assert sqlglot.parse_one(outer.sql()).sql() == outer.sql()


def test_create_view_with_cte_named_stream() -> None:
    create = sqlglot.parse_one(
        """
        CREATE VIEW stream_view AS
        WITH stream AS (SELECT 1 AS id)
        SELECT id FROM stream
        """
    )

    assert isinstance(create, exp.Create)
    assert create.kind == "VIEW"
    _assert_single_stream_cte(create.expression)
    assert sqlglot.parse_one(create.sql()).sql() == create.sql()

import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import Mock

import pytest

from django_cmd import main


def _entry_is_current_directory(entry, cwd):
    """Return whether a sys.path entry makes cwd importable."""
    if entry in ("", "."):
        return True
    try:
        return Path(entry).resolve() == cwd.resolve()
    except (OSError, TypeError, ValueError):
        return False


def test_main_adds_current_directory_before_running_django(
    monkeypatch, tmp_path
):
    """Local project modules must be importable by the Django command."""
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
    monkeypatch.setenv("DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE", "example.settings")

    existing_path = [str(tmp_path.parent), "an-existing-relative-entry"]
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "path", existing_path.copy())
    path_seen_by_django = []

    def record_path(argv):
        path_seen_by_django.append(sys.path.copy())

    command = Mock(side_effect=record_path)
    monkeypatch.setattr("django_cmd.execute_from_command_line", command)

    main()

    assert command.call_count == 1
    assert len(path_seen_by_django) == 1
    assert any(
        _entry_is_current_directory(entry, tmp_path)
        for entry in path_seen_by_django[0]
    )
    # Adding the project directory must not discard the existing import path.
    assert all(entry in path_seen_by_django[0] for entry in existing_path)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("cwd_entry", ["", "."])
def test_main_does_not_duplicate_an_existing_current_directory_entry(
    monkeypatch, tmp_path, cwd_entry
):
    """An already importable current directory should be left alone."""
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
    monkeypatch.setenv("DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE", "example.settings")
    original_path = [cwd_entry, str(tmp_path / "elsewhere")]
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "path", original_path.copy())
    command = Mock()
    monkeypatch.setattr("django_cmd.execute_from_command_line", command)

    main()

    assert command.called
    assert sys.path == original_path


def test_django_command_loads_settings_from_current_directory(tmp_path):
    """Exercise the installed command without PYTHONPATH supplying the cwd."""
    project = tmp_path / "localproject"
    project.mkdir()
    (project / "__init__.py").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
    (project / "settings.py").write_text(
        'SECRET_KEY = "django-cmd-test"\n'
        "INSTALLED_APPS = []\n"
        "DATABASES = {}\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    (tmp_path / "pyproject.toml").write_text(
        '[tool.django]\nsettings_module = "localproject.settings"\n',
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    env = os.environ.copy()
    env.pop("PYTHONPATH", None)
    env.pop("DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE", None)

    result = subprocess.run(
        ["django", "check", "--verbosity", "0"],
        cwd=tmp_path,
        env=env,
        text=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        timeout=30,
    )

    assert result.returncode == 0, (
        "The django command could not import a settings module from its "
        "working directory.\n"
        f"stdout:\n{result.stdout}\n"
        f"stderr:\n{result.stderr}"
    )

import logging

import pytest
from stdatamodels.jwst import datamodels

from jwst import __version__
from jwst.stpipe import core


CRDS_CONTEXT = "jwst_1234.pmap"


class _RecordCollector(logging.Handler):
    """Collect records directly from the stpipe logger.

    The logger does not necessarily propagate to the root logger used by
    pytest's caplog fixture, so attach a handler directly to it.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(level=logging.INFO)
        self.records = []

    def emit(self, record):
        self.records.append(record)


@pytest.fixture
def core_log_records():
    handler = _RecordCollector()
    previous_level = core.log.level
    previous_disabled = core.log.disabled

    core.log.addHandler(handler)
    core.log.setLevel(logging.INFO)
    core.log.disabled = False

    try:
        yield handler.records
    finally:
        core.log.removeHandler(handler)
        core.log.setLevel(previous_level)
        core.log.disabled = previous_disabled
        handler.close()


def _stub_crds(monkeypatch):
    """Prevent CRDS access and provide deterministic finalization values."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(core.crds_client, "get_svn_version", lambda: "1.2.3")
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        core.crds_client, "get_context_used", lambda observatory: CRDS_CONTEXT
    )


def _assert_version_follows_crds_context(records):
    """The version report should be the final message, next to the CRDS report."""
    assert len(records) >= 2
    crds_record, version_record = records[-2:]

    assert crds_record.getMessage() == (
        f"Results used CRDS context: {CRDS_CONTEXT}"
    )
    assert version_record.getMessage() == (
        f"Results used jwst version: {__version__}"
    )
    assert crds_record.levelno == logging.INFO
    assert version_record.levelno == logging.INFO


def test_step_reports_jwst_version_after_crds_context(
    monkeypatch, core_log_records
):
    _stub_crds(monkeypatch)

    step = core.JwstStep()
    result = datamodels.ImageModel()
    step.finalize_result(result, [("flat", "flat.fits")])

    _assert_version_follows_crds_context(core_log_records)


def test_pipeline_reports_jwst_version_after_crds_context(
    monkeypatch, core_log_records
):
    _stub_crds(monkeypatch)

    pipeline = core.JwstPipeline()
    pipeline.finalize_result(datamodels.ImageModel(), [])

    _assert_version_follows_crds_context(core_log_records)


def test_nested_step_does_not_duplicate_final_version_report(
    monkeypatch, core_log_records
):
    """Only the top-level step should emit the final CRDS/version report."""
    _stub_crds(monkeypatch)

    parent = core.JwstStep()
    child = core.JwstStep(parent=parent)
    child.finalize_result(

import dns.exception
import dns.message
import dns.name
import dns.rdatatype
import dns.xfr
import dns.zone
import pytest


BASE_ZONE_TEXT = """@ 3600 IN SOA foo bar 1 2 3 4 5
@ 3600 IN NS old-ns
old-ns 3600 IN A 192.0.2.1
@ 3600 IN TXT "old"
"""

SOA_SERIAL_4 = "@ 3600 IN SOA foo bar 4 2 3 4 5"

FIRST_FALLBACK_RECORDS = """@ 3600 IN NS ns1
ns1 3600 IN A 192.0.2.10
"""

SECOND_FALLBACK_RECORDS = """@ 3600 IN MX 10 mail
mail 3600 IN A 192.0.2.20
"""


def make_zone():
    return dns.zone.from_text(BASE_ZONE_TEXT, "example.")


def make_response(zone, answer, question="example. IN IXFR"):
    text = f"""id 1
opcode QUERY
rcode NOERROR
flags AA
;QUESTION
{question}
;ANSWER
{answer}
"""
    return dns.message.from_text(
        text, origin=zone.origin, one_rr_per_rrset=True
    )


def start_multimessage_fallback(zone):
    """Start an IXFR whose server switches to AXFR-style response data.

    The initial SOA is in a message by itself. The next message starts with
    ordinary zone data rather than the SOA that would start an IXFR deletion
    set, so the receiver must fall back to AXFR processing.
    """
    inbound = dns.xfr.Inbound(zone, dns.rdatatype.IXFR, serial=1)
    assert inbound.process_message(make_response(zone, SOA_SERIAL_4)) is False
    assert (
        inbound.process_message(make_response(zone, FIRST_FALLBACK_RECORDS))
        is False
    )
    return inbound


def assert_fallback_zone_contents(zone):
    soa = zone.get_rdataset("@", dns.rdatatype.SOA)
    assert soa is not None
    assert soa[0].serial == 4

    # The zone and messages use dnspython's default relativization, so names
    # within rdata are stored relative to the zone origin.
    ns = zone.get_rdataset("@", dns.rdatatype.NS)
    assert ns is not None
    assert len(ns) == 1
    assert ns[0].target == dns.name.from_text("ns1")

    mx = zone.get_rdataset("@", dns.rdatatype.MX)
    assert mx is not None
    assert len(mx) == 1
    assert mx[0].preference == 10
    assert mx[0].exchange == dns.name.from_text("mail")

    address = zone.get_rdataset("mail", dns.rdatatype.A)
    assert address is not None
    assert address.to_text() == "3600 IN A 192.0.2.20"

    # Falling back to AXFR replaces the zone; it must not leave data from the
    # old version or partially applied IXFR changes behind.
    assert zone.get_rdataset("@", dns.rdatatype.TXT) is None
    assert zone.find_node("old-ns") is None


def test_ixfr_fallback_accepts_ixfr_question_in_later_messages():
    """An AXFR-style IXFR response may span several DNS messages.

    Servers can continue to echo the original IXFR question after dnspython
    has internally switched to AXFR mode. The transfer must complete rather
    than failing with "wrong question rdatatype".
    """
    zone = make_zone()

    with start_multimessage_fallback(zone) as inbound:
        final_answer = SECOND_FALLBACK_RECORDS + SOA_SERIAL_4
        done = inbound.process_message(make_response(zone, final_answer))

    assert done is True
    assert_fallback_zone_contents(zone)


def test_single_message_ixfr_axfr_style_response_still_completes():
    """The fallback also works when the whole response is in one message."""
    zone = make_zone()
    answer = (
        SOA_SERIAL_4
        + "\n"
        + FIRST_FALLBACK_RECORDS
        + SECOND_FALLBACK_RECORDS
        + SOA_SERIAL_4
    )

    with dns.xfr.Inbound(zone, dns.rdatatype.IXFR, serial=1) as inbound:
        done = inbound.process_message(make_response(zone, answer))

    assert done is True
    assert_fallback_zone_contents(zone)


def test_regular_ixfr_still_applies_incremental_changes():
    """Relaxing fallback question handling must not alter normal IXFRs."""
    zone = make_zone()
    answer = """@ 3600 IN SOA foo bar 1 2 3 4 5
@ 3600 IN TXT "old"
@ 3600 IN SOA foo bar 2 2 3 4 5
@ 3600 IN TXT "new"
@ 3600 IN SOA foo bar 2 2 3 4 5
"""

    with dns.xfr.Inbound(zone, dns.rdatatype.IXFR, serial=1) as inbound:
        first_soa = "@ 3600 IN SOA foo bar 2 2 3 4 5"
        assert inbound.process_message(make_response(zone, first_soa)) is False
        done = inbound.process_message(make_response(zone, answer))

    assert done is True
    soa = zone.get_rdataset("@", dns.rdatatype.SOA)
    assert soa is not None
    assert soa[0].serial == 2

    txt = zone.get_rdataset("@", dns.rdatatype.TXT)
    assert txt is not None
    assert txt.to_text() == '3600 IN TXT "new"'

    # This was an incremental update, not an AXFR replacement.
    assert zone.get_rdataset("@", dns.rdatatype.NS) is not None


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("question", "error"),
    [
        ("other.example. IN IXFR", "wrong question name"),
        ("example. IN A", "wrong question rdatatype"),
    ],
)
def test_fallback_does_not_disable_question_validation(question, error):
    zone = make_zone()

    with start_multimessage_fallback(zone) as inbound:
        message = make_response(zone, SOA_SERIAL_4, question=question)
        with pytest.raises(dns.exception.FormError, match=error):
            inbound.process_message(message)


def test_plain_axfr_still_rejects_an_ixfr_question():
    """The exception is specific to fallback from a requested IXFR."""
    zone = make_zone()
    answer = """@ 3600 IN SOA foo bar 1 2 3 4 5
@ 3600 IN NS ns1
@ 3600 IN SOA foo bar 1 2 3 4 5
"""
    message = make_response(zone, answer)

    with dns.xfr.Inbound(zone, dns.rdatatype.AXFR) as inbound:
        with pytest.raises(
            dns.exception.FormError, match="wrong question rdatatype"
        ):
            inbound.process_message(message)

import numpy as np
import pytest
from astropy import units as u
from astropy.modeling import models

from specutils.fitting import fit_lines
from specutils.spectra import Spectrum1D


def _spectrum(continuum=100.0):
    """A target line plus a strong feature well outside the fitting window."""
    wavelength = np.linspace(6500.0, 6600.0, 400) * u.AA
    x = wavelength.value

    target = 2000.0 * np.exp(-0.5 * ((x - 6563.0) / 3.0) ** 2)
    contaminant = 4000.0 * np.exp(-0.5 * ((x - 6515.0) / 5.0) ** 2)
    flux = continuum + target + contaminant

    return Spectrum1D(flux=flux * u.adu, spectral_axis=wavelength)


def _compound_guess():
    # This is the model construction used in the issue: a Gaussian plus a
    # constant, rather than a bare Gaussian.
    guess = models.Gaussian1D(
        amplitude=2000, mean=6563 * u.AA, stddev=3 * u.AA
    )
    return guess + models.Const1D(0)


def _parameter_value(parameter, unit):
    quantity = getattr(parameter, "quantity", None)
    if quantity is not None:
        return quantity.to_value(unit)
    return getattr(parameter, "value", parameter)


def test_scalar_quantity_window_matches_manual_bounds_for_compound_model():
    """A scalar window is the half-width centered on the Gaussian's mean."""
    automatic = fit_lines(
        _spectrum(), _compound_guess(), window=10 * u.AA
    )
    manual = fit_lines(
        _spectrum(),
        _compound_guess(),
        window=(6553 * u.AA, 6573 * u.AA),
    )

    # Both calls must fit exactly the same samples. In particular, the scalar
    # Quantity must not be silently ignored in favor of the whole spectrum.
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        automatic.parameters, manual.parameters, rtol=1e-8, atol=1e-8
    )

    gaussian = automatic[0]
    constant = automatic[1]
    assert _parameter_value(gaussian.mean, u.AA) == pytest.approx(
        6563.0, abs=1e-3
    )
    assert _parameter_value(gaussian.amplitude, u.adu) == pytest.approx(
        2000.0, rel=1e-5
    )
    assert _parameter_value(gaussian.stddev, u.AA) == pytest.approx(
        3.0, abs=1e-3
    )
    assert _parameter_value(constant.amplitude, u.adu) == pytest.approx(
        100.0, abs=1e-2
    )


def test_scalar_window_preserves_quantity_units():
    """Window and model units must be converted, not compared as raw values."""
    guess = models.Gaussian1D(
        amplitude=2000 * u.adu,
        mean=656.3 * u.nm,  # 6563 Angstrom
        stddev=0.3 * u.nm,
    )

    automatic = fit_lines(
        _spectrum(continuum=0.0), guess, window=1 * u.nm
    )
    manual = fit_lines(
        _spectrum(continuum=0.0),
        models.Gaussian1D(
            amplitude=2000 * u.adu,
            mean=656.3 * u.nm,
            stddev=0.3 * u.nm,
        ),
        window=(6553 * u.AA, 6573 * u.AA),
    )

    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        automatic.parameters, manual.parameters, rtol=1e-8, atol=1e-8
    )
    assert _parameter_value(automatic.mean, u.AA) == pytest.approx(
        6563.0, abs=1e-3
    )
    assert _parameter_value(automatic.amplitude, u.adu) == pytest.approx(
        2000.0, rel=1e-5
    )
    assert _parameter_value(automatic.stddev, u.AA) == pytest.approx(
        3.0, abs=1e-3
    )


def test_empty_scalar_quantity_window_does_not_fall_back_to_full_spectrum():
    """An ignored scalar window would fit successfully instead of reporting
    that the requested window contains no spectral samples.
    """
    guess = models.Gaussian1D(
        amplitude=2000 * u.adu, mean=6563 * u.AA, stddev=3 * u.AA
    )

    with pytest.raises(Exception, match="Spectrum flux is empty or None"):
        fit_lines(_spectrum(), guess, window=1e-6 * u.AA)

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


ISSUE_QUERIES = [
    """
    SELECT
        1730098800::DATETIME64 DATETIME,
        'test' interp
    ORDER BY DATETIME
    WITH FILL
    FROM toDateTime64(1730098800, 3)
    TO toDateTime64(1730185140, 3)
    STEP toIntervalSecond(900)
    INTERPOLATE (interp)
    """,
    """
    SELECT
        1730098800::DATETIME64 DATETIME,
        'test' interp
    ORDER BY DATETIME
    WITH FILL
    FROM toDateTime64(1730098800, 3) - INTERVAL 7 HOUR
    TO toDateTime64(1730185140, 3) - INTERVAL 7 HOUR
    STEP toIntervalSecond(900)
    INTERPOLATE (interp)
    """,
]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("sql", ISSUE_QUERIES, ids=["without_intervals", "with_intervals"])
def test_issue_with_fill_interpolate_column(sql):
    expression = parse_one(sql, read="clickhouse")

    with_fill = expression.find(exp.WithFill)
    assert with_fill is not None
    assert with_fill.args.get("from") is not None
    assert with_fill.args.get("to") is not None
    assert with_fill.args.get("step") is not None

    interpolate = with_fill.args.get("interpolate")
    assert interpolate is not None
    assert len(interpolate) == 1
    assert interpolate[0].name == "interp"

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="clickhouse")
    assert "WITH FILL" in generated
    assert "FROM toDateTime64" in generated
    assert "TO toDateTime64" in generated
    assert "STEP toIntervalSecond(900)" in generated
    assert generated.endswith("INTERPOLATE (interp)")

    # The generated query must itself be valid ClickHouse input and stable.
    reparsed = parse_one(generated, read="clickhouse")
    assert reparsed.sql(dialect="clickhouse") == generated


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [
        "SELECT col1, col2 AS interp_col ORDER BY col1 WITH FILL INTERPOLATE (interp_col)",
        "SELECT col1, col2, col3 ORDER BY col1 WITH FILL INTERPOLATE (col2, col3)",
        "SELECT col1, col2, col3 ORDER BY col1 WITH FILL INTERPOLATE (col2, col3 AS col3 * 2)",
        'SELECT "col1", "col2" ORDER BY "col1" WITH FILL INTERPOLATE ("col2")',
        "SELECT dt, value1, value2 ORDER BY dt WITH FILL STEP 1 "
        "INTERPOLATE (value1 AS value1 + 1, value2 AS COALESCE(value2, 0))",
        "SELECT n, source, inter FROM (SELECT toFloat32(number % 10) AS n, "
        "'original' AS source, number AS inter FROM numbers(10) WHERE number % 3 = 1) "
        "ORDER BY n WITH FILL FROM 0 TO 5.51 STEP 0.5 INTERPOLATE (inter AS inter + 1)",
    ],
    ids=[
        "single_column",
        "multiple_columns",
        "mixed_column_and_expression",
        "quoted_identifier",
        "multiple_expressions",
        "existing_aliased_form",
    ],
)
def test_interpolate_identity_and_roundtrip(sql):
    expression = parse_one(sql, read="clickhouse")
    generated = expression.sql(dialect="clickhouse")

    assert generated == sql
    assert parse_one(generated, read="clickhouse").sql(dialect="clickhouse") == sql


def test_aliased_interpolate_preserves_target_and_expression():
    sql = (
        "SELECT n, inter FROM numbers(10) ORDER BY n WITH FILL "
        "INTERPOLATE (inter AS inter + 1)"
    )
    expression = parse_one(sql, read="clickhouse")
    with_fill = expression.find(exp.WithFill)

    assert with_fill is not None
    interpolate = with_fill.args.get("interpolate")
    assert interpolate is not None
    assert len(interpolate) == 1

    interpolated = interpolate[0]
    assert isinstance(interpolated, exp.Alias)
    assert interpolated.alias == "inter"
    assert interpolated.this.sql(dialect="clickhouse") == "inter + 1"
    assert expression.sql(dialect="clickhouse") == sql

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest
import tomlkit

from pdm.project.core import Project


def _configure_groups(
    project: Project,
    *,
    legacy_groups: dict[str, list[str]],
    dependency_groups: dict[str, list[str]] | None = None,
    optional_dependencies: dict[str, list[str]] | None = None,
) -> None:
    project.pyproject.settings["dev-dependencies"] = legacy_groups
    if dependency_groups is not None:
        project.pyproject._data["dependency-groups"] = dependency_groups
    if optional_dependencies is not None:
        project.pyproject.metadata["optional-dependencies"] = optional_dependencies
    project.pyproject.write()


def _read_pyproject(project: Project) -> dict:
    path = project.root / project.PYPROJECT_FILENAME
    return tomlkit.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).unwrap()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("target_group", ["dev", "lint"])
def test_add_dev_dependency_uses_requested_group_without_copying_legacy_groups(
    project: Project, target_group: str
) -> None:
    """Both the default dev group and an explicit -G group must keep their names."""
    legacy_groups = {
        "docs": ["-e ./packages/pkg-core"],
        # Keep this last so the old loop-variable shadowing reliably selects it.
        "workspaces": [
            "-e ./packages/pkg-app",
            "-e ./packages/pkg-core",
        ],
    }
    existing_groups = {"test": ["pytest>=8"]}
    _configure_groups(
        project,
        legacy_groups=legacy_groups,
        dependency_groups=existing_groups,
    )

    project.add_dependencies(["ruff"], target_group, dev=True)

    data = _read_pyproject(project)
    assert data["dependency-groups"] == {
        "test": ["pytest>=8"],
        target_group: ["ruff"],
    }
    assert data["tool"]["pdm"]["dev-dependencies"] == legacy_groups


def test_add_to_legacy_group_does_not_copy_editables_into_dependency_groups(
    project: Project,
) -> None:
    """A legacy group containing editables must not be migrated as a side effect."""
    editables = ["-e ./packages/pkg-app"]
    legacy_groups = {
        "lint": editables,
        "workspaces": ["-e ./packages/pkg-core"],
    }
    _configure_groups(project, legacy_groups=legacy_groups)

    project.add_dependencies(["ruff"], "lint", dev=True)

    data = _read_pyproject(project)
    legacy_after = data["tool"]["pdm"]["dev-dependencies"]
    pep735_groups = data.get("dependency-groups", {})

    assert legacy_after["workspaces"] == legacy_groups["workspaces"]
    assert set(pep735_groups).issubset({"lint"})

    # The new requirement may either be appended to the existing legacy group
    # or put in a new PEP 735 group. In both cases, editable entries must remain
    # only in the legacy table and the new requirement must not be duplicated.
    assert legacy_after["lint"] in (editables, [*editables, "ruff"])
    assert pep735_groups.get("lint", []) in ([], ["ruff"])
    combined_lint = legacy_after["lint"] + pep735_groups.get("lint", [])
    assert combined_lint.count("ruff") == 1
    assert [line for line in combined_lint if line.startswith("-e ")] == editables


def test_optional_group_update_does_not_materialize_legacy_dev_groups(
    project: Project,
) -> None:
    """Updating an optional group must not copy a same-named legacy group."""
    legacy_groups = {
        "docs": ["-e ./packages/pkg-app"],
        "workspaces": ["-e ./packages/pkg-core"],
    }
    _configure_groups(
        project,
        legacy_groups=legacy_groups,
        dependency_groups={"test": ["pytest"]},
        optional_dependencies={"docs": []},
    )

    project.add_dependencies(["sphinx"], "docs")

    data = _read_pyproject(project)
    assert data["project"]["optional-dependencies"]["docs"] == ["sphinx"]
    assert data["tool"]["pdm"]["dev-dependencies"] == legacy_groups

    # Looking up the optional group must not mutate dependency-groups. In
    # particular, the editable legacy docs dependency must not be duplicated
    # there merely because the optional group has the same name.
    assert data["dependency-groups"] == {"test": ["pytest"]}

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def test_reported_create_table_as_with_stream_cte():
    statement = parse_one(
        """
        CREATE TABLE foo AS
        WITH stream AS (
            SELECT * FROM bar
        )
        SELECT * FROM stream;
        """
    )

    assert isinstance(statement, exp.Create)
    query = statement.expression
    assert isinstance(query, exp.Select)

    ctes = query.args["with"].expressions
    assert len(ctes) == 1
    assert ctes[0].alias == "stream"
    assert isinstance(ctes[0].this, exp.Select)
    assert ctes[0].this.sql() == "SELECT * FROM bar"

    assert query.args["from"].this.name == "stream"
    assert statement.find(exp.Stream) is None
    assert statement.sql() == (
        "CREATE TABLE foo AS WITH stream AS (SELECT * FROM bar) "
        "SELECT * FROM stream"
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("cte_name", ["stream", "STREAM", "Stream"])
def test_stream_cte_name_is_case_insensitive(cte_name):
    query = parse_one(
        f"WITH {cte_name} AS (SELECT 1 AS id) SELECT id FROM {cte_name}"
    )

    cte = query.find(exp.CTE)
    assert cte is not None
    assert cte.alias.lower() == "stream"
    assert query.args["from"].this.name.lower() == "stream"
    assert query.find(exp.Stream) is None

    normalized = query.sql()
    assert parse_one(normalized).sql() == normalized


def test_stream_cte_supports_qualified_column_references():
    query = parse_one(
        "WITH stream AS (SELECT 1 AS id) SELECT stream.id FROM stream"
    )

    projection = query.selects[0]
    assert isinstance(projection, exp.Column)
    assert projection.table == "stream"
    assert projection.name == "id"
    assert query.args["from"].this.name == "stream"
    assert query.find(exp.Stream) is None


def test_stream_cte_with_column_list_and_multiple_ctes():
    query = parse_one(
        "WITH stream(id) AS (SELECT 1), "
        "later AS (SELECT id FROM stream) "
        "SELECT * FROM later"
    )

    ctes = query.args["with"].expressions
    assert [cte.alias for cte in ctes] == ["stream", "later"]
    assert ctes[0].alias_column_names == ["id"]

    later_source = ctes[1].this.args["from"].this
    assert later_source.name == "stream"
    assert query.find(exp.Stream) is None

    normalized = query.sql()
    assert parse_one(normalized).sql() == normalized


def test_stream_cte_inside_subquery():
    query = parse_one(
        "SELECT * FROM ("
        "WITH stream AS (SELECT 1 AS id) SELECT id FROM stream"
        ") AS result"
    )

    assert cte is not None
    assert cte.alias == "stream"
    assert query.find(exp.Stream) is None

    normalized = query.sql()
    assert parse_one(normalized).sql() == normalized


def test_stream_remains_usable_as_an_ordinary_table_name():

    assert query.args["from"].this.name == "stream"

import importlib
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from unittest import mock

import pytest

from django_cmd import main


def test_main_makes_current_directory_importable(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """A settings module beside the invoked project must be importable."""
    module_name = "django_cmd_current_directory_settings_probe"
    (tmp_path / f"{module_name}.py").write_text(
        'SETTINGS_MARKER = "loaded-from-current-directory"\n',
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
    monkeypatch.delenv("DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE", raising=False)

    # Simulate an installed console script: its script directory is on sys.path,
    # but the project's working directory is not.
    original_path = ["/entry-point/bin", "/site-packages"]
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "path", original_path.copy())
    sys.modules.pop(module_name, None)

    imported_modules = []

    def execute_command(argv):
        imported_modules.append(importlib.import_module(module_name))

    try:
        with mock.patch(
            "django_cmd.execute_from_command_line", side_effect=execute_command
        ) as execute:
            main()
    finally:
        sys.modules.pop(module_name, None)

    assert execute.call_count == 1
    assert len(imported_modules) == 1
    assert (
        imported_modules[0].SETTINGS_MARKER == "loaded-from-current-directory"
    )
    # Adjusting the import path must not discard the entry-point environment.
    assert all(entry in sys.path for entry in original_path)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("current_directory_entry", ["", "."])
def test_main_does_not_duplicate_an_existing_current_directory_entry(
    monkeypatch, tmp_path, current_directory_entry
):
    """Repeated invocation should not add duplicate path entries."""
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
    monkeypatch.delenv("DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE", raising=False)
    original_path = [current_directory_entry, "/entry-point/bin"]
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "path", original_path.copy())

    with mock.patch("django_cmd.execute_from_command_line") as execute:
        main()

    assert execute.called
    assert sys.path.count(current_directory_entry) == 1
    assert all(entry in sys.path for entry in original_path)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "settings_source", ["pyproject.toml", "setup.cfg", "environment"]
)
def test_django_command_imports_project_settings_from_current_directory(
    tmp_path, settings_source
):
    """The installed command must work like manage.py for a local project."""
    project_package = tmp_path / "myproject"
    project_package.mkdir()
    (project_package / "__init__.py").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
    (project_package / "settings.py").write_text(
        'SECRET_KEY = "django-cmd-path-test"\nINSTALLED_APPS = []\n',
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    env = os.environ.copy()
    # In particular, do not let the test runner's PYTHONPATH make the project
    # importable and conceal the console-script behavior being tested.
    env.pop("PYTHONPATH", None)
    env.pop("DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE", None)

    if settings_source == "pyproject.toml":
        (tmp_path / "pyproject.toml").write_text(
            '[tool.django]\nsettings_module = "myproject.settings"\n',
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
    elif settings_source == "setup.cfg":
        (tmp_path / "setup.cfg").write_text(
            "[django]\nsettings_module = myproject.settings\n",
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
    else:
        env["DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE"] = "myproject.settings"

    result = subprocess.run(
        ["django", "check"],
        cwd=tmp_path,
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=60,
    )

    assert result.returncode == 0, (
        f"django check failed with settings from {settings_source}.\n"
        f"stdout:\n{result.stdout}\n"
        f"stderr:\n{result.stderr}"
    )
