from six.moves.urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit

from clldutils.badge import badge, Colors


def test_legacy_badge_output_is_preserved():
    assert badge('cov', '20%', Colors.orange) == (
        '![cov: 20%](https://img.shields.io/badge/cov-20%25-orange.svg '
        '"cov: 20%")'
    )
    assert badge('cov', '20%', Colors.orange, markdown=False, style='plastic') == (
        'https://img.shields.io/badge/cov-20%25-orange.svg?style=plastic'
    )


def test_legacy_keyword_arguments_are_still_accepted():
    # subject, status, and color were named parameters in the original public
    # signature, not shields.io query parameters.
    assert badge(
        subject='cov', status='20%', color=Colors.orange, markdown=False
    ) == 'https://img.shields.io/badge/cov-20%25-orange.svg'


def test_legacy_positional_format_and_markdown_arguments_are_preserved():
    assert badge('cov', '20%', Colors.orange, 'png', False) == (
        'https://img.shields.io/badge/cov-20%25-orange.png'
    )


def test_non_badge_shields_endpoints_accept_arbitrary_path_segments():
    # Service badges do not use the static subject-status-color URL layout.
    assert badge(
        'clld',
        'clldutils',
        'master',
        endpoint='travis',
        fmt='png',
        markdown=False,
    ) == 'https://img.shields.io/travis/clld/clldutils/master.png'


def test_shields_query_options_are_encoded_without_leaking_control_arguments():
    url = badge(
        'build',
        'passing',
        Colors.brightgreen,
        markdown=False,
        style='flat-square',
        label='CI status',
        logo='github',
    )
    parsed = urlsplit(url)

    assert parsed.scheme == 'https'
    assert parsed.netloc == 'img.shields.io'
    assert parsed.path == '/badge/build-passing-brightgreen.svg'
    assert parse_qs(parsed.query) == {
        'style': ['flat-square'],
        'label': ['CI status'],
        'logo': ['github'],
    }
    assert 'markdown' not in parse_qs(parsed.query)
    assert 'endpoint' not in parse_qs(parsed.query)

from pyupgrade import main


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('source', 'expected'),
    (
        # The declaration is redundant when it is the entire module.
        ('__metaclass__ = type\n', ''),
        ('__metaclass__ = type', ''),
        ('__metaclass__=type\n', ''),
        ('__metaclass__ = (type)\n', ''),
        # Remove the whole declaration, including an inline comment, without
        # consuming unrelated source or unrelated blank lines.
        (
            '__metaclass__ = type  # python 2 new-style classes\n'
            'x = 1\n',
            'x = 1\n',
        ),
        (
            '__metaclass__ = type\n'
            '\n'
            'class C:\n'
            '    pass\n',
            '\n'
            'class C:\n'
            '    pass\n',
        ),
        (
            '__metaclass__ = type\n'
            'x = 1\n'
            '__metaclass__=type\n'
            'y = 2\n',
            'x = 1\n'
            'y = 2\n',
        ),

import struct

import zlib
from unittest.mock import Mock

import pytest

from lektor.context import Context
from lektor.imagetools import make_image_thumbnail

def _png_chunk(kind, data):
    checksum = zlib.crc32(kind + data) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + kind + data + struct.pack(">I", checksum)


def _write_png(path, width, height):
    """Write a small, valid RGB PNG without requiring Pillow."""
    header = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", width, height, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)
    row = b"\x00" + (b"\x00\x00\x00" * width)
    path.write_bytes(
        b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
        + _png_chunk(b"IHDR", header)
        + _png_chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(row * height))
        + _png_chunk(b"IEND", b"")
    )

from alarmdecoder import AlarmDecoder
from alarmdecoder.messages import Message
from alarmdecoder.panels import ADEMCO
from alarmdecoder.zonetracking import Zone, Zonetracker


COMMUNICATOR_FAILURE = (
    '[00000001000000000A--],0fc,'
    '[f704009f10fc000008020000000000],'
    '"COMM. FAILURE                   "'
)
ECP_CHECK_103 = (
    '[00000001000000100A--],0bf,'
    '[f704009f10bf000208020000000000],'
    '"CHECK 103 LngRngRadio       0000"'
)


def make_zonetracker():
    decoder = Mock(spec=AlarmDecoder)
    decoder.mode = ADEMCO
    return Zonetracker(decoder)


def keypad_message(code, text, ready=False):
    bitfield = (
        "10000000000000000A--"
        if ready
        else "00000000000000100A--"
    )
    return Message(
        '[{0}],{1},[f707000600e5800c0c020000],"{2}"'.format(
            bitfield, code, text.ljust(32)
        )
    )


def test_communicator_failure_followed_by_multidigit_ecp_check():
    """Reproduce the mixed int/str zone list from the reported traceback."""
    tracker = make_zonetracker()

    tracker.update(Message(COMMUNICATOR_FAILURE))
    tracker.update(Message(ECP_CHECK_103))

    # Repeating an existing ECP zone must also take the existing-zone path
    # without creating a second, differently keyed zone.
    tracker.update(Message(ECP_CHECK_103))

    assert 103 in tracker.zones
    assert "103" not in tracker.zones
    assert tracker.zones[103].zone == 103
    assert tracker.zones[103].status == Zone.CHECK
    assert tracker.faulted.count(103) == 1
    assert all(type(zone) is int for zone in tracker.faulted)
    assert tracker.faulted == sorted(tracker.faulted)


def test_ecp_zone_numbers_are_canonical_integers():
    tracker = make_zonetracker()
    message = keypad_message("0bf", "CHECK 001")

    tracker.update(message)
    tracker.update(message)

    assert set(tracker.zones) == {1}
    assert tracker.faulted == [1]
    assert tracker.zones[1].zone == 1
    assert tracker.zones[1].status == Zone.CHECK


def test_ecp_and_regular_faults_share_one_numerically_sorted_zone_list():
    tracker = make_zonetracker()

    tracker.update(keypad_message("002", "FAULT 2"))
    tracker.update(keypad_message("00a", "FAULT 10"))
    tracker.update(keypad_message("0bf", "CHECK 103 LngRngRadio       0000"))

    assert tracker.faulted == [2, 10, 103]
    assert set(tracker.zones) == {2, 10, 103}

"""Regression tests for client EOF while an asynchronous handler is running."""

import asyncio
import unittest

from aiosmtpd.smtp import SMTP as Server
from unittest.mock import Mock


class RecordingHandler:
    """A handler whose MAIL, RCPT, or DATA hook can be made to block."""

    def __init__(self, slow_command, delay=60):
        self.slow_command = slow_command
        self.delay = delay
        self.started = False
        self.cancelled = False
        self.completed = False
        self.exceptions = []
        self.recipients = []

    async def _pause(self, command):
        if command != self.slow_command:
            return
        self.started = True
        try:
            await asyncio.sleep(self.delay)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            self.cancelled = True
            raise
        self.completed = True

    async def handle_MAIL(self, server, session, envelope, address, options):
        await self._pause('MAIL')
        envelope.mail_from = address
        return '250 OK'

    async def handle_RCPT(
            self, server, session, envelope, address, rcpt_options):
        await self._pause('RCPT')
        envelope.rcpt_tos.append(address)
        self.recipients.append(address)
        return '250 OK'

    async def handle_DATA(self, server, session, envelope):
        await self._pause('DATA')
        return '250 OK'

    async def handle_exception(self, error):
        self.exceptions.append(error)
        return '500 handler saw {}'.format(type(error).__name__)


class FailingRCPTHandler:
    error = None

    async def handle_RCPT(
            self, server, session, envelope, address, rcpt_options):
        raise ValueError('handler failed')

    async def handle_exception(self, error):
        self.error = error
        return '451 temporary failure'


class TestClientDisconnectDuringHandler(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.responses = []
        self.protocol = None
        self.transport = Mock()
        self.transport.write = self._write
        self._old_loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
        self.loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
        asyncio.set_event_loop(self.loop)

    def tearDown(self):
        if self.protocol is not None:
            task = self.protocol._handler_coroutine
            if task is not None and not task.done():
                task.cancel()
                try:
                    self.loop.run_until_complete(task)
                except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception):
                    pass
        self.loop.close()
        asyncio.set_event_loop(self._old_loop)

    def _write(self, data):
        self.responses.append(data)
        if data.startswith(b'500') and self.protocol is not None:
            # The unfixed server otherwise spins forever reading EOF and
            # writing "500 Error: bad syntax".  Stop this synthetic connection
            # after the first erroneous response so the test can fail cleanly
            # instead of hanging the test suite.
            self.protocol.transport = None

    def _get_protocol(self, handler):
        self.protocol = Server(handler, loop=self.loop)
        self.protocol.connection_made(self.transport)
        return self.protocol

    async def _wait_until_started(self, handler):
        for unused in range(50):
            if handler.started:
                return
            await asyncio.sleep(0)
        self.fail('The SMTP handler hook was never entered')

    def _run_handler_task(self):
        try:
            self.loop.run_until_complete(self.protocol._handler_coroutine)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            # Propagating cancellation is one valid way to terminate the
            # per-connection task; swallowing it and returning is also fine.
            pass

    def _check_eof_is_graceful(self, handler, session, expected_codes):
        protocol = self._get_protocol(handler)
        protocol.data_received(session)
        self.loop.run_until_complete(self._wait_until_started(handler))

        # This is the same protocol callback exercised when a client sends
        # EOF while the command handler is still awaiting its slow operation.
        protocol.eof_received()
        self._run_handler_task()

        self.assertTrue(protocol._handler_coroutine.done())
        self.assertTrue(handler.cancelled)
        self.assertFalse(handler.completed)
        self.assertEqual(handler.exceptions, [])
        self.assertEqual(
            [response[:3] for response in self.responses], expected_codes)
        self.assertFalse(any(
            response.startswith(b'500') for response in self.responses))

    def test_eof_during_slow_rcpt_does_not_create_error_loop(self):
        # Reproduce the issue's pipelined netcat session, including commands
        # which must not be processed after EOF cancels the RCPT handler.
        handler = RecordingHandler('RCPT')
        self._check_eof_is_graceful(
            handler,
            b'HELO there\r\n'
            b'MAIL FROM: somebody@example.com\r\n'
            b'RCPT TO: anybody@example.com\r\n'
            b'DATA\r\n'
            b'test\r\n'
            b'.\r\n',
            [b'220', b'250', b'250'])
        self.assertEqual(handler.recipients, [])

    def test_eof_during_slow_mail_is_also_graceful(self):
        # Cancellation belongs to command processing generally, not just to
        # the RCPT implementation.
        handler = RecordingHandler('MAIL')
        self._check_eof_is_graceful(
            handler,
            b'HELO there\r\n'
            b'MAIL FROM: somebody@example.com\r\n'
            b'RCPT TO: anybody@example.com\r\n',
            [b'220', b'250'])

    def test_eof_during_slow_data_handler_is_also_graceful(self):
        handler = RecordingHandler('DATA')
        self._check_eof_is_graceful(
            handler,
            b'HELO there\r\n'
            b'MAIL FROM: somebody@example.com\r\n'
            b'RCPT TO: anybody@example.com\r\n'
            b'DATA\r\n'
            b'test\r\n'
            b'.\r\n',
            [b'220', b'250', b'250', b'250', b'354'])

    def test_slow_rcpt_can_still_complete_normally(self):
        handler = RecordingHandler('RCPT', delay=0)
        protocol = self._get_protocol(handler)
        protocol.data_received(
            b'HELO there\r\n'
            b'MAIL FROM: somebody@example.com\r\n'
            b'RCPT TO: anybody@example.com\r\n'
            b'QUIT\r\n')
        self._run_handler_task()

        self.assertTrue(handler.completed)
        self.assertFalse(handler.cancelled)
        self.assertEqual(handler.recipients, ['anybody@example.com'])
        self.assertEqual(handler.exceptions, [])
        self.assertEqual(self.responses[3], b'250 OK\r\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.responses[-1], b'221 Bye\r\n')

    def test_ordinary_handler_exception_still_gets_a_response(self):
        handler = FailingRCPTHandler()
        protocol = self._get_protocol(handler)
        protocol.data_received(
            b'HELO there\r\n'
            b'MAIL FROM: somebody@example.com\r\n'
            b'RCPT TO: anybody@example.com\r\n'
            b'QUIT\r\n')
        self._run_handler_task()

        self.assertIsInstance(handler.error, ValueError)
        self.assertEqual(str(handler.error), 'handler failed')
        self.assertEqual(self.responses[3], b'451 temporary failure\r\n')
        # An ordinary handler error must not be confused with cancellation;
        # the session remains usable and can process the following command.
        self.assertEqual(self.responses[-1], b'221 Bye\r\n')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

import pytest

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


DIALECTS = ("spark2", "spark", "databricks")


def _raw_string(expression: exp.Expression) -> exp.RawString:
    raw_string = expression.find(exp.RawString)
    assert raw_string is not None
    return raw_string


@pytest.mark.parametrize("dialect", DIALECTS)
def test_spark_raw_string_in_regexp_replace(dialect: str) -> None:
    sql = "SELECT REGEXP_REPLACE('100-200', r'([^0-9])', '')"

    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read=dialect)

    assert _raw_string(expression).this == "([^0-9])"
    assert expression.sql(dialect=dialect) == sql


@pytest.mark.parametrize("dialect", DIALECTS)
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql, expected",
    [
        (r"SELECT r'\d+\s*'", r"\d+\s*"),
        (r"SELECT r'C:\Users\me\file.txt'", r"C:\Users\me\file.txt"),
        (r"SELECT r'\n'", r"\n"),
        (r"SELECT r'\\d+'", r"\\d+"),
    ],
)
def test_spark_raw_string_preserves_backslashes(
    dialect: str, sql: str, expected: str
) -> None:
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read=dialect)

    assert _raw_string(expression).this == expected

    # Backslashes in a Spark raw string are literal and must not be doubled
    # when generating SQL, since doing so changes the string's value.
    generated = expression.sql(dialect=dialect)
    assert generated == sql

    round_tripped = sqlglot.parse_one(generated, read=dialect)
    assert _raw_string(round_tripped).this == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize("dialect", DIALECTS)
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [
        "SELECT R'([^0-9])'",
        'SELECT r"([^0-9])"',
        'SELECT R"([^0-9])"',
    ],
)
def test_spark_raw_string_prefix_and_quote_variants(dialect: str, sql: str) -> None:
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read=dialect)

    assert _raw_string(expression).this == "([^0-9])"

    generated = expression.sql(dialect=dialect)
    round_tripped = sqlglot.parse_one(generated, read=dialect)
    assert _raw_string(round_tripped).this == "([^0-9])"

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def test_postgres_multi_unit_interval_without_parentheses():
    """The unparenthesized form must not consume AND as the interval unit."""
    sql = """
        select *
        from table
        where
            some_column >= current_date + interval '1 day 1 hour'
            and some_another_column is True;
    """

    parsed = parse_one(sql, dialect="postgres")
    where = parsed.args["where"].this

    assert isinstance(where, exp.And)

    comparison = where.this
    assert isinstance(comparison, exp.GTE)
    assert comparison.this == exp.column("some_column")

    addition = comparison.expression
    assert isinstance(addition, exp.Add)
    assert isinstance(addition.this, exp.CurrentDate)

    interval = addition.expression
    assert isinstance(interval, exp.Interval)
    assert interval.this == exp.Literal.string("1 day 1 hour")
    assert interval.args.get("unit") is None

    other_predicate = where.expression
    assert isinstance(other_predicate, exp.Is)
    assert other_predicate.this == exp.column("some_another_column")
    assert isinstance(other_predicate.expression, exp.Boolean)
    assert other_predicate.expression.this is True

    # Parentheses may change the surrounding tree, but not the interval itself.
    parenthesized = parse_one(
        """
        SELECT *
        FROM table
        WHERE some_column >= (CURRENT_DATE + INTERVAL '1 day 1 hour')
          AND some_another_column IS TRUE
        """,
        dialect="postgres",
    )
    assert parenthesized.find(exp.Interval) == interval

    # The resulting tree must also generate SQL that can be parsed again without
    # losing the interval contents or the predicate following it.
    reparsed = parse_one(parsed.sql(dialect="postgres"), dialect="postgres")
    assert reparsed.find(exp.Interval) == interval
    assert isinstance(reparsed.args["where"].this, exp.And)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "interval_text",
    [
        "1 day 1 hour",
        "2 years 3 months",
        "10 days 5 hours 30 minutes",
        "1 year 2 months 3 days 4 hours 5 minutes 6 seconds",
    ],
)
def test_postgres_multi_unit_intervals_preserve_all_text_and_stop_at_and(interval_text):
    parsed = parse_one(
        f"""
        SELECT *
        FROM t
        WHERE ts >= CURRENT_DATE + INTERVAL '{interval_text}' AND enabled
        """,
        dialect="postgres",
    )

    interval = parsed.find(exp.Interval)
    assert isinstance(interval, exp.Interval)
    assert interval.this == exp.Literal.string(interval_text)
    assert interval.args.get("unit") is None

    where = parsed.args["where"].this
    assert isinstance(where, exp.And)
    assert where.expression == exp.column("enabled")


def test_postgres_standalone_multi_unit_interval_has_no_external_unit():
    interval = parse_one("INTERVAL '1 day 1 hour'", dialect="postgres")

    assert isinstance(interval, exp.Interval)
    assert interval.this == exp.Literal.string("1 day 1 hour")
    assert interval.args.get("unit") is None
    assert interval.sql(dialect="postgres") == "INTERVAL '1 day 1 hour'"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("source", "number", "unit", "rendered"),
    [
        ("INTERVAL '1 day'", "1", "DAY", "INTERVAL '1 DAY'"),
        ("INTERVAL '5 hours'", "5", "HOURS", "INTERVAL '5 HOURS'"),
    ],
)
def test_postgres_single_unit_interval_extraction_is_unchanged(
    source, number, unit, rendered
):
    interval = parse_one(source, dialect="postgres")

    assert isinstance(interval, exp.Interval)
    assert interval.this == exp.Literal.string(number)
    assert interval.args.get("unit") == exp.var(unit)
    assert interval.sql(dialect="postgres") == rendered


def test_postgres_explicit_interval_unit_is_unchanged():
    interval = parse_one("INTERVAL '1' DAY", dialect="postgres")

    assert isinstance(interval, exp.Interval)
    assert interval.this == exp.Literal.string("1")
    assert interval.args.get("unit") == exp.var("DAY")
    assert interval.sql(dialect="postgres") == "INTERVAL '1' DAY"

import pytest

from sqlglot import parse_one


ISSUE_QUERY = """
SELECT datasets.a,
       id AS history_id,
       app_users.id AS user_id,
       companies.name AS companyname,
       app_users.email AS email,
       app_users.group_id AS group_id
FROM datasets
JOIN companies ON datasets.companyid = companies.companyid
JOIN app_users USING (short_user_id)
WHERE (datasets.companyid = '405')
AND (mmh_trip_start NOTNULL)
"""


def assert_equivalent(sql, standard_sql, read=None):
    actual = parse_one(sql, read=read)
    expected = parse_one(standard_sql, read=read)
    assert actual == expected, (
        f"{sql!r} was parsed as {actual.sql()!r}, "
        f"but should be equivalent to {expected.sql()!r}"
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("read", [None, "postgres"])
def test_issue_query_with_notnull(read):
    """The reported query parses and has the same AST as IS NOT NULL."""
    assert_equivalent(
        ISSUE_QUERY,
        ISSUE_QUERY.replace("NOTNULL", "IS NOT NULL"),
        read=read,
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "operator, standard_operator",
    [("NOTNULL", "IS NOT NULL"), ("ISNULL", "IS NULL")],
)
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "value",
    ["col", "t.col", "(col + 1)", "COALESCE(col, 0)"],
)
def test_postfix_null_operators_match_standard_syntax(
    value, operator, standard_operator
):
    assert_equivalent(
        f"SELECT {value} {operator} AS null_check FROM t",
        f"SELECT {value} {standard_operator} AS null_check FROM t",
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "operator, standard_operator",
    [("NOTNULL", "IS NOT NULL"), ("ISNULL", "IS NULL")],
)
def test_postfix_null_operators_in_compound_where(operator, standard_operator):
    assert_equivalent(
        f"""
        SELECT * FROM datasets
        WHERE (datasets.companyid = '405')
        AND (mmh_trip_start {operator})
        """,
        f"""
        SELECT * FROM datasets
        WHERE (datasets.companyid = '405')
        AND (mmh_trip_start {standard_operator})
        """,
    )


def test_postfix_null_operators_are_case_insensitive():
    assert_equivalent(
        "select * from t where a notnull and b isnull",
        "SELECT * FROM t WHERE a IS NOT NULL AND b IS NULL",
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "operator, standard_operator",
    [("NOTNULL", "IS NOT NULL"), ("ISNULL", "IS NULL")],
)
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "predicate",
    ["a IN (1, 2)", "a BETWEEN 1 AND 2", "a LIKE 'x%'"],
)
def test_postfix_null_operators_apply_to_complete_predicates(
    predicate, operator, standard_operator
):
    """PostgreSQL gives IN/BETWEEN/LIKE higher precedence than ISNULL/NOTNULL.

    Consequently, the postfix operator applies to the complete predicate, not
    merely to its final operand.
    """
    assert_equivalent(
        f"SELECT * FROM t WHERE {predicate} {operator}",
        f"SELECT * FROM t WHERE ({predicate}) {standard_operator}",
    )

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Tests for uploading the complete local workflow directory."""

import os
from unittest.mock import patch

from click.testing import CliRunner

from reana_client.cli import cli


ACCESS_TOKEN = "000000"
WORKFLOW = "mytest.1"
ENV = {"REANA_SERVER_URL": "http://localhost"}


def _write_file(path, content="test content"):
    """Create a file and any missing parent directories."""
    parent = os.path.dirname(path)
    if parent:
        os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as file_:
        file_.write(content)


def _invoke_upload(runner, uploaded, sources=(), specification=None):
    """Invoke upload while recording every file sent to the API client.

    The fake accepts both individual files and directories so that the tests
    exercise the CLI contract without prescribing how it enumerates files.
    """
    if specification is None:
        specification = {
            "specification": {"inputs": {"files": [], "directories": []}}
        }

    def fake_upload_to_server(workflow, filename, access_token):
        assert workflow == WORKFLOW
        assert access_token == ACCESS_TOKEN

        if os.path.isdir(filename):
            paths = []
            for root, dirs, files in os.walk(filename):
                dirs.sort()
                for name in sorted(files):
                    paths.append(os.path.join(root, name))
        else:
            if not os.path.isfile(filename):
                raise FileNotFoundError(filename)
            paths = [filename]

        relative_paths = []
        for path in paths:
            relative_path = os.path.relpath(os.path.abspath(path), os.getcwd())
            relative_path = relative_path.replace(os.sep, "/")
            uploaded.append(relative_path)
            relative_paths.append(relative_path)
        return relative_paths

    with patch(
        "reana_client.api.client.get_workflow_specification",
        return_value=specification,
    ), patch(
        "reana_client.api.client.upload_to_server",
        side_effect=fake_upload_to_server,
    ):
        return runner.invoke(
            cli,
            [
                "upload",
                "-t",
                ACCESS_TOKEN,
                "--workflow",
                WORKFLOW,
                *sources,
            ],
        )


def test_upload_without_sources_uploads_entire_directory_recursively():
    """Workflow definitions and their dependencies must not be omitted."""
    runner = CliRunner(env=ENV)
    uploaded = []
    specification = {
        "specification": {
            "inputs": {"files": ["inputs/data.txt"], "directories": []},
            "workflow": {"file": "workflow/serial.yaml"},
        }
    }

    with runner.isolated_filesystem():
        expected = {
            "reana.yaml",
            "README.md",
            "inputs/data.txt",
            "workflow/serial.yaml",
            "code/analysis.py",
            "code/helpers.py",
            "environment/Dockerfile",
        }
        for path in expected:
            _write_file(path)

        result = _invoke_upload(runner, uploaded, specification=specification)

        assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
        assert set(uploaded) == expected


def test_upload_with_explicit_source_does_not_upload_whole_directory():
    """Supplying SOURCES retains the existing selective-upload behavior."""
    runner = CliRunner(env=ENV)
    uploaded = []

    with runner.isolated_filesystem():
        _write_file("reana.yaml")
        _write_file("selected.txt")
        _write_file("unselected.txt")
        _write_file("nested/other.txt")

        result = _invoke_upload(runner, uploaded, sources=["selected.txt"])

        assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
        assert set(uploaded) == {"selected.txt"}


def test_upload_without_sources_respects_gitignore_recursively():
    """Files matched by .gitignore are excluded at every directory level."""
    runner = CliRunner(env=ENV)
    uploaded = []

    with runner.isolated_filesystem():
        _write_file(".gitignore", "ignored.txt\n*.log\nbuild/\n")
        for path in (
            "reana.yaml",
            "keep.txt",
            "ignored.txt",
            "debug.log",
            "data/keep.txt",
            "data/debug.log",
            "build/output.txt",
        ):
            _write_file(path)

        result = _invoke_upload(runner, uploaded)

        assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
        uploaded_set = set(uploaded)
        assert {"reana.yaml", "keep.txt", "data/keep.txt"} <= uploaded_set
        assert {
            "ignored.txt",
            "debug.log",
            "data/debug.log",
            "build/output.txt",
        }.isdisjoint(uploaded_set)


def test_upload_without_sources_applies_gitignore_and_reanaignore():
    """A file excluded by either ignore file must not be uploaded."""
    runner = CliRunner(env=ENV)
    uploaded = []

    with runner.isolated_filesystem():
        _write_file(".gitignore", "from-git.txt\n")
        _write_file(".reanaignore", "secret.txt\n*.tmp\ncache/\n")
        for path in (
            "reana.yaml",
            "keep.txt",
            "data/keep.csv",
            "from-git.txt",
            "secret.txt",
            "scratch.tmp",
            "cache/item.txt",
        ):

"""Tests for Nickname leading/trailing whitespace handling."""

import pytest

from precis_i18n import get_profile


NICKNAME_PROFILES = (
    "NicknameCasePreserved",
    "NicknameCaseMapped",
    "NicknameCaseMapped:ToLower",
    "NicknameCaseMapped:CaseFold",
    "Nickname",
)

# Characters stripped by str.strip() that must not silently disappear from
# the edges of a Nickname. Newline is intentionally excluded: it retains its
# historical stripping behavior for compatibility.
INVALID_EDGE_WHITESPACE = (
    "\t",
    "\v",
    "\f",
    "\r",
    "\x1c",
    "\x1d",
    "\x1e",
    "\x1f",
    "\x85",
    "\u2028",
    "\u2029",
)


def assert_invalid_white_space(profile, value):
    """The input must be rejected with the new, specific diagnostic."""
    with pytest.raises(UnicodeEncodeError) as exc_info:
        profile.enforce(value)
    assert "DISALLOWED/invalid_white_space" in str(exc_info.value)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("profile_name", NICKNAME_PROFILES)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("char", INVALID_EDGE_WHITESPACE)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("position", ("leading", "trailing"))
def test_invalid_edge_whitespace_has_diagnostic(profile_name, char, position):
    profile = get_profile(profile_name)
    value = char + "alpha" if position == "leading" else "alpha" + char
    assert_invalid_white_space(profile, value)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "value",
    (
        " \talpha",             # Invalid character behind an ASCII space.
        "\n\talpha",            # Invalid character behind a newline.
        "alpha\r ",
        "alpha\x1f\n",
        "\u00a0\talpha",        # Zs is mapped before whitespace is checked.
        "alpha\u2029\u00a0",
        "\tcharlie\r\n",        # Mixed example from the issue.
    ),
)
def test_invalid_whitespace_behind_strippable_characters(value):
    """Spaces/newlines must not hide other invalid edge whitespace."""
    assert_invalid_white_space(get_profile("NicknameCasePreserved"), value)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("profile_name", NICKNAME_PROFILES)
def test_ascii_spaces_and_newlines_are_stripped(profile_name):
    profile = get_profile(profile_name)
    assert profile.enforce(" \n  alpha  \n") == "alpha"
    assert profile.enforce(" a\n") == "a"


def test_non_ascii_zs_spaces_are_mapped_stripped_and_collapsed():
    profile = get_profile("NicknameCasePreserved")
    value = "\u00a0\u2000Alpha\u2003\u202fBeta\u3000"
    assert profile.enforce(value) == "Alpha Beta"


def test_interior_control_whitespace_is_not_silently_accepted():
    """The edge-whitespace diagnostic must not make interior controls valid."""
    profile = get_profile("NicknameCasePreserved")
    for value in ("alpha\tbeta", "alpha\nbeta", "alpha\rbeta"):
        with pytest.raises(UnicodeEncodeError):
            profile.enforce(value)

import pytest

from pyupgrade import _fix_py3_plus
from pyupgrade import main


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('source', 'expected'),
    (
        # The basic Python 2 new-style class declaration is redundant in py3.
        ('__metaclass__ = type\n', ''),
        ('__metaclass__ = type', ''),
        ('__metaclass__=type\n', ''),
        ('__metaclass__ = (type)\n', ''),
        ('__metaclass__ = type  # new-style classes\n', ''),
        (
            '__metaclass__ = type\n'
            'class C:\n'
            '    pass\n',
            'class C:\n'
            '    pass\n',
        ),
        (
            'import os\n'
            '__metaclass__ = type\n'
            '\n'
            'class C:\n'
            '    pass\n',
            'import os\n'
            '\n'
            'class C:\n'
            '    pass\n',
        ),
        # Every module-level occurrence should be removed, without disturbing
        # unrelated assignments.
        (
            '__metaclass__ = type\n'
            'x = 1\n'
            '__metaclass__ = type\n',
            'x = 1\n',
        ),
        # Visiting a function or class must not prevent a later module-level
        # assignment from being recognized.
        (
            'def f():\n'
            '    pass\n'
            '__metaclass__ = type\n',
            'def f():\n'
            '    pass\n',
        ),
        (
            'class C:\n'
            '    __metaclass__ = type\n'
            '__metaclass__ = type\n',
            'class C:\n'
            '    __metaclass__ = type\n',
        ),
        # Conditionals do not introduce a new Python scope.  Removing the
        # statement must also remove its indentation, not corrupt the suite.
        (

from mock import Mock

from alarmdecoder import AlarmDecoder
from alarmdecoder.messages import Message
from alarmdecoder.panels import ADEMCO
from alarmdecoder.zonetracking import Zone, Zonetracker


COMM_FAILURE = (
    '[00000001000000000A--],0fc,'
    '[f704009f10fc000008020000000000],'
    '"COMM. FAILURE                   "'
)
CHECK_103 = (
    '[00000001000000100A--],0bf,'
    '[f704009f10bf000208020000000000],'
    '"CHECK 103 LngRngRadio       0000"'
)


def _make_zonetracker():
    decoder = Mock(spec=AlarmDecoder)
    decoder.mode = ADEMCO
    return Zonetracker(decoder)


def _panel_message(numeric_code, text):
    return Message(
        '[00000000000000000A--],{0},'
        '[f707000600e5800c0c020000],"{1}"'.format(numeric_code, text)
    )


def _ecp_check_message(zone_text):
    return Message(
        '[00000001000000100A--],0bf,'
        '[f704009f10bf000208020000000000],'
        '"CHECK {0} LngRngRadio       0000"'.format(zone_text)
    )


def test_issue_messages_do_not_mix_integer_and_string_zone_ids():
    """A normal fault followed by the reported ECP failure must not crash."""
    tracker = _make_zonetracker()
    fault_events = []

    def on_fault(sender, *args, **kwargs):
        fault_events.append(kwargs['zone'])

    tracker.on_fault += on_fault

    # An ordinary keypad fault puts an integer zone in the faulted list.  The
    # subsequent CHECK message used to add a string and fail while sorting.
    tracker.update(_panel_message('002', 'FAULT 2'))
    tracker.update(Message(COMM_FAILURE))

    # A communicator failure is not itself a zone fault.
    assert tracker.faulted == [2]
    assert set(tracker.zones) == {2}

    tracker.update(Message(CHECK_103))

    assert tracker.faulted == [2, 103]
    assert set(tracker.zones) == {2, 103}
    assert all(isinstance(zone, int) for zone in tracker.faulted)
    assert all(isinstance(zone, int) for zone in tracker.zones)

    assert tracker.zones[103].zone == 103
    assert tracker.zones[103].status == Zone.CHECK
    assert fault_events == [2, 103]


def test_ecp_check_zones_are_sorted_numerically_and_updates_are_idempotent():
    tracker = _make_zonetracker()

    tracker.update(Message(CHECK_103))
    tracker.update(_ecp_check_message('9'))
    tracker.update(Message(CHECK_103))  # Repeated report for the same zone.

    # Numeric zone IDs also avoid lexicographic ordering such as "103" < "9".
    assert tracker.faulted == [9, 103]
    assert set(tracker.zones) == {9, 103}
    assert tracker.zones[9].status == Zone.CHECK
    assert tracker.zones[103].status == Zone.CHECK


def test_ecp_check_with_leading_zeroes_reuses_the_numeric_zone():
    tracker = _make_zonetracker()
    fault_events = []

    def on_fault(sender, *args, **kwargs):
        fault_events.append(kwargs['zone'])

    tracker.on_fault += on_fault

    tracker.update(_panel_message('007', 'FAULT 7'))
    tracker.update(_ecp_check_message('007'))

    # "007" and 7 identify the same zone; no string-keyed duplicate should be
    # created and the repeated report should not emit another fault event.
    assert tracker.faulted == [7]
    assert set(tracker.zones) == {7}
    assert fault_events == [7]


def test_communicator_failure_alone_does_not_create_a_zone():
    tracker = _make_zonetracker()

    tracker.update(Message(COMM_FAILURE))

    assert tracker.zones == {}
    assert tracker.faulted == []

"""Tests for Windows-safe adb log excerpt filenames."""

import io
import os
from unittest import mock

from mobly import utils
from mobly.controllers import android_device
from tests.lib import mock_android_device


MOCK_ADB_LOGCAT = (
    '02-29 14:02:19.123  4454  Nothing\n'
    '02-29 14:02:21.456  4454  Something\n'
    '02-29 14:02:21.789  4454  Something again\n'
    '02-29 14:02:22.123  4454  Something again and again\n'
)
MOCK_ADB_LOGCAT_BEGIN_TIME = '02-29 14:02:20.123'
MOCK_ADB_LOGCAT_EXCERPT = (
    '02-29 14:02:21.456  4454  Something\n'
    '02-29 14:02:21.789  4454  Something again\n'
    '02-29 14:02:22.123  4454  Something again and again\n'
)


def _create_device_with_logcat(tmp_path):
    """Creates a device and a logcat file without starting real services."""
    with mock.patch(
            'mobly.controllers.android_device_lib.adb.AdbProxy',
            return_value=mock_android_device.MockAdbProxy('1')), mock.patch(
                'mobly.controllers.android_device_lib.fastboot.FastbootProxy',
                return_value=mock_android_device.MockFastbootProxy('1')):
        ad = android_device.AndroidDevice(serial='1')

    ad._log_path = str(tmp_path / ('AndroidDevice%s' % ad.serial))
    utils.create_dir(ad.log_path)

    logcat_path = os.path.join(
        ad.log_path, 'adblog,%s,%s.txt' % (ad.model, ad.serial))
    with io.open(logcat_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as logcat_file:
        logcat_file.write(MOCK_ADB_LOGCAT)
    ad.adb_logcat_file_path = logcat_path
    return ad


def _get_only_excerpt(ad):
    excerpt_dir = os.path.join(ad.log_path, 'AdbLogExcerpts')
    excerpt_names = os.listdir(excerpt_dir)
    assert len(excerpt_names) == 1
    return os.path.join(excerpt_dir, excerpt_names[0])


def test_cat_adb_log_uses_windows_safe_timestamp_in_filename(tmp_path):
    """The excerpt name must not contain the log timestamp's colons."""
    ad = _create_device_with_logcat(tmp_path)

    ad.cat_adb_log('some_test', MOCK_ADB_LOGCAT_BEGIN_TIME)

    excerpt_path = _get_only_excerpt(ad)
    excerpt_name = os.path.basename(excerpt_path)
    expected_name = 'some_test,02-29_14-02-20.123,%s,%s.txt' % (
        ad.model, ad.serial)

    assert ':' not in excerpt_name
    assert excerpt_name == expected_name

    # Sanitizing the filename must not change the timestamp used to find the
    # beginning of the excerpt in the original logcat output.
    with io.open(excerpt_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as excerpt_file:
        assert excerpt_file.read() == MOCK_ADB_LOGCAT_EXCERPT


def test_cat_adb_log_safe_filename_preserves_long_tag_truncation(tmp_path):
    """Normalizing the timestamp must not break filename length limiting."""
    ad = _create_device_with_logcat(tmp_path)
    # Use a smaller limit so truncation can be exercised on filesystems whose
    # actual name limit is lower than Mobly's platform-independent constant.
    max_filename_len = 80
    tag = 'long_test_' + ('x' * (max_filename_len + 50))

    with mock.patch.object(
            android_device.utils, 'MAX_FILENAME_LEN', max_filename_len):
        ad.cat_adb_log(tag, MOCK_ADB_LOGCAT_BEGIN_TIME)

    excerpt_path = _get_only_excerpt(ad)
    excerpt_name = os.path.basename(excerpt_path)
    suffix = ',02-29_14-02-20.123,%s,%s.txt' % (ad.model, ad.serial)
    expected_name = tag[:max_filename_len - len(suffix)] + suffix

    assert ':' not in excerpt_name
    assert excerpt_name == expected_name
    assert len(excerpt_name) == max_filename_len
    assert os.path.isfile(excerpt_path)

from __future__ import unicode_literals

import pytest

from clldutils.badge import badge


@pytest.mark.parametrize('url', [
    # Static badges, including a non-default format and shields.io options.
    'https://img.shields.io/badge/build-passing-brightgreen.png?style=flat-square',
    # Service-specific badges must be usable as well; their URL structure is
    # not limited to the static "badge/subject-status-color" form.
    'https://img.shields.io/travis/clld/clldutils.svg',
    'https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/clld/clldutils.svg?logo=github',
])
def test_badge_accepts_complete_shields_url(url):
    label = 'build status'
    assert badge(url, label) == '![{0}]({1} "{0}")'.format(label, url)


def test_badge_label_is_independent_of_url():
    url = 'https://img.shields.io/badge/cov-20%25-orange.svg?style=plastic'
    assert badge(url, 'coverage: 20%') == (
        '![coverage: 20%]'
        '(https://img.shields.io/badge/cov-20%25-orange.svg?style=plastic '
        '"coverage: 20%")'
    )


def test_badge_can_return_url_without_markdown():
    url = 'https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/clldutils.svg?style=plastic'
    assert badge(url, 'PyPI', markdown=False) == url


def test_badge_accepts_url_and_label_as_keyword_arguments():
    url = 'https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-passing-blue.svg'
    assert badge(url=url, label='documentation', markdown=False) == url


def test_badge_does_not_rewrite_or_restrict_the_url():
    # Accepting the complete URL keeps the helper independent of individual
    # shields.io endpoints and of present or future query parameters.
    url = (
        'https://img.shields.io/endpoint'
        '?url=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.org%2Fstatus.json&style=flat'
    )
    assert badge(url, '') == '![]({0} "")'.format(url)
    assert badge(url, 'status', markdown=False) == url

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


ISSUE_SQL = """
insert into newtable as t (a,b,c) values (1,2,3)
on conflict (c)
do update
   set a = t.a + 1
where
   t.a < 1
"""


def assert_postgres_roundtrip(statement: exp.Expression) -> str:
    """The generated SQL must retain the complete statement and remain parseable."""
    generated = statement.sql(dialect="postgres")
    reparsed = parse_one(generated, read="postgres")
    assert reparsed == statement
    return generated


def insert_target(statement: exp.Insert):
    """Return the target table and its INSERT column list.

    Depending on how the target is represented, the column list can be stored
    either on a Schema or on the TableAlias. Both representations preserve the
    same public SQL semantics.
    """
    target = statement.this

    if isinstance(target, exp.Schema):
        table = target.this
        columns = [column.name for column in target.expressions]
    else:
        table = target
        columns = table.alias_column_names if isinstance(table, exp.Table) else []

    assert isinstance(table, exp.Table)
    return table, columns


def test_issue_insert_target_alias_with_on_conflict_where():
    statement = parse_one(ISSUE_SQL, read="postgres")

    assert isinstance(statement, exp.Insert)
    table, columns = insert_target(statement)
    assert table.name == "newtable"
    assert table.alias == "t"
    assert columns == ["a", "b", "c"]

    # This is the public operation shown in the issue report.
    assert [table.name for table in statement.find_all(exp.Table)] == ["newtable"]

    conflict = statement.find(exp.OnConflict)
    assert conflict is not None
    assert [key.name for key in conflict.args["conflict_keys"]] == ["c"]

    assert len(conflict.expressions) == 1
    assignment = conflict.expressions[0]
    assert isinstance(assignment, exp.EQ)
    assert assignment.this.name == "a"
    assert isinstance(assignment.expression, exp.Add)
    assert assignment.expression.this.table == "t"
    assert assignment.expression.this.name == "a"

    # WHERE is part of DO UPDATE; it must not be mistaken for another clause or
    # silently discarded after parsing.
    where = conflict.args.get("where")
    assert isinstance(where, exp.LT)
    assert where.this.table == "t"
    assert where.this.name == "a"
    assert where.expression.name == "1"

    generated = assert_postgres_roundtrip(statement)
    assert "WHERE" in generated.upper()


def test_on_conflict_where_is_preserved_without_target_alias():
    # The issue explicitly notes that removing the alias already works. The
    # alias fix must not regress target names, insert columns, or the upsert.
    statement = parse_one(
        """
        INSERT INTO newtable (a, b, c) VALUES (1, 2, 3)
        ON CONFLICT (c)
        DO UPDATE SET a = newtable.a + 1
        WHERE newtable.a < 1
        """,
        read="postgres",
    )

    table, columns = insert_target(statement)
    assert table.name == "newtable"
    assert table.alias == ""
    assert columns == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert [table.name for table in statement.find_all(exp.Table)] == ["newtable"]

    conflict = statement.find(exp.OnConflict)
    assert conflict is not None
    where = conflict.args.get("where")
    assert isinstance(where, exp.LT)
    assert where.this.table == "newtable"

    generated = assert_postgres_roundtrip(statement)
    assert "WHERE" in generated.upper()


def test_insert_target_alias_without_column_list():
    statement = parse_one(
        """
        INSERT INTO newtable AS t VALUES (1, 2, 3)
        ON CONFLICT (c)
        DO UPDATE SET a = t.a + 1
        WHERE t.a < 1
        """,
        read="postgres",
    )

    table, columns = insert_target(statement)
    assert table.name == "newtable"
    assert table.alias == "t"
    assert columns == []

    conflict = statement.find(exp.OnConflict)
    assert conflict is not None
    assert isinstance(conflict.args.get("where"), exp.LT)
    assert_postgres_roundtrip(statement)


def test_aliased_upsert_with_multiple_assignments_compound_where_and_returning():
    statement = parse_one(
        """
        INSERT INTO products AS p (id, name, price)
        VALUES (1, 'Product', 10.0)
        ON CONFLICT (id)
        DO UPDATE SET
            name = p.name || '_updated',
            price = p.price * 1.1
        WHERE p.price > 5.0 AND p.name IS NOT NULL
        RETURNING id
        """,
        read="postgres",
    )

    table, columns = insert_target(statement)
    assert table.name == "products"
    assert table.alias == "p"
    assert columns == ["id", "name", "price"]

    conflict = statement.find(exp.OnConflict)
    assert conflict is not None
    assert len(conflict.expressions) == 2
    assert isinstance(conflict.args.get("where"), exp.And)
    assert isinstance(statement.args.get("returning"), exp.Returning)

    generated = assert_postgres_roundtrip(statement)
    assert "WHERE" in generated.upper()
    assert "RETURNING" in generated.upper()


def test_aliased_insert_on_conflict_do_nothing_still_roundtrips():
    statement = parse_one(
        """
        INSERT INTO newtable AS t (a, b, c) VALUES (1, 2, 3)
        ON CONFLICT (c) DO NOTHING
        """,
        read="postgres",
    )

    table, columns = insert_target(statement)
    assert table.name == "newtable"
    assert table.alias == "t"
    assert columns == ["a", "b", "c"]

    conflict = statement.find(exp.OnConflict)
    assert conflict is not None
    assert conflict.expressions == []
    assert conflict.args.get("where") is None

    generated = assert_postgres_roundtrip(statement)
    assert "DO NOTHING" in generated.upper()
    assert "WHERE" not in generated.upper()

from pyupgrade import _fix_py3_plus
from pyupgrade import main


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('source', 'expected'),
    (
        # The assignment and its line should be removed.
        ('__metaclass__ = type\n', ''),
        ('__metaclass__ = type', ''),
        ('__metaclass__ = type\nx = 1\n', 'x = 1\n'),

        # Whitespace and a trailing comment are part of the removed statement.
        (
            '__metaclass__  =  type  # python 2 compatibility\n'
            'x = 1\n',
            'x = 1\n',
        ),

        # Surrounding statements must be preserved.
        (
            'x = 1\n'
            '__metaclass__ = type\n'
            'y = 2\n',
            'x = 1\n'
            'y = 2\n',
        ),
        (
            '__metaclass__ = type\n'
            'x = 1\n'
            '__metaclass__=type\n',
            'x = 1\n',
        ),
        (
            '"""module docstring"""\n'
            '# compatibility declaration follows\n'
            '__metaclass__ = type\n'
            'class C:\n'
            '    pass\n',
            '"""module docstring"""\n'
            '# compatibility declaration follows\n'
            'class C:\n'
            '    pass\n',
        ),

        # Visiting an earlier function must not prevent a later module-level
        # assignment from being removed.
        (
            'def f():\n'
            '    return 1\n'
            '__metaclass__ = type\n'
            'x = 1\n',
            'def f():\n'
            '    return 1\n'
            'x = 1\n',
        ),
    ),
)
def test_py3_plus_removes_module_level_metaclass_type(source, expected):
    assert _fix_py3_plus(source) == expected
    # Rewriting must be idempotent.
    assert _fix_py3_plus(expected) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    'source',
    (
        # Class scope is not module scope.
        'class C:\n'
        '    __metaclass__ = type\n',
        'class Outer:\n'
        '    class Inner:\n'
        '        __metaclass__ = type\n',

        # Function scope is not module scope.
        'def f():\n'
        '    __metaclass__ = type\n',
        'async def f():\n'
        '    __metaclass__ = type\n',

        # In particular, returning from a nested function must not make the
        # rest of the outer function look like module scope.
        'def outer():\n'
        '    def inner():\n'
        '        return 1\n'
        '    __metaclass__ = type\n'
        '    return inner\n',

        # Only the exact, side-effect-free `__metaclass__ = type` assignment
        # is redundant.
        '__metaclass__ = object\n',
        '__metaclass__ = Type\n',
        '__metaclass__ = type()\n',
        '__metaclass__ = type or object\n',
        'metaclass = type\n',
        'obj.__metaclass__ = type\n',

        # Removing these whole statements would also remove another assignment.
        'x = __metaclass__ = type\n',
        '__metaclass__ = x = type\n',
    ),
)
def test_py3_plus_metaclass_type_noop(source):
    assert _fix_py3_plus(source) == source


def test_metaclass_removal_requires_py3_plus(tmp_path):

    source = '__metaclass__ = type\nx = 1\n'
    path.write_text(source)

    assert main((str(path),)) == 0
    assert path.read_text() == source

    assert main(('--py3-plus', str(path))) == 1
    assert path.read_text() == 'x = 1\n'

import asyncio
import subprocess
import sys
import textwrap

import pytest

from anyio.to_thread import run_sync


def _run_in_subprocess(source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    """Run a reproduction with a hard timeout so a regression cannot hang pytest."""
    try:
        return subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-c", textwrap.dedent(source)],
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
            universal_newlines=True,
            timeout=15,
        )
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        pytest.fail(
            "run_sync() hung when successive top-level awaits were executed "
            "with run_until_complete()"
        )


def test_run_sync_in_successive_top_level_awaits() -> None:
    """
    IPython runs every top-level await in a new task on the same event loop.

    Finishing one of those tasks must not prevent later calls to run_sync()
    from completing.
    """
    completed = _run_in_subprocess(
        """
        import asyncio

        from anyio.to_thread import run_sync


        def identity(value):
            return value


        loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
        asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)
        try:
            for value in range(3):
                result = loop.run_until_complete(run_sync(identity, value))
                assert result == value, (result, value)
        finally:
            loop.close()
            asyncio.set_event_loop(None)

        print("all top-level awaits completed")
        """
    )

    assert completed.returncode == 0, completed.stdout + completed.stderr
    assert "all top-level awaits completed" in completed.stdout


def test_run_sync_in_top_level_await_after_worker_exception() -> None:
    """A failed top-level await must not poison worker threads for the next one."""
    completed = _run_in_subprocess(
        """
        import asyncio

        from anyio.to_thread import run_sync


        def fail():
            raise ValueError("expected failure")


        loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
        asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)
        try:
            try:
                loop.run_until_complete(run_sync(fail))
            except ValueError as exc:
                assert str(exc) == "expected failure"
            else:
                raise AssertionError("the worker exception was not propagated")

            result = loop.run_until_complete(run_sync(lambda: "after failure"))
            assert result == "after failure", result
        finally:
            loop.close()
            asyncio.set_event_loop(None)

        print("call after exception completed")
        """
    )

    assert completed.returncode == 0, completed.stdout + completed.stderr
    assert "call after exception completed" in completed.stdout


def test_run_sync_does_not_reuse_a_finished_root_task() -> None:
    """
    Regression test for the state left behind by an IPython-style await.

    A finished task from a previous run_until_complete() cannot manage the
    lifetime of workers used by a later top-level await. Checking this before
    the second run_sync() also makes a broken implementation fail rather than
    leaving this test itself hanging.
    """
    from anyio._backends._asyncio import find_root_task

    loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
    asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)
    try:
        async def first_top_level_await() -> asyncio.Task:
            root_task = find_root_task()
            assert root_task is asyncio.current_task()
            assert await run_sync(lambda: "first") == "first"
            return root_task

        first_root_task = loop.run_until_complete(first_top_level_await())
        assert first_root_task.done()

        async def second_top_level_await() -> str:
            assert find_root_task() is asyncio.current_task()
            assert find_root_task() is not first_root_task
            return await run_sync(lambda: "second")

        assert loop.run_until_complete(second_top_level_await()) == "second"
    finally:
        loop.close()
        asyncio.set_event_loop(None)

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp


ORIGINAL_ISSUE_SQL = (
    "select art from table1 inner join lateral "
    "(select art from table2) table2 on table2.art=table2.art"
)


def assert_postgres_round_trip(sql, expected):
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="postgres")
    generated = expression.sql(dialect="postgres")

    assert generated == expected
    reparsed = sqlglot.parse_one(generated, read="postgres")
    assert reparsed.sql(dialect="postgres") == expected

    return expression


def test_original_lateral_subquery_issue():
    expression = assert_postgres_round_trip(
        ORIGINAL_ISSUE_SQL,
        "SELECT art FROM table1 INNER JOIN LATERAL "
        "(SELECT art FROM table2) table2 ON table2.art = table2.art",
    )

    joins = expression.args.get("joins")
    assert joins is not None and len(joins) == 1

    lateral = joins[0].this
    assert isinstance(lateral, exp.Lateral)
    assert lateral.find(exp.Select) is not None
    assert joins[0].args.get("on") is not None

    aliases = [alias.name for alias in lateral.find_all(exp.TableAlias)]
    assert aliases == ["table2"]

"""Regression tests for PostgreSQL's postfix ISNULL and NOTNULL operators."""

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


ISSUE_QUERY = """
SELECT datasets.a,
       id AS history_id,
       app_users.id AS user_id,
       companies.name AS companyname,
       app_users.email AS email,
       app_users.group_id AS group_id
FROM datasets
JOIN companies ON datasets.companyid = companies.companyid
JOIN app_users USING (short_user_id)
WHERE (datasets.companyid = '405')
AND (mmh_trip_start NOTNULL)
"""


@pytest.mark.parametrize("read", [None, "postgres"])
def test_issue_query_is_equivalent_to_is_not_null(read):
    actual = parse_one(ISSUE_QUERY, read=read)
    expected = parse_one(
        ISSUE_QUERY.replace("mmh_trip_start NOTNULL", "mmh_trip_start IS NOT NULL"),
        read=read,
    )

    assert actual == expected
    assert actual.sql() == expected.sql()


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("postfix_expression", "standard_expression"),
    [
        ("a NOTNULL", "a IS NOT NULL"),
        ("a notnull", "a IS NOT NULL"),
        ("a NoTnUlL", "a IS NOT NULL"),
        ("a ISNULL", "a IS NULL"),
        ("a isnull", "a IS NULL"),
        ("datasets.a NOTNULL", "datasets.a IS NOT NULL"),
        ("(a + 1) NOTNULL", "(a + 1) IS NOT NULL"),
        ("(a + 1) ISNULL", "(a + 1) IS NULL"),
        ("COALESCE(a, b) NOTNULL", "COALESCE(a, b) IS NOT NULL"),
        ("COALESCE(a, b) ISNULL", "COALESCE(a, b) IS NULL"),
    ],
)
def test_postfix_null_operators_in_expressions(postfix_expression, standard_expression):
    actual = parse_one(f"SELECT {postfix_expression} AS predicate FROM datasets")
    expected = parse_one(f"SELECT {standard_expression} AS predicate FROM datasets")

    assert actual == expected


def test_notnull_builds_a_negated_null_check():
    predicate = parse_one(
        "SELECT * FROM datasets WHERE mmh_trip_start NOTNULL"
    ).args["where"].this

    assert isinstance(predicate, exp.Not)
    assert isinstance(predicate.this, exp.Is)
    assert predicate.this.this.sql() == "mmh_trip_start"
    assert isinstance(predicate.this.args["expression"], exp.Null)


def test_isnull_builds_a_null_check():
    predicate = parse_one(
        "SELECT * FROM datasets WHERE mmh_trip_start ISNULL"
    ).args["where"].this

    assert isinstance(predicate, exp.Is)
    assert predicate.this.sql() == "mmh_trip_start"
    assert isinstance(predicate.args["expression"], exp.Null)


def test_postfix_null_operators_combine_with_boolean_conditions():
    actual = parse_one(
        "SELECT * FROM datasets "
        "WHERE a ISNULL AND (b NOTNULL OR c NOTNULL)"
    )
    expected = parse_one(
        "SELECT * FROM datasets "
        "WHERE a IS NULL AND (b IS NOT NULL OR c IS NOT NULL)"
    )

    assert actual == expected


def test_notnull_remains_usable_as_a_column_name():
    # PostgreSQL treats NOTNULL as nonreserved, just like ISNULL. Supporting the
    # postfix operator must not make an existing column name unparseable.
    assert (
        parse_one("SELECT notnull FROM datasets").sql()
        == "SELECT notnull FROM datasets"
    )


def test_notnull_remains_usable_as_an_alias():
    assert (
        parse_one("SELECT a AS notnull FROM datasets").sql()
        == "SELECT a AS notnull FROM datasets"
    )

"""Regression tests for EOF and cancellation during SMTP command handlers."""

import asyncio
import socket
import threading
import unittest

from aiosmtpd.controller import Controller
from aiosmtpd.smtp import SMTP as Server
from smtplib import SMTP
from unittest.mock import Mock


class BlockingProtocolRCPTHandler:
    """An RCPT handler whose cancellation can be observed deterministically."""

    def __init__(self, loop):
        self.started = loop.create_future()
        self.blocker = loop.create_future()
        self.cancelled = False
        self.exceptions = []

    async def handle_RCPT(self, server, session, envelope, address, options):
        self.started.set_result(None)
        try:
            await self.blocker
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            self.cancelled = True
            raise

    async def handle_exception(self, error):
        self.exceptions.append(error)
        return "500 command exception was handled"


class BlockingSocketRCPTHandler:
    """Thread-safe observations for a handler running in Controller's thread."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.started = threading.Event()
        self.cancelled = threading.Event()
        self.exceptions = []

    async def handle_RCPT(self, server, session, envelope, address, options):
        self.started.set()
        try:
            await asyncio.sleep(30)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            self.cancelled.set()
            raise
        envelope.rcpt_tos.append(address)
        return "250 OK"

    async def handle_exception(self, error):
        self.exceptions.append(error)
        return "500 command exception was handled"


class SuccessfulRCPTHandler:
    def __init__(self):
        self.addresses = []

    async def handle_RCPT(self, server, session, envelope, address, options):
        # A delay must not, by itself, prevent normal completion of a command.
        await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
        envelope.rcpt_tos.append(address)
        self.addresses.append(address)
        return "250 OK"


class FailingRCPTHandler:
    def __init__(self):
        self.exceptions = []

    async def handle_RCPT(self, server, session, envelope, address, options):
        raise ValueError("RCPT failed")

    async def handle_exception(self, error):
        self.exceptions.append(error)
        return "451 temporary failure"


class TestCancellationAtProtocolLevel(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        try:
            self.old_loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
        except RuntimeError:
            self.old_loop = None
        self.loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
        asyncio.set_event_loop(self.loop)
        self.responses = []
        self.transport = Mock()
        self.transport.write = self.responses.append
        self.protocol = None

    def tearDown(self):
        if self.protocol is not None:
            task = self.protocol._handler_coroutine
            # Also make cleanup terminate promptly on a broken implementation
            # which catches cancellation and spins on EOF.
            if self.protocol.transport is not None:
                self.protocol.connection_lost(None)
            if not task.done():
                task.cancel()
                try:
                    self.loop.run_until_complete(task)
                except BaseException:
                    pass
        self.loop.close()
        asyncio.set_event_loop(self.old_loop)

    def test_eof_during_rcpt_is_not_an_smtp_command_error(self):
        handler = BlockingProtocolRCPTHandler(self.loop)
        self.protocol = Server(handler, loop=self.loop)
        self.protocol.connection_made(self.transport)

        # Include commands after RCPT, as in the netcat reproduction.  None of
        # them may be processed after EOF cancels the in-progress RCPT command.
        self.protocol.data_received(b"\r\n".join([
            b"HELO example.com",
            b"MAIL FROM: <anne@example.com>",
            b"RCPT TO: <bart@example.com>",
            b"DATA",
            b"test",
            b".",
            b"",
        ]))
        self.loop.run_until_complete(
            asyncio.wait_for(handler.started, timeout=1))

        self.protocol.eof_received()
        task = self.protocol._handler_coroutine
        done, pending = self.loop.run_until_complete(
            asyncio.wait([task], timeout=0.5))

        self.assertIn(
            task, done,
            "EOF left the command loop running; it can spin on empty lines")
        self.assertTrue(handler.cancelled)
        self.assertEqual(
            handler.exceptions, [],
            "CancelledError must not be reported as a handler failure")

        # Only the greeting, HELO, and MAIL responses are valid.  In
        # particular, there must be no 500 response for cancellation and no
        # responses to the pipelined commands following the aborted RCPT.
        self.assertEqual(len(self.responses), 3)
        self.assertTrue(self.responses[0].startswith(b"220 "))
        self.assertTrue(self.responses[1].startswith(b"250 "))
        self.assertEqual(self.responses[2], b"250 OK\r\n")


class TestCancellationThroughController(unittest.TestCase):
    def start_controller(self, handler):
        controller = Controller(handler, hostname="127.0.0.1", port=0)
        controller.start()
        self.addCleanup(controller.stop)
        port = controller.server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]
        return controller, port

    def test_disconnect_does_not_spam_errors_and_server_survives(self):
        handler = BlockingSocketRCPTHandler()
        controller, port = self.start_controller(handler)

        with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port), timeout=2) as client:
            client.settimeout(2)
            with client.makefile("rb") as reader:
                self.assertTrue(reader.readline().startswith(b"220 "))

                client.sendall(b"HELO example.com\r\n")
                self.assertTrue(reader.readline().startswith(b"250 "))
                client.sendall(b"MAIL FROM: <anne@example.com>\r\n")
                self.assertEqual(reader.readline(), b"250 OK\r\n")

                client.sendall(b"RCPT TO: <bart@example.com>\r\n")
                self.assertTrue(
                    handler.started.wait(2),
                    "the RCPT handler was never entered")

                # Reproduce a client which pipelines more input and then sends
                # EOF without waiting for the RCPT response or sending QUIT.
                client.sendall(b"DATA\r\ntest\r\n.\r\n")
                client.shutdown(socket.SHUT_WR)

                self.assertTrue(
                    handler.cancelled.wait(2),
                    "EOF did not cancel the in-progress RCPT handler")

                # A server may close its half of the connection or leave it
                # half-open, but it must not emit cancellation errors or spin
                # producing '500 Error: bad syntax' responses.
                client.settimeout(0.25)
                try:
                    unexpected = reader.readline()
                except socket.timeout:
                    unexpected = None
                self.assertIn(unexpected, (None, b""))
                self.assertEqual(handler.exceptions, [])

        # The aborted session must not cancel or otherwise destabilize the
        # server's event loop; a fresh client still gets normal service.
        with SMTP("127.0.0.1", port, timeout=2) as client:
            self.assertEqual(client.helo("survivor.example.com")[0], 250)
            self.assertEqual(client.noop()[0], 250)

    def test_slow_rcpt_can_still_complete_normally(self):
        handler = SuccessfulRCPTHandler()
        controller, port = self.start_controller(handler)

        with SMTP("127.0.0.1", port, timeout=2) as client:
            self.assertEqual(client.helo("example.com")[0], 250)
            self.assertEqual(client.mail("anne@example.com")[0], 250)
            code, response = client.rcpt("bart@example.com")
            self.assertEqual((code, response), (250, b"OK"))
            self.assertEqual(client.data(b"test\r\n")[0], 250)

        self.assertEqual(handler.addresses, ["bart@example.com"])

    def test_regular_handler_exception_is_still_reported(self):
        # Cancellation needs special treatment, but genuine command failures
        # must continue through handle_exception and leave the session usable.
        handler = FailingRCPTHandler()
        controller, port = self.start_controller(handler)

        with SMTP("127.0.0.1", port, timeout=2) as client:
            client.helo("example.com")
            client.mail("anne@example.com")
            code, response = client.rcpt("bart@example.com")
            self.assertEqual((code, response), (451, b"temporary failure"))
            self.assertEqual(client.noop()[0], 250)

        self.assertEqual(len(handler.exceptions), 1)
        self.assertIsInstance(handler.exceptions[0], ValueError)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import pytest
from mock import Mock

from alarmdecoder import AlarmDecoder
from alarmdecoder.devices import USBDevice
from alarmdecoder.event.event import Event, EventHandler
from alarmdecoder.messages import Message
from alarmdecoder.panels import ADEMCO
from alarmdecoder.zonetracking import Zone, Zonetracker


FAULT_1 = (
    '[00000000000000000A--],001,[f707000600e5800c0c020000],'
    '"FAULT 1                         "'
)
COMM_FAILURE = (
    '[00000001000000000A--],0fc,[f704009f10fc000008020000000000],'
    '"COMM. FAILURE                   "'
)
CHECK_103 = (
    '[00000001000000100A--],0bf,[f704009f10bf000208020000000000],'
    '"CHECK 103 LngRngRadio       0000"'
)
READY = (
    '[10000000000000000A--],000,[f707000600e5800c0c020000],'
    '"                                "'
)


def make_check_message(text):
    """Build an ECP/communicator CHECK message whose numeric code is 191."""
    return Message(
        '[00000001000000100A--],0bf,'
        '[f704009f10bf000208020000000000],"{}"'.format(text.ljust(32))
    )


@pytest.fixture
def zone_tracker():
    alarmdecoder = Mock(spec=AlarmDecoder)
    alarmdecoder.mode = ADEMCO
    return Zonetracker(alarmdecoder)


def test_issue_message_sequence_does_not_mix_string_and_integer_zones(zone_tracker):
    # An ordinary fault supplies the integer zone that used to make sorting
    # fail when the subsequent CHECK message added its zone as a string.
    zone_tracker.update(Message(FAULT_1))
    zone_tracker.update(Message(COMM_FAILURE))

    # COMM. FAILURE is not itself a zone fault.
    assert zone_tracker.faulted == [1]
    assert set(zone_tracker.zones) == {1}

    # This update previously raised TypeError while sorting [1, '103'].
    zone_tracker.update(Message(CHECK_103))

    assert zone_tracker.faulted == [1, 103]
    assert set(zone_tracker.zones) == {1, 103}
    assert all(isinstance(zone, int) for zone in zone_tracker.faulted)
    assert zone_tracker.zones[1].status == Zone.FAULT
    assert zone_tracker.zones[103].status == Zone.CHECK
    assert zone_tracker.zones[103].zone == 103


def test_ecp_check_zones_are_sorted_numerically(zone_tracker):
    zone_tracker.update(make_check_message('CHECK 103 LngRngRadio       0000'))
    zone_tracker.update(make_check_message('CHECK 9 LngRngRadio'))
    zone_tracker.update(make_check_message('CHECK 20 LngRngRadio'))

    # Numeric zone identifiers also avoid lexicographic ordering such as
    # ['103', '20', '9'].
    assert zone_tracker.faulted == [9, 20, 103]
    assert set(zone_tracker.zones) == {9, 20, 103}
    assert all(zone.status == Zone.CHECK for zone in zone_tracker.zones.values())


def test_repeated_ecp_check_updates_one_zone_and_can_be_restored(zone_tracker):
    fault_events = []
    restore_events = []

    def on_fault(sender, *args, **kwargs):
        fault_events.append(kwargs['zone'])

    def on_restore(sender, *args, **kwargs):
        restore_events.append(kwargs['zone'])

    zone_tracker.on_fault += on_fault
    zone_tracker.on_restore += on_restore

    zone_tracker.update(Message(CHECK_103))
    zone_tracker.update(Message(CHECK_103))

    assert zone_tracker.faulted == [103]
    assert set(zone_tracker.zones) == {103}
    assert fault_events == [103]

    zone_tracker.update(Message(READY))

    assert zone_tracker.faulted == []
    assert zone_tracker.zones[103].status == Zone.CLEAR
    assert restore_events == [103]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    'text',
    [
        'CHECK',
        'CHECK A',
        'CHECK SYSTEM FAILURE',
    ],
)
def test_ecp_check_without_numeric_zone_is_ignored(zone_tracker, text):
    # A communicator failure must not create a bogus zone 191 or raise while
    # trying to extract a zone number that is not present.
    zone_tracker.update(make_check_message(text))

    assert zone_tracker.faulted == []
    assert zone_tracker.zones == {}


def test_issue_sequence_through_alarmdecoder_emits_integer_zone():
    device = Mock(spec=USBDevice)
    device.on_open = EventHandler(Event(), device)
    device.on_close = EventHandler(Event(), device)
    device.on_read = EventHandler(Event(), device)
    device.on_write = EventHandler(Event(), device)

    decoder = AlarmDecoder(device, ignore_lrr_states=False)
    decoder.address_mask = int('ffffffff', 16)

    fault_events = []

    def on_zone_fault(sender, *args, **kwargs):
        fault_events.append(kwargs['zone'])

    decoder.on_zone_fault += on_zone_fault
    decoder.open()

    decoder._handle_message(FAULT_1.encode('ascii'))
    decoder._handle_message(COMM_FAILURE.encode('ascii'))
    message = decoder._handle_message(CHECK_103.encode('ascii'))

    assert isinstance(message, Message)
    assert fault_events == [1, 103]
    assert all(isinstance(zone, int) for zone in fault_events)

import pytest

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


SPARK_DIALECTS = ["spark2", "spark", "databricks"]


def _parse_single_select(sql: str, dialect: str) -> exp.Select:
    statement = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read=dialect)
    assert isinstance(statement, exp.Select)
    assert len(statement.expressions) == 1
    return statement


@pytest.mark.parametrize("dialect", SPARK_DIALECTS)
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("literal", "expected"),
    [
        ("r'([^0-9])'", "([^0-9])"),
        (r"r'\d+\s*'", r"\d+\s*"),
        (r"r'\n\t'", r"\n\t"),
        (r"r'\\d'", r"\\d"),
        (r'R"\d+"', r"\d+"),
        ("R\"it's\"", "it's"),
        ("r''", ""),
    ],
)
def test_spark_raw_strings_preserve_contents(dialect, literal, expected):
    statement = _parse_single_select(f"SELECT {literal}", dialect)
    parsed = statement.expressions[0]

    assert isinstance(parsed, exp.RawString)
    assert parsed.this == expected

    # Generation may use either a raw literal or an equivalent escaped ordinary
    # literal. In both cases, it must remain valid and retain the exact value.
    generated = statement.sql(dialect=dialect)
    reparsed_statement = _parse_single_select(generated, dialect)
    reparsed = reparsed_statement.expressions[0]

    assert isinstance(reparsed, (exp.Literal, exp.RawString))
    assert reparsed.this == expected


def test_databricks_raw_string_in_regexp_replace():
    sql = """select regexp_replace('100-200', r'([^0-9])', '')"""
    statement = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="databricks")

    regexp_replace = statement.find(exp.RegexpReplace)
    assert regexp_replace is not None

    pattern = regexp_replace.expression
    assert isinstance(pattern, exp.RawString)
    assert pattern.this == "([^0-9])"

    generated = statement.sql(dialect="databricks")
    reparsed = sqlglot.parse_one(generated, read="databricks")
    reparsed_regexp_replace = reparsed.find(exp.RegexpReplace)

    assert reparsed_regexp_replace is not None
    assert reparsed_regexp_replace.expression.this == "([^0-9])"

# coding: utf8
from __future__ import unicode_literals

import pytest

from clldutils.badge import badge, Colors


BADGE_URL = 'https://img.shields.io/badge/cov-20%25-orange.svg'


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    'kw,alt,title',
    [
        ({}, 'cov: 20%', 'cov: 20%'),
        ({'label': 'coverage'}, 'coverage', 'coverage'),
        ({'title': 'Coverage report'}, 'cov: 20%', 'Coverage report'),
        (
            {'label': 'coverage', 'title': 'Coverage report'},
            'coverage',
            'Coverage report',
        ),
    ],
)
def test_badge_markdown_label_and_title_are_configurable(kw, alt, title):
    """The alt label and title are independent parts of the markdown image."""
    assert badge('cov', '20%', Colors.orange, **kw) == \
        '![{0}]({1} "{2}")'.format(alt, BADGE_URL, title)


def test_badge_markdown_only_parts_do_not_leak_into_the_url():
    """Markdown label/title arguments are not shields.io query parameters."""
    assert badge(
        'cov',
        '20%',
        Colors.orange,
        markdown=False,
        label='coverage',
        title='Coverage report',
    ) == BADGE_URL


def test_badge_custom_label_can_be_combined_with_shields_query_options():
    """Other keyword arguments must still be passed to shields.io."""
    assert badge(
        'cov',
        '20%',
        Colors.orange,
        label='coverage',
        style='flat-square',
    ) == (
        '![coverage](https://img.shields.io/badge/cov-20%25-orange.svg'
        '?style=flat-square "coverage")'
    )


def test_badge_positional_format_and_markdown_arguments_remain_supported():
    """Adding flexibility must not break the original public calling convention."""
    assert badge('cov', '20%', Colors.orange, 'png', False) == \
        'https://img.shields.io/badge/cov-20%25-orange.png'


def test_badge_keyword_arguments_remain_supported():
    """The original arguments can also be supplied entirely by keyword."""
    assert badge(
        subject='cov',
        status='20%',
        color=Colors.orange,
        fmt='png',
        markdown=False,
    ) == 'https://img.shields.io/badge/cov-20%25-orange.png'


def test_badge_mixed_positional_and_keyword_arguments_remain_supported():
    """A required argument may still follow positional arguments as a keyword."""
    assert badge('cov', '20%', color=Colors.orange, markdown=False) == BADGE_URL

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


ISSUE_QUERY = """
SELECT datasets.a,
       id AS history_id,
       app_users.id AS user_id,
       companies.name AS companyname,
       app_users.email AS email,
       app_users.group_id AS group_id
FROM datasets
JOIN companies ON datasets.companyid = companies.companyid
JOIN app_users USING (short_user_id)
WHERE (datasets.companyid = '405')
  AND (mmh_trip_start NOTNULL)
"""


def test_notnull_in_issue_query_is_equivalent_to_is_not_null():
    expression = parse_one(ISSUE_QUERY)
    expected = parse_one(ISSUE_QUERY.replace("NOTNULL", "IS NOT NULL"))

    assert expression == expected
    assert expression.sql() == expected.sql()

    # NOTNULL must produce a negated NULL test, rather than an alias, function
    # call, or some other expression that merely happens to parse.
    negation = expression.find(exp.Not)
    assert negation is not None

    null_test = negation.this
    assert isinstance(null_test, exp.Is)
    assert isinstance(null_test.this, exp.Column)
    assert null_test.this.sql() == "mmh_trip_start"
    assert isinstance(null_test.args["expression"], exp.Null)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "operator, standard_operator, expected_predicate",
    [
        ("NOTNULL", "IS NOT NULL", "NOT col IS NULL"),
        ("notnull", "IS NOT NULL", "NOT col IS NULL"),
        ("NoTnUlL", "IS NOT NULL", "NOT col IS NULL"),
        ("ISNULL", "IS NULL", "col IS NULL"),
        ("isnull", "IS NULL", "col IS NULL"),
    ],
)
def test_postfix_null_operators(operator, standard_operator, expected_predicate):
    expression = parse_one(f"SELECT * FROM t WHERE col {operator}")
    expected = parse_one(f"SELECT * FROM t WHERE col {standard_operator}")

    assert expression == expected
    assert expression.sql() == f"SELECT * FROM t WHERE {expected_predicate}"

    # The normalized SQL must remain parseable and retain the same meaning.
    assert parse_one(expression.sql()) == expression


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql, standard_sql",
    [
        (
            "SELECT * FROM t WHERE (a ISNULL) AND (b NOTNULL)",
            "SELECT * FROM t WHERE (a IS NULL) AND (b IS NOT NULL)",
        ),
        (
            "SELECT * FROM t WHERE (a + b) NOTNULL",
            "SELECT * FROM t WHERE (a + b) IS NOT NULL",

        ),

        ),
        (
            "SELECT * FROM t WHERE a NOTNULL AND b = 1",
            "SELECT * FROM t WHERE a IS NOT NULL AND b = 1",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_postfix_null_operators_in_larger_expressions(sql, standard_sql):
    expression = parse_one(sql)
    expected = parse_one(standard_sql)

    assert expression == expected
    assert expression.sql() == expected.sql()
