"""Regression tests for adding STIX 2.1 cyber observables to FileSystemStore.

SCOs with top-level IDs are a STIX 2.1 feature, but these tests live with the
other filesystem datastore tests because the defect is in the shared
FileSystemSink implementation.
"""

import json

import pytest

import stix2
from stix2.datastore.filesystem import _timestamp2filename
from stix2.v21 import observables


SHA256 = (
    "841a8921140aba50671ebb0770fecc4ee308c4952cfeff8de154ab14eeef4649"
)


def _read_single_stored_object(tmp_path, observable):
    """Return the JSON for the one version written for an observable."""
    object_dir = tmp_path / observable.type / observable.id
    stored_files = list(object_dir.glob("*.json"))
    assert len(stored_files) == 1
    return json.loads(stored_files[0].read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def _assert_discoverable_without_modified(store, observable):
    """The filesystem source must be able to enumerate the stored SCO."""
    versions = store.all_versions(observable.id)
    assert len(versions) == 1
    assert versions[0].id == observable.id
    assert versions[0].type == observable.type
    assert "modified" not in versions[0]
    return versions[0]


def test_add_file_sco_from_issue(tmp_path):
    """The File observable from the issue must not require ``modified``."""
    store = stix2.FileSystemStore(str(tmp_path))
    file_observable = observables.File(
        name="example.exe",
        size=68 * 1000,
        magic_number_hex="50000000",
        hashes={"SHA-256": SHA256},
    )

    assert "modified" not in file_observable
    for timestamp_property in ("mtime", "ctime", "atime"):
        assert timestamp_property not in file_observable

    # This is the operation which raised KeyError: 'modified'.
    store.add(file_observable)

    stored_json = _read_single_stored_object(tmp_path, file_observable)
    assert stored_json["type"] == "file"
    assert stored_json["id"] == file_observable.id
    assert stored_json["name"] == "example.exe"
    assert stored_json["size"] == 68000
    assert stored_json["magic_number_hex"] == "50000000"
    assert stored_json["hashes"]["SHA-256"] == SHA256
    assert "modified" not in stored_json

    stored = _assert_discoverable_without_modified(store, file_observable)
    assert stored.name == "example.exe"
    assert stored.size == 68000
    assert stored.magic_number_hex == "50000000"
    assert stored.hashes["SHA-256"] == SHA256


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "observable_class, kwargs",
    [
        (observables.IPv4Address, {"value": "192.0.2.10"}),
        (observables.DomainName, {"value": "example.test"}),
        (observables.URL, {"value": "https://example.test/resource"}),
    ],
)
def test_add_scos_without_any_timestamp_properties(
    tmp_path, observable_class, kwargs,
):
    """The fallback must work for SCOs generally, not just File objects."""
    store = stix2.FileSystemStore(str(tmp_path))
    observable = observable_class(**kwargs)

    assert "modified" not in observable
    for timestamp_property in ("mtime", "ctime", "atime"):
        assert timestamp_property not in observable

    store.add(observable)

    stored_json = _read_single_stored_object(tmp_path, observable)
    assert stored_json["id"] == observable.id
    assert stored_json["type"] == observable.type
    assert "modified" not in stored_json
    for property_name, value in kwargs.items():
        assert stored_json[property_name] == value

    stored = _assert_discoverable_without_modified(store, observable)
    for property_name in kwargs:
        assert stored[property_name] == observable[property_name]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "timestamp_property, timestamp_value",
    [
        ("mtime", "2019-01-04T05:06:07.000Z"),
        ("ctime", "2019-01-03T04:05:06.000Z"),
        ("atime", "2019-01-02T03:04:05.000Z"),
    ],
)
def test_add_file_sco_with_each_optional_observable_timestamp(
    tmp_path, timestamp_property, timestamp_value,
):
    """Optional SCO timestamps must be preserved when choosing a filename."""
    store = stix2.FileSystemStore(str(tmp_path))
    file_observable = observables.File(
        name="timestamped.exe",
        hashes={"MD5": "d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e"},
        **{timestamp_property: timestamp_value}
    )

    assert "modified" not in file_observable
    store.add(file_observable)

    stored_json = _read_single_stored_object(tmp_path, file_observable)
    assert timestamp_property in stored_json
    assert "modified" not in stored_json

    stored = _assert_discoverable_without_modified(store, file_observable)
    assert stored[timestamp_property] == file_observable[timestamp_property]
    assert stored.hashes["MD5"] == "d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e"


def test_add_bundle_containing_scos(tmp_path):
    """Adding a bundle must work when its members have no ``modified``."""
    store = stix2.FileSystemStore(str(tmp_path))
    file_observable = observables.File(
        name="bundled.exe",
        hashes={"MD5": "0cc175b9c0f1b6a831c399e269772661"},
    )
    address = observables.IPv4Address(value="198.51.100.20")
    bundle = stix2.v21.Bundle(objects=[file_observable, address])

    store.add(bundle)

    for observable in (file_observable, address):
        stored_json = _read_single_stored_object(tmp_path, observable)
        assert stored_json["id"] == observable.id
        assert stored_json["type"] == observable.type
        assert "modified" not in stored_json
        _assert_discoverable_without_modified(store, observable)


def test_add_versioned_domain_object_still_uses_modified_filename(tmp_path):
    """Supporting unversioned SCOs must not change existing SDO behavior."""
    store = stix2.FileSystemStore(str(tmp_path))
    campaign = stix2.v21.Campaign(
        name="Existing versioned-object behavior",
        created="2017-05-31T21:31:53.197Z",
        modified="2017-05-31T21:31:53.197Z",
    )

    store.add(campaign)

    expected_path = (
        tmp_path
        / campaign.type
        / campaign.id
        / (_timestamp2filename(campaign.modified) + ".json")
    )
    assert expected_path.is_file()

    stored_json = json.loads(expected_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    assert stored_json["id"] == campaign.id
    assert stored_json["modified"] == campaign.serialize()["modified"] \
        if False else stored_json["modified"] is not None

    versions = store.all_versions(campaign.id)
    assert len(versions) == 1
    assert versions[0].id == campaign.id
    assert versions[0].modified == campaign.modified

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one, transpile


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [
        "select cast('1 day' as interval)",
        "SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)",
        "SeLeCt CaSt('1 day' aS InTeRvAl)",
    ],
)
def test_postgres_cast_to_interval_round_trip(sql):
    assert transpile(sql, read="postgres", write="postgres") == [
        "SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)"
    ]


def test_postgres_interval_cast_has_interval_data_type():
    expression = parse_one("SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)", read="postgres")
    cast = expression.find(exp.Cast)

    assert cast is not None
    assert cast.this == exp.Literal.string("1 day")

    data_type = cast.args.get("to")
    assert isinstance(data_type, exp.DataType)
    assert data_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL
    assert data_type.sql(dialect="postgres") == "INTERVAL"


def test_postgres_interval_cast_supports_columns_aliases_and_nested_casts():
    sql = (
        "SELECT CAST(duration AS INTERVAL) AS elapsed, "
        "CAST(CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL) AS TEXT) FROM events"
    )
    expression = parse_one(sql, read="postgres")

    interval_casts = [
        cast
        for cast in expression.find_all(exp.Cast)
        if cast.args["to"].this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL
    ]

    assert len(interval_casts) == 2
    assert any(
        isinstance(cast.this, exp.Column) and cast.this.name == "duration"
        for cast in interval_casts
    )
    assert expression.sql(dialect="postgres") == sql

import dynamic_yaml
import pytest


ISSUE_YAML = """
names:
  n1: "name1"
  n2: "name2"
columns:
  - "{names.n1}"
  - "{names.n2}"
"""


def test_iteration_supplies_resolved_values_to_list_consumers():
    """Consumers such as pandas should see values, not format strings."""
    config = dynamic_yaml.load(ISSUE_YAML)

    # Indexing already resolved values; whole-sequence consumption must agree.
    assert config.columns[0] == "name1"
    assert config.columns[1] == "name2"
    assert list(config.columns) == ["name1", "name2"]
    assert tuple(config.columns) == ("name1", "name2")

    first, second = config.columns
    assert (first, second) == ("name1", "name2")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("method_name", ["as_list", "resolve"])
def test_list_returning_resolution_methods(method_name):
    config = dynamic_yaml.load(ISSUE_YAML)

    resolved = getattr(config.columns, method_name)()

    assert type(resolved) is list
    assert resolved == ["name1", "name2"]

    # The result is an independent built-in list, not the dynamic collection.
    resolved.append("extra")
    resolved[0] = "changed"
    assert list(config.columns) == ["name1", "name2"]
    assert len(config.columns) == 2


def test_as_set_returns_resolved_values_and_removes_duplicates():
    config = dynamic_yaml.load(
        """
names:
  n1: "name1"
  n2: "name2"
columns:
  - "{names.n1}"
  - "{names.n2}"
  - "{names.n1}"
"""
    )

    resolved = config.columns.as_set()

    assert type(resolved) is set
    assert resolved == {"name1", "name2"}


def test_resolution_remains_dynamic_after_references_change():
    config = dynamic_yaml.load(ISSUE_YAML)
    original_snapshot = config.columns.as_list()

    config.names.n1 = "updated-name"

    assert original_snapshot == ["name1", "name2"]
    assert list(config.columns) == ["updated-name", "name2"]
    assert config.columns.as_list() == ["updated-name", "name2"]
    assert config.columns.resolve() == ["updated-name", "name2"]
    assert config.columns.as_set() == {"updated-name", "name2"}


def test_iteration_handles_embedded_references_literals_and_non_strings():
    config = dynamic_yaml.load(

names:
  n1: "name1"
  n2: "name2"
values:
  - "prefix-{names.n1}"
  - "{names.n2}-suffix"
  - "{{names.n1}}"
  - 42
  - 3.5
  - true
  - null
"""

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


ISSUE_SQL = "select cast([struct_pack(a := 1)] as struct(a bigint)[])"


def _parse_cast(sql):
    expression = parse_one(sql, read="duckdb")
    casts = list(expression.find_all(exp.Cast))
    assert len(casts) == 1
    return expression, casts[0]


def _assert_struct_array(data_type, expected_fields):
    """Assert ARRAY<STRUCT<...>> semantics for DuckDB's [] type syntax."""
    assert isinstance(data_type, exp.DataType)
    assert data_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.ARRAY
    assert len(data_type.expressions) == 1

    struct_type = data_type.expressions[0]
    assert isinstance(struct_type, exp.DataType)
    assert struct_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.STRUCT

    fields = struct_type.expressions
    assert len(fields) == len(expected_fields)
    for field, (expected_name, expected_type) in zip(fields, expected_fields):
        assert isinstance(field, exp.ColumnDef)
        assert field.name == expected_name
        assert field.args["kind"].this == expected_type

    return struct_type


def _assert_duckdb_roundtrip(expression):
    rendered = expression.sql(dialect="duckdb")
    assert parse_one(rendered, read="duckdb") == expression


def test_issue_cast_array_literal_to_array_of_struct():
    expression, cast = _parse_cast(ISSUE_SQL)

    # The value being cast must remain an array literal, and the complete target
    # type must be consumed as an array of structs.
    assert isinstance(cast.this, exp.Array)
    assert len(cast.this.expressions) == 1
    _assert_struct_array(
        cast.args["to"],
        [("a", exp.DataType.Type.BIGINT)],
    )

    _assert_duckdb_roundtrip(expression)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "type_sql, expected_fields",
    [
        ("STRUCT(a BIGINT)[]", [("a", exp.DataType.Type.BIGINT)]),
        (
            "STRUCT(a BIGINT, b VARCHAR)[]",
            [
                ("a", exp.DataType.Type.BIGINT),
                ("b", exp.DataType.Type.VARCHAR),
            ],
        ),
        (
            "struct(a bigint, b double) []",
            [
                ("a", exp.DataType.Type.BIGINT),
                ("b", exp.DataType.Type.DOUBLE),
            ],
        ),
    ],
)
def test_cast_to_array_of_struct_variants(type_sql, expected_fields):
    expression, cast = _parse_cast(f"SELECT CAST(x AS {type_sql})")
    _assert_struct_array(cast.args["to"], expected_fields)
    _assert_duckdb_roundtrip(expression)


def test_duckdb_double_colon_cast_to_array_of_struct():
    expression, cast = _parse_cast("SELECT x::STRUCT(a BIGINT, b VARCHAR)[]")
    _assert_struct_array(
        cast.args["to"],
        [
            ("a", exp.DataType.Type.BIGINT),
            ("b", exp.DataType.Type.VARCHAR),
        ],
    )
    _assert_duckdb_roundtrip(expression)


def test_repeated_array_brackets_after_struct_type():
    expression, cast = _parse_cast("SELECT CAST(x AS STRUCT(a BIGINT)[][])")
    target = cast.args["to"]

    assert target.this == exp.DataType.Type.ARRAY
    assert len(target.expressions) == 1

    inner_array = target.expressions[0]
    assert inner_array.this == exp.DataType.Type.ARRAY
    assert len(inner_array.expressions) == 1
    assert inner_array.expressions[0].this == exp.DataType.Type.STRUCT

    _assert_duckdb_roundtrip(expression)


def test_array_brackets_inside_struct_fields_are_not_confused_with_suffix():
    expression, cast = _parse_cast("SELECT CAST(x AS STRUCT(a INT[], b TEXT)[])")
    struct_type = _assert_struct_array(
        cast.args["to"],
        [
            ("a", exp.DataType.Type.ARRAY),
            ("b", exp.DataType.Type.TEXT),
        ],
    )

    array_field_type = struct_type.expressions[0].args["kind"]
    assert len(array_field_type.expressions) == 1
    assert array_field_type.expressions[0].this == exp.DataType.Type.INT

    _assert_duckdb_roundtrip(expression)


def test_array_of_struct_can_be_parsed_as_a_data_type():
    data_type = parse_one(
        "STRUCT(a BIGINT, b VARCHAR)[]",
        read="duckdb",
        into=exp.DataType,
    )
    _assert_struct_array(
        data_type,
        [
            ("a", exp.DataType.Type.BIGINT),
            ("b", exp.DataType.Type.VARCHAR),
        ],
    )


def test_plain_struct_and_scalar_array_casts_are_unchanged():
    _, struct_cast = _parse_cast("SELECT CAST(x AS STRUCT(a BIGINT))")
    struct_type = struct_cast.args["to"]
    assert struct_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.STRUCT
    assert len(struct_type.expressions) == 1
    assert struct_type.expressions[0].name == "a"

    _, array_cast = _parse_cast("SELECT CAST(x AS INT[])")
    array_type = array_cast.args["to"]
    assert array_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.ARRAY
    assert len(array_type.expressions) == 1
    assert array_type.expressions[0].this == exp.DataType.Type.INT

import pytest

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


@pytest.mark.parametrize("dialect", [None, "postgres"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [
        "select cast('1 day' as interval)",
        "SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)",
        "SELECT cast('1 day' as Interval)",
    ],
)
def test_cast_string_to_interval(sql, dialect):
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read=dialect)

    cast = expression.find(exp.Cast)
    assert cast is not None
    assert cast.this == exp.Literal.string("1 day")

    data_type = cast.args.get("to")
    assert isinstance(data_type, exp.DataType)
    assert data_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL
    assert data_type.expressions == []

    assert expression.sql(dialect=dialect) == "SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "interval_value",
    [
        "1 day",
        "1 year 2 months 3 days",
        "04:05:06",
        "-2 days",
    ],
)
def test_cast_to_interval_preserves_interval_string(interval_value):
    sql = f"SELECT CAST('{interval_value}' AS INTERVAL)"
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="postgres")

    cast = expression.find(exp.Cast)
    assert cast is not None
    assert cast.this == exp.Literal.string(interval_value)
    assert cast.args["to"].this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL
    assert expression.sql(dialect="postgres") == sql


def test_cast_non_literal_to_interval():
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(
        "SELECT CAST(duration AS INTERVAL) FROM events", read="postgres"
    )

    cast = expression.find(exp.Cast)
    assert cast is not None
    assert isinstance(cast.this, exp.Column)
    assert cast.this.name == "duration"
    assert cast.args["to"].this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL
    assert (
        expression.sql(dialect="postgres")
        == "SELECT CAST(duration AS INTERVAL) FROM events"
    )


def test_try_cast_to_interval():
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one("SELECT TRY_CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)")

    cast = expression.find(exp.Cast)
    assert cast is not None
    assert cast.args["to"].this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL
    assert expression.sql() == "SELECT TRY_CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)"

import pytest

import esper


class Position:
    def __init__(self, x=0, y=0):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y


class Velocity:
    def __init__(self, x=0, y=0):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y


@pytest.fixture
def world():
    return esper.World()


def test_create_entity_without_components_creates_real_entities(world):
    first = world.create_entity()
    second = world.create_entity()

    assert (first, second) == (1, 2)
    assert world.entity_exists(first)
    assert world.entity_exists(second)
    assert not world.entity_exists(second + 1)

    # An entity created without components is valid and has no components.
    assert world.components_for_entity(first) == ()
    assert not world.has_component(first, Position)
    assert world.try_component(first, Position) is None
    assert world.get_component(Position) == []


def test_empty_entity_can_be_built_up_with_components_later(world):
    entity = world.create_entity()
    position = Position(10, 20)
    velocity = Velocity(1, 2)

    world.add_component(entity, position)
    world.add_component(entity, velocity)

    assert world.entity_exists(entity)
    assert world.has_components(entity, Position, Velocity)
    assert world.component_for_entity(entity, Position) is position
    assert world.component_for_entity(entity, Velocity) is velocity
    assert world.components_for_entity(entity) == (position, velocity)
    assert world.get_component(Position) == [(entity, position)]


def test_create_entity_with_components_still_works(world):
    position = Position(3, 4)
    velocity = Velocity(5, 6)

    entity = world.create_entity(position, velocity)

    assert world.entity_exists(entity)
    assert world.component_for_entity(entity, Position) is position
    assert world.component_for_entity(entity, Velocity) is velocity


def test_add_component_rejects_made_up_entity_without_side_effects(world):
    made_up_entity = 123

    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.add_component(made_up_entity, None)

    assert not world.entity_exists(made_up_entity)
    assert world.get_component(type(None)) == []
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.components_for_entity(made_up_entity)

    # A failed attempt to add a component must not consume an entity ID.
    assert world.create_entity() == 1


@pytest.mark.parametrize("immediate", [True, False])
def test_empty_entity_can_be_deleted_and_cannot_receive_components_afterward(
    world, immediate
):
    entity = world.create_entity()
    assert world.entity_exists(entity)

    if immediate:
        world.delete_entity(entity, immediate=True)
    else:
        world.delete_entity(entity)
        assert not world.entity_exists(entity)
        world.process()

    assert not world.entity_exists(entity)
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.components_for_entity(entity)
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.add_component(entity, Position())

    assert not world.entity_exists(entity)
    assert world.get_component(Position) == []


def test_clear_database_removes_empty_entities_and_resets_ids(world):
    empty_entity = world.create_entity()
    populated_entity = world.create_entity(Position())

    world.clear_database()

    assert not world.entity_exists(empty_entity)
    assert not world.entity_exists(populated_entity)
    assert world.get_component(Position) == []

    new_entity = world.create_entity()
    assert new_entity == 1
    assert world.entity_exists(new_entity)

import pytest

from dynamic_yaml import load


ISSUE_YAML = """
names:
  n1: "name1"
  n2: "name2"
columns:
  - "{names.n1}"
  - "{names.n2}"
"""


def test_issue_example_resolves_when_consumed_as_an_iterable():
    """External consumers such as pandas obtain the columns by iteration."""
    config = load(ISSUE_YAML)

    assert list(config.columns) == ["name1", "name2"]
    assert tuple(config.columns) == ("name1", "name2")
    assert [column for column in config.columns] == ["name1", "name2"]

    # Iteration must be repeatable and must not change indexed access or size.
    assert len(config.columns) == 2
    assert config.columns[0] == "name1"
    assert config.columns[1] == "name2"


def test_explicit_resolution_helpers_return_resolved_builtin_containers():
    config = load(ISSUE_YAML)

    for method_name in ("as_list", "resolve"):
        resolved = getattr(config.columns, method_name)()
        assert type(resolved) is list
        assert resolved == ["name1", "name2"]

    resolved_set = config.columns.as_set()
    assert type(resolved_set) is set
    assert resolved_set == {"name1", "name2"}


def test_as_set_deduplicates_after_resolution():
    config = load(
        """
names:
  n1: "name1"
  n2: "name2"
columns:
  - "{names.n1}"
  - "{names.n2}"
  - "{names.n1}"
"""
    )

    assert config.columns.as_list() == ["name1", "name2", "name1"]
    assert config.columns.as_set() == {"name1", "name2"}


def test_iteration_handles_embedded_references_non_strings_and_empty_lists():
    config = load(
        """
names:
  n1: "name1"
  n2: "name2"
mixed_items:
  - "{names.n1}"
  - "prefix/{names.n2}"
  - 0
  - 2.5
  - false
  - null
empty_items: []
"""
    )

    expected = ["name1", "prefix/name2", 0, 2.5, False, None]
    assert list(config.mixed_items) == expected
    assert config.mixed_items.as_list() == expected

    assert list(config.empty_items) == []
    assert config.empty_items.as_list() == []
    assert config.empty_items.resolve() == []
    assert config.empty_items.as_set() == set()


def test_root_level_list_iteration_uses_root_references():
    config = load(
        """
- "a"
- "b"
- "{root[0]}"
- "{root[1]}/c"
"""
    )

    assert list(config) == ["a", "b", "a", "b/c"]
    assert config.as_list() == ["a", "b", "a", "b/c"]


def test_iteration_respects_recursive_resolution():
    config = load(
        """
prefix: "/opt/ml"
input_path: "{prefix}/input"
training_data_path: "{input_path}/data/training"
paths:
  - "{training_data_path}"
  - "{input_path}/models"
""",
        recursive=True,
    )

    assert list(config.paths) == [
        "/opt/ml/input/data/training",
        "/opt/ml/input/models",

  n1: "name1"

groups:
  - - "{names.n1}"

  - - "prefix/{names.n2}"
"""
    )

        ["name1", "name2"],

    ]


def test_iteration_resolves_current_values_after_configuration_changes():
    config = load(ISSUE_YAML)

    assert list(config.columns) == ["name1", "name2"]

    assert config.columns.as_list() == ["updated", "name2"]

import os

import casbin
import pytest
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

from casbin_sqlalchemy_adapter import Adapter, Base, CasbinRule


MODEL_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "rbac_model.conf")


def stored_rules(engine, ptype):
    """Read rules through an independent session, bypassing the enforcer model."""
    session = sessionmaker(bind=engine)()
    try:
        rows = (
            session.query(CasbinRule)
            .filter(CasbinRule.ptype == ptype)
            .order_by(CasbinRule.id)
            .all()
        )
        rules = []
        for row in rows:
            rule = []
            for index in range(6):
                value = getattr(row, "v{}".format(index))
                if value is None:
                    break
                rule.append(value)
            rules.append(rule)
        return rules
    finally:
        session.close()


def seed_rules(engine, ptype, rules):
    """Seed storage without using the batch API under test."""
    session = sessionmaker(bind=engine)()
    try:
        for rule in rules:
            values = {"ptype": ptype}
            values.update(
                {"v{}".format(index): value for index, value in enumerate(rule)}
            )
            session.add(CasbinRule(**values))
        session.commit()
    finally:
        session.close()


def make_enforcer():
    engine = create_engine("sqlite://")
    adapter = Adapter(engine)

    seed_rules(
        engine,
        "p",
        [
            ["alice", "data1", "read"],
            ["bob", "data2", "write"],
            ["data2_admin", "data2", "read"],
            ["data2_admin", "data2", "write"],
        ],
    )
    seed_rules(engine, "g", [["alice", "data2_admin"]])

    return casbin.Enforcer(MODEL_PATH, adapter), engine


@pytest.fixture
def enforcer_and_engine():
    return make_enforcer()


def test_adapter_add_policies_persists_policy_and_grouping_rules():
    engine = create_engine("sqlite://")
    adapter = Adapter(engine)

    policy_rules = [
        ["eve", "data3", "read"],
        ["carol", "data4", "write"],
    ]
    grouping_rules = [
        ["eve", "data2_admin"],
        ["carol", "data2_admin"],
    ]

    # These are the public batch-adapter methods missing from the issue.
    adapter.add_policies("p", "p", policy_rules)
    adapter.add_policies("g", "g", grouping_rules)

    assert stored_rules(engine, "p") == policy_rules
    assert stored_rules(engine, "g") == grouping_rules

    # A new enforcer must load the batch from storage, rather than merely
    # seeing changes in an existing enforcer's in-memory model.
    enforcer = casbin.Enforcer(MODEL_PATH, adapter)
    assert enforcer.enforce("eve", "data3", "read")
    assert enforcer.enforce("carol", "data4", "write")
    assert enforcer.enforce("eve", "data2", "read")
    assert enforcer.enforce("carol", "data2", "write")


def test_enforcer_batch_add_is_auto_saved_and_does_not_duplicate_rules(
    enforcer_and_engine,
):
    enforcer, engine = enforcer_and_engine
    new_rules = [
        ["eve", "data3", "read"],
        ["carol", "data4", "write"],
    ]

    assert enforcer.add_policies(new_rules) is True
    assert enforcer.add_named_policies("g", [["eve", "data2_admin"]]) is True

    # Re-adding an existing rule follows normal Casbin duplicate handling.
    assert enforcer.add_policies([new_rules[0]]) is False

    persisted_policies = stored_rules(engine, "p")
    assert persisted_policies.count(new_rules[0]) == 1
    assert persisted_policies.count(new_rules[1]) == 1
    assert ["eve", "data2_admin"] in stored_rules(engine, "g")

    reloaded = casbin.Enforcer(MODEL_PATH, enforcer.get_adapter())
    assert reloaded.enforce("eve", "data3", "read")
    assert reloaded.enforce("carol", "data4", "write")
    assert reloaded.enforce("eve", "data2", "read")


def test_adapter_remove_policies_removes_only_requested_rules():
    engine = create_engine("sqlite://")
    adapter = Adapter(engine)
    rules = [
        ["alice", "data1", "read"],
        ["bob", "data2", "write"],
        ["carol", "data3", "read"],
    ]
    grouping_rules = [["alice", "data2_admin"]]
    seed_rules(engine, "p", rules)
    seed_rules(engine, "g", grouping_rules)

    adapter.remove_policies("p", "p", rules[:2])
    assert stored_rules(engine, "p") == [rules[2]]

    # Removal is scoped to the supplied ptype and a missing batch is a no-op.
    assert stored_rules(engine, "g") == grouping_rules
    adapter.remove_policies("p", "p", [["nobody", "data9", "read"]])
    assert stored_rules(engine, "p") == [rules[2]]

    # Empty batches must not accidentally add or delete storage contents.
    adapter.add_policies("p", "p", [])
    adapter.remove_policies("p", "p", [])
    assert stored_rules(engine, "p") == [rules[2]]
    assert stored_rules(engine, "g") == grouping_rules


def test_enforcer_batch_remove_is_auto_saved(enforcer_and_engine):
    enforcer, engine = enforcer_and_engine

    assert enforcer.enforce("alice", "data1", "read")
    assert enforcer.enforce("bob", "data2", "write")
    assert enforcer.enforce("alice", "data2", "read")

    assert (
        enforcer.remove_policies(
            [
                ["alice", "data1", "read"],
                ["bob", "data2", "write"],
            ]
        )
        is True
    )
    assert (
        enforcer.remove_named_policies("g", [["alice", "data2_admin"]])
        is True
    )

    assert not enforcer.enforce("alice", "data1", "read")
    assert not enforcer.enforce("bob", "data2", "write")
    assert not enforcer.enforce("alice", "data2", "read")

    # Unrelated policies remain, and all removals survive a reload.
    assert stored_rules(engine, "p") == [
        ["data2_admin", "data2", "read"],
        ["data2_admin", "data2", "write"],
    ]
    assert stored_rules(engine, "g") == []

    reloaded = casbin.Enforcer(MODEL_PATH, enforcer.get_adapter())
    assert not reloaded.enforce("alice", "data1", "read")
    assert not reloaded.enforce("bob", "data2", "write")
    assert reloaded.enforce("data2_admin", "data2", "read")
    assert reloaded.enforce("data2_admin", "data2", "write")

    before = stored_rules(engine, "p")
    assert reloaded.remove_policies([["nobody", "data9", "read"]]) is False
    assert stored_rules(engine, "p") == before

"""Tests for power operations with array exponents."""

import operator

import numpy as np
import pytest

from unyt import cm, s
from unyt.array import unyt_array, unyt_quantity
from unyt.exceptions import UnitOperationError


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "operation", [operator.pow, np.power], ids=["power-operator", "numpy-power"]
)
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "make_exponent",
    [unyt_array, np.asarray],
    ids=["unyt-exponent", "ndarray-exponent"],
)
def test_dimensionless_array_exponent(operation, make_exponent):
    """Array exponents should give the same element-wise result as NumPy.

    A plain ndarray exponent is dimensionless, just like an explicitly
    dimensionless unyt_array exponent, so both forms must be supported.
    """
    base = unyt_array([1, 2, 3, 4])
    exponent = make_exponent([1, 2, 3, 4])

    result = operation(base, exponent)

    assert isinstance(result, unyt_array)
    assert result.units.is_dimensionless
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(np.asarray(result), [1, 4, 27, 256])


def test_array_exponent_with_zero_fractional_and_negative_powers():
    base = unyt_array([2.0, 4.0, 9.0, 16.0])
    exponent = unyt_array([0.0, 0.5, -1.0, 2.0])

    result = base**exponent
    expected = np.power(np.asarray(base), np.asarray(exponent))

    assert result.units.is_dimensionless
    np.testing.assert_allclose(np.asarray(result), expected)


def test_array_exponent_broadcasting():
    base = unyt_array([[2.0], [3.0], [4.0]])
    exponent = unyt_array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])

    result = base**exponent
    expected = np.power(np.asarray(base), np.asarray(exponent))

    assert result.shape == (3, 3)
    assert result.units.is_dimensionless
    np.testing.assert_allclose(np.asarray(result), expected)


def test_scalar_base_with_array_exponent():
    base = unyt_quantity(2.0)
    exponent = unyt_array([0, 1, 2, 3])

    result = base**exponent

    assert isinstance(result, unyt_array)
    assert result.units.is_dimensionless
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(np.asarray(result), [1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0])


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("base_units", "exponent_units"),
    [
        (cm, None),  # A dimensional base cannot have an element-wise exponent.
        (None, s),  # The exponent itself must be dimensionless.
        (cm, s),
    ],
)
def test_invalid_array_power_units_are_rejected(base_units, exponent_units):
    base = unyt_array([1.0, 2.0], base_units)
    exponent = unyt_array([1.0, 2.0], exponent_units)

    with pytest.raises(UnitOperationError):
        base**exponent


def test_dimensional_base_with_plain_array_exponent_is_rejected():
    base = unyt_array([1.0, 2.0], cm)

    with pytest.raises(UnitOperationError):
        base ** np.array([1.0, 2.0])


def test_scalar_exponent_behavior_is_preserved():
    data = unyt_array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0], cm)

    squared = data**2
    assert squared.units == cm**2
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(np.asarray(squared), [1.0, 4.0, 9.0])

    zeroth_power = data**0
    assert zeroth_power.units.is_dimensionless
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(np.asarray(zeroth_power), [1.0, 1.0, 1.0])

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one, transpile


def assert_interval_cast(cast):
    assert isinstance(cast, exp.Cast)
    data_type = cast.args.get("to")
    assert isinstance(data_type, exp.DataType)
    assert data_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL
    assert data_type.sql() == "INTERVAL"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("dialect", [None, "postgres"])
def test_cast_string_to_interval(dialect):
    expression = parse_one("select cast('1 day' as interval)", read=dialect)

    cast = expression.expressions[0]
    assert_interval_cast(cast)
    assert cast.this == exp.Literal.string("1 day")
    assert expression.sql(dialect=dialect) == "SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)"
    assert expression.sql(dialect="postgres") == "SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [
        "SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)",
        "SELECT CAST( '1 day' AS interval )",
        "SELECT CAST('1 day' AS InTeRvAl)",
    ],
)
def test_cast_to_interval_is_case_insensitive(sql):
    expression = parse_one(sql, read="postgres")

    assert_interval_cast(expression.expressions[0])
    assert (
        expression.sql(dialect="postgres")
        == "SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)"
    )


def test_nested_and_multiple_interval_casts():
    expression = parse_one(
        "SELECT CAST(CAST(duration_text AS TEXT) AS INTERVAL), "
        "CAST(other_text AS INTERVAL) FROM events",
        read="postgres",
    )

    assert len(expression.expressions) == 2
    for cast in expression.expressions:
        assert_interval_cast(cast)

    assert expression.sql(dialect="postgres") == (
        "SELECT CAST(CAST(duration_text AS TEXT) AS INTERVAL), "
        "CAST(other_text AS INTERVAL) FROM events"
    )


def test_interval_can_be_parsed_as_a_standalone_data_type():
    data_type = parse_one("interval", into=exp.DataType, read="postgres")

    assert isinstance(data_type, exp.DataType)
    assert data_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL
    assert data_type.sql() == "INTERVAL"


def test_interval_column_definition():
    expression = parse_one(
        "CREATE TABLE events (duration INTERVAL)", read="postgres"
    )

    column = expression.find(exp.ColumnDef)
    assert column is not None
    assert isinstance(column.args.get("kind"), exp.DataType)
    assert column.args["kind"].this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL
    assert expression.sql() == "CREATE TABLE events (duration INTERVAL)"

    expression = parse_one("SELECT INTERVAL '1' DAY", read="postgres")

    assert isinstance(expression.expressions[0], exp.Interval)
    assert expression.sql() == "SELECT INTERVAL '1' DAY"

        read="postgres",
        write="postgres",
    ) == ["SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)"]

import pytest

from sqlglot import transpile


def transpile_one(sql: str, read: str, write: str = "duckdb") -> str:
    return transpile(sql, read=read, write=write)[0]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("spark_sql", "expected"),
    [
        (
            "SELECT DATEDIFF('2020-01-05', '2020-01-01') AS diff",
            "SELECT DATE_DIFF('Day', CAST('2020-01-01' AS DATE), "
            "CAST('2020-01-05' AS DATE)) AS diff",
        ),
        (
            "SELECT DATEDIFF(end_date, start_date) FROM transactions",
            "SELECT DATE_DIFF('Day', CAST(start_date AS DATE), "
            "CAST(end_date AS DATE)) FROM transactions",
        ),
        (
            "SELECT DATEDIFF(CURRENT_DATE(), hire_date) AS days_employed FROM employees",
            "SELECT DATE_DIFF('Day', CAST(hire_date AS DATE), "
            "CAST(CURRENT_DATE AS DATE)) AS days_employed FROM employees",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_spark_datediff_defaults_to_day_in_duckdb(spark_sql, expected):
    """Spark's two-argument DATEDIFF must not produce a NULL/None date part."""
    assert transpile_one(spark_sql, read="spark") == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize("unit", ["day", "month", "year", "DAY"])
def test_duckdb_date_diff_preserves_an_explicit_unit(unit):
    """Supplying the default must not overwrite units already present."""
    sql = f"SELECT DATE_DIFF('{unit}', start_date, end_date)"
    assert transpile_one(sql, read="duckdb") == sql


def test_spark_datediff_does_not_emit_none_anywhere_in_the_statement():
    sql = """
        SELECT DATEDIFF(end_date, start_date) AS elapsed
        FROM transactions
        WHERE DATEDIFF(end_date, start_date) > 30
    """

    result = transpile_one(sql, read="spark")

    assert "'None'" not in result
    assert (
        result.count(
            "DATE_DIFF('Day', CAST(start_date AS DATE), CAST(end_date AS DATE))"
        )
        == 2
    )

from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

import pytest

from click.testing import CliRunner

from ..create import _main
from .helpers import setup_simple_project


def _effective_editor_suffix(mock_edit):
    """Return the suffix Click will use for the editor's temporary file."""
    mock_edit.assert_called_once()
    kwargs = mock_edit.call_args.kwargs

    # click.edit() gives an explicit filename precedence over extension. When
    # neither is supplied, its default temporary-file extension is .txt.
    filename = kwargs.get("filename")
    if filename is not None:
        return Path(filename).suffix.lower()

    extension = kwargs.get("extension", ".txt")
    return extension.lower() if extension else ""


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("extra_config", "expected_suffix"),
    [
        ("", ".rst"),
        ('filename = "NEWS.md"', ".md"),
        # Extension recognition should not depend on the configuration's case.
        ('filename = "NEWS.MD"', ".md"),
    ],
)
def test_explicit_edit_uses_configured_markup_suffix(
    extra_config, expected_suffix
):
    runner = CliRunner()

    with runner.isolated_filesystem():
        setup_simple_project(extra_config=extra_config)

        with mock.patch("click.edit", return_value="Edited content") as mock_edit:
            result = runner.invoke(_main, ["123.feature", "--edit"])

        assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
        assert _effective_editor_suffix(mock_edit) == expected_suffix

        fragments = list(Path("foo", "newsfragments").iterdir())
        assert len(fragments) == 1
        assert fragments[0].read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "Edited content\n"


def test_interactive_edit_uses_configured_markup_suffix():
    """Interactive creation opens an editor file with the markup suffix."""
    runner = CliRunner()

    with runner.isolated_filesystem():
        setup_simple_project(extra_config='filename = "NEWS.md"')

        with mock.patch(
            "click.edit", return_value="Interactive content"
        ) as mock_edit:
            result = runner.invoke(_main, input="456\nfeature\n")

        assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
        assert _effective_editor_suffix(mock_edit) == ".md"
        assert Path("foo", "newsfragments", "456.feature.md").read_text(
            encoding="utf-8"
        ) == "Interactive content\n"


def test_edit_with_initial_content_still_uses_markup_suffix():
    """Supplying initial content with -c must not bypass the suffix handling."""
    runner = CliRunner()

    with runner.isolated_filesystem():
        setup_simple_project()

        with mock.patch("click.edit", return_value="Final content") as mock_edit:
            result = runner.invoke(
                _main,
                ["123.feature.rst", "--edit", "--content", "Initial content"],
            )

        assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
        assert _effective_editor_suffix(mock_edit) == ".rst"
        initial_editor_content = mock_edit.call_args.args[0]
        assert initial_editor_content.startswith("Initial content\n")
        assert Path("foo", "newsfragments", "123.feature.rst").read_text(
            encoding="utf-8"
        ) == "Final content\n"

import sqlite3

import casbin
import pytest

from casbin_sqlalchemy_adapter import Adapter


ALICE = ["alice", "data1", "read"]
BOB = ["bob", "data2", "write"]
CAROL = ["carol", "data3", "read"]


def stored_rules(db_path):
    """Read through a separate connection so uncommitted work is not accepted."""
    with sqlite3.connect(str(db_path)) as connection:
        return connection.execute(
            "SELECT ptype, v0, v1, v2 FROM casbin_rule ORDER BY id"
        ).fetchall()


@pytest.fixture
def db_path(tmp_path):
    return tmp_path / "casbin.db"


@pytest.fixture
def adapter(db_path):
    instance = Adapter("sqlite:///" + str(db_path))
    yield instance
    instance._session.close()


def test_add_policies_persists_the_whole_batch(adapter, db_path):
    adapter.add_policies("p", "p", [ALICE, BOB])
    adapter.add_policies("p", "p2", [CAROL])

    assert stored_rules(db_path) == [
        ("p", "alice", "data1", "read"),
        ("p", "bob", "data2", "write"),
        ("p2", "carol", "data3", "read"),
    ]


def test_empty_add_policies_is_a_committed_noop(adapter, db_path):
    adapter.add_policies("p", "p", [ALICE])
    before = stored_rules(db_path)

    adapter.add_policies("p", "p", [])

    assert stored_rules(db_path) == before


def test_remove_policies_removes_only_requested_rules(adapter, db_path):
    adapter.add_policies("p", "p", [ALICE, BOB, CAROL])
    # The same rule under another ptype must not be removed with the p rules.
    adapter.add_policies("p", "p2", [ALICE])

    adapter.remove_policies("p", "p", [ALICE, BOB])
    assert stored_rules(db_path) == [
        ("p", "carol", "data3", "read"),
        ("p2", "alice", "data1", "read"),
    ]

    # A batch containing both missing and existing rules still removes the
    # existing one. Missing rules and empty batches leave other data intact.
    adapter.remove_policies(
        "p", "p", [["nobody", "missing", "read"], CAROL]
    )
    assert stored_rules(db_path) == [("p2", "alice", "data1", "read")]

    adapter.remove_policies("p", "p2", [])
    adapter.remove_policies("p", "p2", [BOB])
    assert stored_rules(db_path) == [("p2", "alice", "data1", "read")]


def test_enforcer_batch_operations_are_saved_and_reloaded(
    adapter, db_path, tmp_path
):
    model_path = tmp_path / "model.conf"
    model_path.write_text(
        """
[request_definition]
r = sub, obj, act

[policy_definition]
p = sub, obj, act

[policy_effect]
e = some(where (p.eft == allow))

[matchers]
m = r.sub == p.sub && r.obj == p.obj && r.act == p.act
""".strip(),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    enforcer = casbin.Enforcer(str(model_path), adapter)

    assert enforcer.add_policies([ALICE, BOB]) is True
    assert enforcer.enforce("alice", "data1", "read") is True
    assert enforcer.enforce("bob", "data2", "write") is True
    assert stored_rules(db_path) == [
        ("p", "alice", "data1", "read"),
        ("p", "bob", "data2", "write"),
    ]

    assert enforcer.remove_policies([ALICE]) is True
    assert stored_rules(db_path) == [("p", "bob", "data2", "write")]

    reloaded_adapter = Adapter("sqlite:///" + str(db_path))
    try:
        reloaded = casbin.Enforcer(str(model_path), reloaded_adapter)
        assert reloaded.get_policy() == [BOB]
        assert reloaded.enforce("alice", "data1", "read") is False
        assert reloaded.enforce("bob", "data2", "write") is True
    finally:
        reloaded_adapter._session.close()

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse, parse_one


def _assert_mysql_round_trip(sql: str, expected: str) -> exp.Expression:
    statement = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")
    generated = statement.sql(dialect="mysql")

    assert generated == expected
    assert parse_one(generated, dialect="mysql").sql(dialect="mysql") == expected
    return statement


def test_mysql_issue_example_preserves_descending_index_column():
    statements = parse(
        "CREATE TABLE `foo` (a VARCHAR(10), KEY idx_a (a DESC))", dialect="mysql"
    )

    assert len(statements) == 1
    statement = statements[0]
    assert statement.sql(dialect="mysql") == (
        "CREATE TABLE `foo` (a VARCHAR(10), INDEX idx_a (a DESC))"
    )

    index = statement.find(exp.IndexColumnConstraint)
    assert index is not None
    assert index.name == "idx_a"

    schema = index.args.get("schema")
    assert isinstance(schema, exp.Schema)
    assert len(schema.expressions) == 1

    column = schema.expressions[0]
    assert isinstance(column, exp.Ordered)
    assert column.this.name == "a"
    assert column.args.get("desc") is True
    assert not list(schema.find_all(exp.Alias))


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("sql", "expected"),
    [
        (
            "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, KEY idx_a (a ASC))",
            "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, INDEX idx_a (a ASC))",
        ),
        (
            "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, b INT, KEY idx_ab (a, b DESC))",
            "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, b INT, INDEX idx_ab (a, b DESC))",
        ),
        (
            "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, b INT, c INT, KEY idx_abc (a ASC, b DESC, c))",
            "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, b INT, c INT, INDEX idx_abc (a ASC, b DESC, c))",
        ),
        (
            "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, KEY (a DESC))",
            "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, INDEX (a DESC))",
        ),
        (
            "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, b INT, KEY idx_ab (a, b))",
            "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, b INT, INDEX idx_ab (a, b))",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_mysql_index_ordering_composite_unnamed_and_unqualified(sql, expected):
    _assert_mysql_round_trip(sql, expected)


def test_mysql_ordered_index_column_does_not_displace_other_index_syntax():
    _assert_mysql_round_trip(
        "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, KEY idx_a USING BTREE (a DESC) COMMENT 'ordered')",
        "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, INDEX idx_a USING BTREE (a DESC) COMMENT 'ordered')",
    )

    statement = _assert_mysql_round_trip(
        "CREATE TABLE `foo` (`a` INT, `b` INT, KEY `idx_ab` (`a` ASC, `b` DESC))",
        "CREATE TABLE `foo` (`a` INT, `b` INT, INDEX `idx_ab` (`a` ASC, `b` DESC))",
    )
    index = statement.find(exp.IndexColumnConstraint)
    ordered_columns = index.args["schema"].expressions

    assert [column.this.name for column in ordered_columns] == ["a", "b"]
    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in ordered_columns] == [False, True]


def test_postgres_create_index_supports_ordering_and_nondefault_null_ordering():
    sql = "CREATE INDEX idx_ab ON foo (a ASC NULLS FIRST, b DESC NULLS LAST)"
    expected = "CREATE INDEX idx_ab ON foo(a ASC NULLS FIRST, b DESC NULLS LAST)"
    statement = parse_one(sql, dialect="postgres")

    assert statement.sql(dialect="postgres") == expected
    assert parse_one(expected, dialect="postgres").sql(dialect="postgres") == expected

    ordered_columns = list(statement.find_all(exp.Ordered))
    assert len(ordered_columns) == 2
    assert [column.this.name for column in ordered_columns] == ["a", "b"]
    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in ordered_columns] == [False, True]
    assert [column.args.get("nulls_first") for column in ordered_columns] == [True, False]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("column_name", ["key", "index"])
def test_postgres_index_keywords_remain_valid_column_names(column_name):
    # KEY and INDEX are unreserved PostgreSQL keywords. Adding index-constraint
    # parsing must not cause ordinary column definitions to be consumed as constraints.
    sql = f"CREATE TABLE foo ({column_name} INT)"
    statement = parse_one(sql, dialect="postgres")

    column = statement.find(exp.ColumnDef)
    assert column is not None
    assert column.name == column_name

import dynamic_yaml


ISSUE_YAML = """
names:
  n1: "name1"
  n2: "name2"
columns:
  - "{names.n1}"
  - "{names.n2}"
"""


def test_issue_columns_resolve_when_consumed_as_an_iterable():
    """Consumers such as pandas should see values, not format strings."""
    config = dynamic_yaml.load(ISSUE_YAML)

    assert list(config.columns) == ["name1", "name2"]
    assert tuple(config.columns) == ("name1", "name2")
    assert [column for column in config.columns] == ["name1", "name2"]


def test_as_list_and_resolve_return_resolved_plain_lists():
    config = dynamic_yaml.load(ISSUE_YAML)

    for method_name in ("as_list", "resolve"):
        resolved = getattr(config.columns, method_name)()

        assert type(resolved) is list
        assert resolved == ["name1", "name2"]

        # The result is a separate regular list, not the dynamic collection.
        resolved.append("extra")
        assert list(config.columns) == ["name1", "name2"]


def test_as_set_resolves_values_before_removing_duplicates():
    config = dynamic_yaml.load(
        """
names:
  n1: "name1"
  n2: "name2"
columns:
  - "{names.n1}"
  - "{names.n2}"
  - "{names.n1}"
"""
    )

    resolved = config.columns.as_set()

    assert type(resolved) is set
    assert resolved == {"name1", "name2"}


def test_iteration_handles_mixed_scalar_values():
    config = dynamic_yaml.load(
        """
names:
  n1: "name1"
  n2: "name2"
entries:
  - "{names.n1}"
  - "prefix-{names.n2}"
  - "plain"
  - 7
  - false
  - null
"""
    )

    assert list(config.entries) == [
        "name1",
        "prefix-name2",
        "plain",
        7,
        False,
        None,
    ]


def test_empty_lists_can_be_iterated_and_resolved():
    config = dynamic_yaml.load("entries: []\n")

    assert list(config.entries) == []
    assert config.entries.as_list() == []
    assert config.entries.resolve() == []
    assert config.entries.as_set() == set()


def test_iteration_uses_current_values_from_the_configuration():
    config = dynamic_yaml.load(ISSUE_YAML)

    assert list(config.columns) == ["name1", "name2"]

    config.names.n1 = "updated"

    assert list(config.columns) == ["updated", "name2"]
    assert config.columns.as_list() == ["updated", "name2"]


def test_references_added_after_loading_are_resolved_during_iteration():
    config = dynamic_yaml.load(ISSUE_YAML)

    config.columns.insert(0, "{names.n2}")
    config.columns.append("{names.n1}")

    assert list(config.columns) == ["name2", "name1", "name2", "name1"]

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one, transpile


@pytest.mark.parametrize("dialect", [None, "postgres"], ids=["default", "postgres"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "value",
    ["1 day", "1 hour", "2 hours", "1 year 2 months 3 days"],
)
def test_cast_string_to_interval(dialect, value):
    statement = parse_one(f"select cast('{value}' as interval)", read=dialect)

    cast = statement.expressions[0]
    assert isinstance(cast, (exp.Cast, exp.TryCast))
    assert cast.this == exp.Literal.string(value)

    target = cast.args["to"]
    assert isinstance(target, exp.DataType)
    assert target.this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL

    assert statement.sql(dialect) == f"SELECT CAST('{value}' AS INTERVAL)"


def test_cast_to_interval_is_case_insensitive():
    statement = parse_one(
        "SeLeCt CaSt('1 day' aS iNtErVaL)",
        read="postgres",
    )

    assert statement.sql("postgres") == "SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "dialect, expected_sql",
    [
        (None, "SELECT TRY_CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)"),
        ("postgres", "SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)"),
    ],
    ids=["default", "postgres"],
)
def test_try_cast_to_interval(dialect, expected_sql):
    statement = parse_one(
        "SELECT TRY_CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)",
        read=dialect,
    )

    cast = statement.expressions[0]
    assert isinstance(cast, exp.TryCast)
    assert cast.args["to"].this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL
    assert statement.sql(dialect) == expected_sql


def test_cast_column_to_interval():
    statement = parse_one(
        "SELECT CAST(duration AS INTERVAL) FROM measurements",
        read="postgres",
    )

    cast = statement.expressions[0]
    assert isinstance(cast.this, exp.Column)
    assert cast.this.name == "duration"
    assert cast.args["to"].this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL
    assert (
        statement.sql("postgres")
        == "SELECT CAST(duration AS INTERVAL) FROM measurements"
    )


def test_nested_cast_to_interval():
    statement = parse_one("SELECT CAST(CAST('1 day' AS TEXT) AS INTERVAL)")

    outer_cast = statement.expressions[0]
    inner_cast = outer_cast.this
    assert outer_cast.args["to"].this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL
    assert isinstance(inner_cast, exp.Cast)
    assert inner_cast.args["to"].this == exp.DataType.Type.TEXT
    assert statement.sql() == "SELECT CAST(CAST('1 day' AS TEXT) AS INTERVAL)"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("dialect", [None, "postgres"], ids=["default", "postgres"])
def test_interval_is_a_standalone_data_type(dialect):
    data_type = parse_one("interval", into=exp.DataType, read=dialect)

    assert isinstance(data_type, exp.DataType)
    assert data_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL
    assert data_type.sql(dialect) == "INTERVAL"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("dialect", [None, "postgres"], ids=["default", "postgres"])
def test_interval_literal_behavior_is_preserved(dialect):
    statement = parse_one("SELECT INTERVAL '1 day'", read=dialect)

    interval = statement.expressions[0]
    assert isinstance(interval, exp.Interval)
    assert interval.this == exp.Literal.string("1 day")
    assert statement.sql(dialect) == "SELECT INTERVAL '1 day'"


def test_postgres_transpile_cast_to_interval():
    assert transpile(
        "select cast('1 day' as interval)",
        read="postgres",
        write="postgres",
    ) == ["SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)"]

import os

from pre_commit.meta_hooks import check_useless_excludes
from pre_commit.util import cmd_output
from testing.fixtures import add_config_to_repo


def _add_broken_symlink():
    # Simulate a symlink into a submodule which has not been initialized.
    os.symlink(os.path.join('submodule', 'target'), 'broken-link')
    assert os.path.islink('broken-link')
    assert not os.path.exists('broken-link')
    cmd_output('git', 'add', 'broken-link')


def _add_hook_config(in_git_dir, hook_id, exclude, types):
    config = {
        'repos': [
            {
                'repo': 'local',
                'hooks': [
                    {
                        'id': hook_id,
                        'name': hook_id,
                        'entry': 'true',
                        'language': 'system',
                        'files': '',
                        'types': types,
                        'exclude': exclude,
                    },
                ],
            },
        ],
    }
    add_config_to_repo(in_git_dir.strpath, config)


def test_exclude_matching_broken_symlink_is_not_useless(
        capsys, in_git_dir,
):
    _add_broken_symlink()
    _add_hook_config(
        in_git_dir,
        hook_id='check-symlinks',
        exclude='^broken-link$',
        types=['symlink'],
    )

    assert check_useless_excludes.main(()) == 0

    out, _ = capsys.readouterr()
    assert out == ''


def test_broken_symlink_does_not_make_nonmatching_exclude_useful(
        capsys, in_git_dir,
):
    _add_broken_symlink()
    _add_hook_config(
        in_git_dir,
        hook_id='check-symlinks',
        exclude='^some-other-file$',
        types=['symlink'],
    )

    assert check_useless_excludes.main(()) == 1

    out, _ = capsys.readouterr()
    assert out.strip() == (
        "The exclude pattern '^some-other-file$' for check-symlinks "
        'does not match any files'
    )


def test_broken_symlink_does_not_bypass_type_filtering(
        capsys, in_git_dir,
):
    _add_broken_symlink()
    _add_hook_config(
        in_git_dir,
        hook_id='python-only',
        exclude='^broken-link$',
        types=['python'],
    )

    # The symlink matches the regular expression, but the hook would never
    # receive it, so the exclude is still useless.
    assert check_useless_excludes.main(()) == 1

    out, _ = capsys.readouterr()
    assert out.strip() == (
        "The exclude pattern '^broken-link$' for python-only "
        'does not match any files'
    )

import pytest

import sqlglot as sg
from sqlglot import exp


def _parse_cast(sql):
    statement = sg.parse_one(sql, read="duckdb")
    assert isinstance(statement, exp.Select)

    cast = statement.expressions[0]
    assert isinstance(cast, exp.Cast)
    return cast


def _unwrap_array_type(data_type):
    dimensions = 0
    while data_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.ARRAY:
        dimensions += 1
        assert len(data_type.expressions) == 1
        data_type = data_type.expressions[0]
    return dimensions, data_type


def _assert_struct_array_cast(sql, expected_type_sql, expected_dimensions=1):
    cast = _parse_cast(sql)
    target = cast.args["to"]

    dimensions, element_type = _unwrap_array_type(target)
    assert dimensions == expected_dimensions
    assert element_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.STRUCT

    # Check the complete type through sqlglot's public SQL generation API. This
    # also verifies that struct field names and field types were not discarded.
    assert target.sql("duckdb") == expected_type_sql
    return cast


def test_duckdb_cast_to_array_of_struct_issue_example():
    cast = _assert_struct_array_cast(
        "select cast([struct_pack(a := 1)] as struct(a bigint)[])",
        "STRUCT(a BIGINT)[]",
    )

    # The array literal being cast must remain part of the expression; the fix
    # concerns parsing the target type, not replacing or dropping the input.
    assert isinstance(cast.this, exp.Array)
    assert len(cast.this.expressions) == 1


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("source_type", "expected_type", "dimensions"),

        ("struct(a bigint)[]", "STRUCT(a BIGINT)[]", 1),

            "STRUCT(a BIGINT, b BOOLEAN)[]",

)

        "STRUCT(a BIGINT[], b STRUCT(c BOOLEAN))[]",
    )

import pytest

import esper


class Position:
    def __init__(self, x=0, y=0):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y


class Velocity:
    def __init__(self, x=0, y=0):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y


@pytest.fixture
def world():
    return esper.World()


def test_create_entity_without_components_registers_every_entity(world):
    first = world.create_entity()
    second = world.create_entity()

    assert first == 1
    assert second == 2
    assert world.entity_exists(first)
    assert world.entity_exists(second)
    assert not world.entity_exists(second + 1)

    assert world.components_for_entity(first) == ()
    assert world.components_for_entity(second) == ()
    assert world.has_component(first, Position) is False
    assert world.get_component(Position) == []


def test_empty_entity_can_be_populated_later(world):
    entity = world.create_entity()
    position = Position(10, 20)
    velocity = Velocity(1, 2)

    world.add_component(entity, position)
    world.add_component(entity, velocity)

    assert world.entity_exists(entity)
    assert world.component_for_entity(entity, Position) is position
    assert world.component_for_entity(entity, Velocity) is velocity
    assert world.has_components(entity, Position, Velocity)
    assert len(world.components_for_entity(entity)) == 2
    assert world.get_component(Position) == [(entity, position)]


def test_create_entity_with_components_retains_existing_behavior(world):
    position = Position(3, 4)
    entity = world.create_entity(position)

    assert world.entity_exists(entity)
    assert world.has_component(entity, Position)
    assert world.component_for_entity(entity, Position) is position
    assert world.components_for_entity(entity) == (position,)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "component",
    [None, Position(9, 9)],
    ids=["none-component", "regular-component"],
)
def test_add_component_rejects_missing_entity_without_creating_it(world, component):
    made_up_entity = 123

    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.add_component(made_up_entity, component)

    assert not world.entity_exists(made_up_entity)
    assert world.get_component(type(component)) == []

    # A failed attempt to add a component must not consume an entity ID.
    assert world.create_entity() == 1


def test_add_component_does_not_recreate_or_revive_a_deleted_entity(world):
    entity = world.create_entity(Position())
    world.delete_entity(entity)

    assert not world.entity_exists(entity)
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.add_component(entity, Velocity())

    # Finalizing deferred deletion must not make the entity reusable either.
    world.process()
    assert not world.entity_exists(entity)
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.add_component(entity, Velocity())

def test_empty_entity_can_be_deleted(world, immediate):

    assert world.entity_exists(entity)

    world.delete_entity(entity, immediate=immediate)
    assert not world.entity_exists(entity)

    # For deferred deletion this finalizes removal; for immediate deletion it
    # verifies that a later process call does not cause any problems.
    world.process()
    assert not world.entity_exists(entity)
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.components_for_entity(entity)


def test_clear_database_removes_empty_entities_and_resets_ids(world):
    empty_entity = world.create_entity()
    populated_entity = world.create_entity(Position())

    world.clear_database()

    assert not world.entity_exists(empty_entity)
    assert not world.entity_exists(populated_entity)
    assert world.get_component(Position) == []

    new_entity = world.create_entity()
    assert new_entity == 1
    assert world.entity_exists(new_entity)
    assert world.components_for_entity(new_entity) == ()

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one, transpile


def _transpiled_date_diff(sql, read):
    generated = transpile(sql, read=read, write="duckdb")[0]
    assert "'None'" not in generated

    date_diff = parse_one(generated, read="duckdb").find(exp.DateDiff)
    assert date_diff is not None, generated
    return generated, date_diff


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [
        "SELECT DATEDIFF(end_date, start_date) FROM transactions",
        "SELECT DATEDIFF('2020-01-05', '2020-01-01') AS diff",
        "SELECT DATEDIFF(CURRENT_DATE(), hire_date) AS days_employed FROM employees",
    ],
)
def test_spark_datediff_defaults_to_day_in_duckdb(sql):
    _, date_diff = _transpiled_date_diff(sql, read="spark")

    # Spark's two-argument DATEDIFF always measures days. DuckDB requires the
    # unit as its first argument, so a missing AST unit must not become 'None'.
    assert date_diff.text("unit").lower() == "day"


def test_spark_datediff_preserves_argument_order():
    generated, date_diff = _transpiled_date_diff(
        "SELECT DATEDIFF(end_date, start_date) FROM transactions", read="spark"
    )

    # Spark is DATEDIFF(end, start), whereas DuckDB is
    # DATE_DIFF(unit, start, end). Spark operands may also be cast to DATE;
    # those casts do not affect the argument-order check.
    start = date_diff.expression
    end = date_diff.this
    if isinstance(start, exp.Cast):
        start = start.this
    if isinstance(end, exp.Cast):
        end = end.this

    assert start.sql(dialect="duckdb") == "start_date", generated
    assert end.sql(dialect="duckdb") == "end_date", generated


@pytest.mark.parametrize("unit", ["day", "month", "year"])
def test_explicit_duckdb_date_diff_units_are_preserved(unit):
    sql = f"SELECT DATE_DIFF('{unit}', start_date, end_date)"
    _, date_diff = _transpiled_date_diff(sql, read="duckdb")

    assert date_diff.text("unit") == unit
    assert date_diff.expression.sql(dialect="duckdb") == "start_date"
    assert date_diff.this.sql(dialect="duckdb") == "end_date"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("explicit_none", [False, True])
def test_duckdb_date_diff_defaults_for_missing_or_none_unit(explicit_none):
    args = {
        "this": exp.column("end_date"),
        "expression": exp.column("start_date"),
    }
    if explicit_none:
        args["unit"] = None

    generated = exp.DateDiff(**args).sql(dialect="duckdb")
    assert "'None'" not in generated

    date_diff = parse_one(generated, read="duckdb").find(exp.DateDiff)
    assert date_diff is not None
    assert date_diff.text("unit").lower() == "day"
    assert date_diff.expression.sql(dialect="duckdb") == "start_date"
    assert date_diff.this.sql(dialect="duckdb") == "end_date"

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one, transpile


def _assert_interval_type(tree):
    data_type = tree.find(exp.DataType)
    assert data_type is not None
    assert data_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL
    assert data_type.sql() == "INTERVAL"
    return data_type


def test_postgres_cast_string_to_interval():
    sql = "select cast('1 day' as interval)"
    tree = parse_one(sql, read="postgres")

    cast = tree.expressions[0]
    assert cast.this == exp.Literal.string("1 day")
    assert cast.args["to"] == _assert_interval_type(tree)

    expected = "SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)"
    assert tree.sql(dialect="postgres") == expected
    assert transpile(sql, read="postgres", write="postgres") == [expected]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("read", [None, "postgres"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql, expected",
    [
        (
            "SELECT CAST('2 hours' AS interval)",
            "SELECT CAST('2 hours' AS INTERVAL)",
        ),
        (
            "SELECT CAST('3 days' AS InTeRvAl)",
            "SELECT CAST('3 days' AS INTERVAL)",
        ),
        (
            "SELECT CAST(interval_text AS INTERVAL)",
            "SELECT CAST(interval_text AS INTERVAL)",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_cast_to_interval_is_case_insensitive_and_accepts_expressions(
    sql, expected, read
):
    tree = parse_one(sql, read=read)
    _assert_interval_type(tree)
    assert tree.sql(dialect=read) == expected


def test_try_cast_to_interval_uses_the_same_type_parser():
    tree = parse_one("SELECT TRY_CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)")

    assert isinstance(tree.expressions[0], exp.TryCast)
    _assert_interval_type(tree)
    assert tree.sql() == "SELECT TRY_CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)"


def test_interval_can_be_parsed_as_a_data_type():
    data_type = parse_one("interval", into=exp.DataType)

    assert isinstance(data_type, exp.DataType)
    assert data_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL
    assert data_type.sql() == "INTERVAL"


def test_interval_literal_syntax_is_not_changed():
    tree = parse_one("SELECT INTERVAL '1 day'", read="postgres")
    interval = tree.expressions[0]

    assert isinstance(interval, exp.Interval)
    assert interval.this == exp.Literal.string("1 day")
    assert tree.find(exp.DataType) is None

import operator

import numpy as np
import pytest
from numpy.testing import assert_array_equal

from unyt import unyt_array, unyt_quantity
from unyt.exceptions import UnitOperationError


def assert_dimensionless_result(result, expected):
    """Check values without discarding the units before validating them."""
    assert isinstance(result, unyt_array)
    assert result.units.is_dimensionless
    assert_array_equal(result.to_ndarray(), expected)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "power_operation", [operator.pow, np.power], ids=["operator", "ufunc"]
)
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "exponent_factory", [unyt_array, np.asarray], ids=["unyt_array", "ndarray"]
)
def test_dimensionless_array_exponent(power_operation, exponent_factory):
    # Reproduction from the issue: this must not evaluate the exponent array
    # as a boolean, and must agree with NumPy element by element. A plain
    # ndarray exponent is also dimensionless and must work equivalently.
    base = unyt_array([1, 2, 3, 4])
    exponent = exponent_factory([1, 2, 3, 4])

    result = power_operation(base, exponent)

    assert_dimensionless_result(result, [1, 4, 27, 256])


def test_array_exponent_with_zero_and_broadcasting():
    base = unyt_array([[2.0], [3.0]])
    exponent = unyt_array([0.0, 2.0])

    result = base**exponent

    assert_dimensionless_result(result, [[1.0, 4.0], [1.0, 9.0]])


def test_dimensionless_scalar_base_with_array_exponent():
    result = unyt_quantity(2.0) ** unyt_array([0, 1, 2, 3])

    assert_dimensionless_result(result, [1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0])


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "power_operation", [operator.pow, np.power], ids=["operator", "ufunc"]
)
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "exponent_factory", [unyt_array, np.asarray], ids=["unyt_array", "ndarray"]
)
def test_dimensionful_base_rejects_varying_array_exponent(
    power_operation, exponent_factory
):
    # Different elements would require different powers of cm, so the
    # operation must not silently discard the base units.
    base = unyt_array([1.0, 2.0], "cm")
    exponent = exponent_factory([1, 2])

    with pytest.raises(UnitOperationError):
        power_operation(base, exponent)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "power_operation", [operator.pow, np.power], ids=["operator", "ufunc"]
)
def test_dimensionful_array_exponent_is_rejected(power_operation):
    base = unyt_array([1.0, 2.0])
    exponent = unyt_array([1.0, 2.0], "cm")

    with pytest.raises(UnitOperationError):
        power_operation(base, exponent)


def test_scalar_power_unit_behavior_is_unchanged():
    base = unyt_array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0], "cm")

    squared = base**2
    assert squared.units == (base.units**2)
    assert_array_equal(squared.to_ndarray(), [1.0, 4.0, 9.0])

    zeroth_power = base**0
    assert_dimensionless_result(zeroth_power, [1.0, 1.0, 1.0])

import os

import casbin
import pytest
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

from casbin_sqlalchemy_adapter import Adapter, CasbinRule


MODEL_CONF = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "rbac_model.conf")


@pytest.fixture
def engine():
    engine = create_engine("sqlite://")
    yield engine
    engine.dispose()


def make_enforcer(engine):
    return casbin.Enforcer(MODEL_CONF, Adapter(engine))


def stored_rules(engine):
    """Read committed rules through a separate database session."""
    session = sessionmaker(bind=engine)()
    try:
        lines = session.query(CasbinRule).order_by(CasbinRule.id).all()
        return [
            (
                line.ptype,
                [
                    value
                    for value in (
                        line.v0,
                        line.v1,
                        line.v2,
                        line.v3,
                        line.v4,
                        line.v5,
                    )
                    if value is not None
                ],
            )
            for line in lines
        ]
    finally:
        session.close()


def canonical_rules(rules):
    return sorted((ptype, tuple(rule)) for ptype, rule in rules)


def test_add_policies_updates_enforcer_and_persists_every_rule(engine):
    enforcer = make_enforcer(engine)
    rules = [
        ["alice", "data1", "read"],
        ["bob", "data2", "write"],
        ["carol", "data3", "read"],
    ]

    assert enforcer.add_policies(rules) is True

    for subject, resource, action in rules:
        assert enforcer.enforce(subject, resource, action)

    assert canonical_rules(stored_rules(engine)) == canonical_rules(
        [("p", rule) for rule in rules]
    )

    # A new enforcer must see the batch after loading it from storage, rather
    # than merely seeing changes in the first enforcer's in-memory model.
    reloaded = make_enforcer(engine)
    assert sorted(reloaded.get_policy()) == sorted(rules)
    for subject, resource, action in rules:
        assert reloaded.enforce(subject, resource, action)


def test_remove_policies_removes_only_requested_rules_and_persists(engine):
    enforcer = make_enforcer(engine)
    rules = [
        ["alice", "data1", "read"],
        ["bob", "data2", "write"],
        ["carol", "data3", "read"],
    ]
    assert enforcer.add_policies(rules) is True

    assert enforcer.remove_policies([rules[0], rules[2]]) is True

    assert not enforcer.enforce("alice", "data1", "read")
    assert enforcer.enforce("bob", "data2", "write")
    assert not enforcer.enforce("carol", "data3", "read")
    assert enforcer.get_policy() == [rules[1]]
    assert stored_rules(engine) == [("p", rules[1])]

    reloaded = make_enforcer(engine)
    assert reloaded.get_policy() == [rules[1]]
    assert not reloaded.enforce("alice", "data1", "read")
    assert reloaded.enforce("bob", "data2", "write")
    assert not reloaded.enforce("carol", "data3", "read")

    # Removing an already absent rule is a no-op and reports failure.
    before = stored_rules(engine)
    assert enforcer.remove_policies([rules[0]]) is False
    assert stored_rules(engine) == before


def test_named_batch_operations_respect_the_policy_type(engine):
    enforcer = make_enforcer(engine)
    policy = ["eve", "data4", "read"]
    grouping_rules = [
        ["eve", "data4_admin"],
        ["frank", "data4_admin"],
    ]

    assert enforcer.add_policies([policy]) is True
    assert enforcer.add_named_grouping_policies("g", grouping_rules) is True
    assert canonical_rules(stored_rules(engine)) == canonical_rules(
        [("p", policy)] + [("g", rule) for rule in grouping_rules]
    )

    assert (
        enforcer.remove_named_grouping_policies("g", [grouping_rules[0]]) is True
    )
    assert enforcer.get_policy() == [policy]
    assert enforcer.get_grouping_policy() == [grouping_rules[1]]

    reloaded = make_enforcer(engine)
    assert reloaded.get_policy() == [policy]
    assert reloaded.get_grouping_policy() == [grouping_rules[1]]


def test_adapter_batch_edge_cases_and_ptype_isolation(engine):
    adapter = Adapter(engine)

    # Empty batches must be harmless.
    adapter.add_policies("p", "p", [])
    assert stored_rules(engine) == []

    shared_rule = ["alice", "data1", "read"]
    remaining_rule = ["bob", "data2", "write"]
    missing_rule = ["nobody", "missing", "read"]
    adapter.add_policies("p", "p", [shared_rule, remaining_rule])
    adapter.add_policies("p", "p2", [shared_rule])

    before = stored_rules(engine)
    assert adapter.remove_policies("p", "p", []) is False
    assert adapter.remove_policies("p", "p", [missing_rule]) is False
    assert stored_rules(engine) == before

    # A batch containing both absent and present rules still removes the
    # present rule. The identical rule under another ptype must be untouched.
    assert (
        adapter.remove_policies("p", "p", [missing_rule, shared_rule]) is True
    )
    assert canonical_rules(stored_rules(engine)) == canonical_rules(
        [("p", remaining_rule), ("p2", shared_rule)]
    )

import os

import pytest

from pre_commit.meta_hooks import check_useless_excludes
from pre_commit.util import cmd_output
from testing.fixtures import add_config_to_repo


def _add_config(in_git_dir, **hook_settings):
    hook = {'id': 'check-useless-excludes', **hook_settings}
    config = {'repos': [{'repo': 'meta', 'hooks': [hook]}]}
    add_config_to_repo(in_git_dir.strpath, config)


def _track_symlink(in_git_dir, link_name, target):
    link = in_git_dir.join(link_name)
    os.symlink(target, link.strpath)
    cmd_output('git', 'add', link_name)
    return link


def test_exclude_matching_broken_symlink_is_not_useless(capsys, in_git_dir):
    """A symlink hook can use an exclude for a tracked, broken symlink."""
    _add_config(
        in_git_dir,
        exclude='^broken-symlink$',
        types=['symlink'],
    )
    link = _track_symlink(
        in_git_dir,
        'broken-symlink',
        os.path.join('deinitialized-submodule', 'file.txt'),
    )
    assert os.path.islink(link.strpath)
    assert not os.path.exists(link.strpath)

    assert check_useless_excludes.main(()) == 0

    out, _ = capsys.readouterr()
    assert out == ''


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    'hook_settings',
    (
        {'types': ['python']},
        {'exclude_types': ['symlink']},
    ),
)
def test_type_filtered_symlink_still_has_useless_exclude(
        capsys, in_git_dir, hook_settings,
):
    """The broken-symlink fix must not bypass normal type filtering."""
    _add_config(
        in_git_dir,
        exclude='^intact-symlink$',
        **hook_settings,
    )
    in_git_dir.join('target.txt').write('target\n')
    link = _track_symlink(in_git_dir, 'intact-symlink', 'target.txt')
    assert os.path.exists(link.strpath)

    assert check_useless_excludes.main(()) == 1

    out, _ = capsys.readouterr()
    expected = (
        "The exclude pattern '^intact-symlink$' for check-useless-excludes "
        'does not match any files'
    )
    assert out.strip() == expected


def test_unrelated_exclude_is_still_useless_with_broken_symlink(
        capsys, in_git_dir,
):
    _add_config(
        in_git_dir,
        exclude='^some-other-path$',
        types=['symlink'],
    )
    _track_symlink(in_git_dir, 'broken-symlink', 'missing-target')

    assert check_useless_excludes.main(()) == 1

    out, _ = capsys.readouterr()
    expected = (
        "The exclude pattern '^some-other-path$' for check-useless-excludes "
        'does not match any files'
    )
    assert out.strip() == expected


def test_broken_symlink_outside_files_pattern_does_not_validate_exclude(
        capsys, in_git_dir,
):
    _add_config(
        in_git_dir,
        files='^included/',
        exclude='^broken-symlink$',
        types=['symlink'],
    )
    _track_symlink(in_git_dir, 'broken-symlink', 'missing-target')

    assert check_useless_excludes.main(()) == 1

    out, _ = capsys.readouterr()
    expected = (
        "The exclude pattern '^broken-symlink$' for check-useless-excludes "
        'does not match any files'
    )
    assert out.strip() == expected
